content:
发言人办公室关于七国集团外长巴黎会议的联合声明 媒体报道 2026年11月13日，加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国、美国等七国集团外长和欧盟高级代表发表以下声明。文本开头：2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日在巴黎举行的七国集团外长会议后的联合声明 我们，代表加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、英国和美利坚合众国的七国集团外长，以及欧盟高级代表，于 2026 年 11 月 9 日至 10 日在法国担任 2026 年七国集团主席国期间在巴黎举行会议。 乌克兰 我们重申对乌克兰及其勇敢人民的坚定支持他们捍卫自己的领土完整、主权、自由和独立。我们完全声援乌克兰人民，他们每天都遭受俄罗斯袭击，影响住宅楼、民用基础设施和文化遗产，以及针对乌克兰和其他伙伴的恶意混合活动。我们谴责黑海地区针对民用航运的袭击行动，这对全球粮食安全产生了重大影响，并加强了我们对保障粮食供应链的承诺。我们重申支持美国领导的通过直接和认真的谈判促进和平的持续努力。
我们重申了确保全面、全面和互惠停火的重要性。相互停止对所有能源基础设施和黑海的攻击，以保护平民，减少对能源（包括供暖、水和卫生设施以及粮食供应）的干扰，并支持全球市场的更大稳定，这是实现公正和持久和平的重要第一步。我们重申，有关欧洲未来安全的谈判必须包括欧洲人。正如我们在埃维昂七国集团峰会上所承诺的那样，我们评估了向乌克兰提供防空能力、系统和拦截器、远程能力和许可证方面取得的进展，这些能力将使其能够增加军事生产并行使其固有的自卫权。我们仍然致力于继续并加强朝这个方向的努力。我们承认需要以协调一致的方式解决乌克兰 2027 年及以后紧迫的融资需求，以支持乌克兰。我们谴责朝鲜和伊朗向俄罗斯提供军事援助，以及中国提供武器、军事训练和军民两用部件，这使得战争得以继续。我们明确表示打算继续对这些国家采取行动。基于我们领导人在埃维昂达成的共识，我们讨论了对俄罗斯战时经济日益增加的压力，包括通过制裁。
我们重申两国领导人承诺在针对俄罗斯的制裁问题上密切协调。我们重申决心重点关注悬挂假旗的船只或无国籍船只，以及保险公司、石油贸易商和中介机构等结构性推动者，以进一步扰乱和威慑用于规避制裁的影子舰队。我们重申支持乌克兰能源安全和恢复力，决定加大资金和物资支持力度，帮助乌克兰度过冬季。我们欢迎为使切尔诺贝利新安全隔离设施的修复保持在国际议程上的高度重视而做出的努力

【原文 English Original】
Office of the Spokesman Joint Statement on the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris Media Note November 13, 2026 The following statement was released by the G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and the High Representative of the European Union. Begin Text: Joint declaration following the G7 Foreign Ministers Meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November 2026 We, the G7 Foreign Ministers representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America, along with the High Representative of the European Union, met under the 2026 French G7 Presidency in Paris, on 9 and 10 November 2026. Ukraine We reaffirmed our unwavering support to Ukraine and its courageous people as they defend their territorial integrity, sovereignty, freedom, and independence. We stand in full solidarity with the Ukrainian population suffering from daily Russian attacks affecting residential buildings, civilian infrastructure, and cultural heritage, as well as malicious hybrid activities against Ukraine and other partners. We condemned the campaign of strikes carried out against civilian shipping in the Black Sea area, which have significant consequences on global food security, and strengthened our commitment to safeguarding food supply chains. We reiterated our support to ongoing U.S.-led efforts to facilitate peace through direct and serious negotiations. We reaffirmed the importance of securing a full, comprehensive, and reciprocal ceasefire. A reciprocal halt to attacks on all energy infrastructure and in the Black Sea to protect civilians, reduce disruption to energy, including heating, water and sanitation, and food supply and support greater stability in global markets is an important first step towards just and lasting peace. We reiterated that negotiations on the future security of Europe must include the Europeans. As we pledged during the G7 Summit in Évian, we took stock of progress on supplying Ukraine with air defense capabilities, systems and interceptors, long-range capabilities and licenses that will allow it to increase its military production and to exercise its inherent right of self-defense. We remain committed to continuing and strengthening our efforts in this direction. We acknowledged the need to address Ukraine’s pressing financing needs for 2027 and beyond in a coordinated way to support Ukraine. We condemned the provision of military assistance to Russia by North Korea and Iran, and the provision of weapons, military training and dual-use components by China, which enables the continuation of the war. We made clear our intention to continue to take action against these countries. Building on the consensus among our leaders in Évian, we discussed increasing pressure on Russia’s war economy, including through sanctions. We reaffirmed the commitment of our leaders to closely coordinate on sanctions against Russia. We reiterated our determination to focus on ships flying false flags or stateless ships, as well as structural enablers, such as insurers, oil traders, and intermediaries, to further disrupt and deter shadow fleet vessels used to circumvent sanctions. We reaffirmed our support to Ukraine’s energy security and resilience, and decided to step up our financial and material support to help the country get through the winter. We welcomed efforts to keep the repair of the Chornobyl New Safe Confinement high on the international agenda, as demonstrated by the donors’ conference organized in Paris on 9 November by France, EBRD, and Ukraine. We also welcomed the ongoing projects coordinated through the Tallinn Mechanism under Italy’s Chairpersonship to support Ukraine’s civilian cyber resilience. Middle East On Iran, we commended the work of the regional mediators and reiterated our support for all diplomatic efforts aimed at reaching a lasting settlement that addresses international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and contributes to regional security. We reiterated that Iran must never be allowed to develop or acquire a nuclear weapon. We urged Iran to stop its support for nonstate armed groups in the region. Absent a diplomatic solution, we committed to continuing our coordination to economically and politically constrain the Iranian regime’s ability to sow instability in the region and around the world. We strongly condemned Iran’s attacks against its neighbors and the disruption of international trade, energy security, and the global economy caused by the obstruction of transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed the importance of protecting civilians and civilian objects, and called on Iran to respect its international human rights and humanitarian law obligations. We called on Iran to cease its persistent attacks against civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. We reaffirmed our commitment to the right of safe and free passage and our opposition to any tolls, fees, illegal costs, discriminations or any limitation imposed on maritime transit through the Strait. We underscored the importance of the defensive activities undertaken by U.S. Central Command in the Strait of Hormuz to demine the waterway and escort civilian vessels. We recognized that the multinational, independent, and defensive initiative led by France and the UK can play an important role in facilitating the resumption of maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz also by supporting the verification of the removal of all mines. We reaffirmed our commitment to fully implement the obligations under all relevant UN Security Council resolutions sanctions and related restrictive measures reinstated in September 2025 through the snapback mechanism under UN Security Council resolution 2231, and called on all UN Member States to do the same. We urged Iran to return to compliance with its international obligations, and in particular to resume full cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in order to restore transparency regarding the nature of its nuclear program. We also expressed grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots against many of our citizens and territories. We recognized the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty. On Yemen, we condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable continued strikes carried out by the Houthis in Yemen and against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including those on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We called on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions and threats and refrain from any further escalation to enable a return to an inclusive political process. We expressed our solidarity with the Government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and reaffirmed their right to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law. We urged all actors, including Iran, to end their arming of and support for the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions. We expressed deep concern at the worsening humanitarian impact of the conflict and called for the protection of civilians and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access with the urgent opening of a humanitarian corridor in Taiz. We reiterated our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all humanitarian personnel, including the 70 UN staff who remain unjustly detained by the Houthis. We reaffirmed the importance of maritime safety and security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. We shared the importance of continuing support to the Government of Yemen, including through capacity-building. We recognized the positive contribution of the EU maritime defensive operations EUNAVFOR ASPIDES and EUNAVFOR ATALANTA to restore maritime security and protect maritime shipping and the lives of seafarers in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. On Lebanon, we stressed the need for all parties to fully respect the ceasefire and expressed support for implementation of the Trilateral Framework and of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. We reiterated that the disarmament of all non-state armed groups, foremost among them Hezbollah, remains essential to ensuring that all weapons are brought under the authority and control of the Lebanese state. We called on Lebanon and Israel to make progress implementing the pilot zones to allow for full and verifiable Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli redeployment as the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) deploy. We reiterated our support for the Lebanese authorities’ efforts to achieve the disarmament of all non-state armed groups and for Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity. As the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) is set to expire at the end of the year, we underscored the need for a robust, credible, and long-lasting security architecture in Lebanon in support of the LAF, in line with UN Security Council resolution 1701 and enabling further implementation of the Trilateral Framework. In calling for a strengthened LAF, we welcomed the establishment of the EU CSDP mission EU Support Mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon). We called upon Lebanese actors to move forward in the adoption and implementation of financial reforms in view of agreeing on an IMF program. On Gaza, we remained committed to the swift implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and to accelerate humanitarian, recovery and reconstruction efforts aimed at fostering long-term stability. We unequivocally condemned the attacks committed by Hamas on the 7th of October, reiterating that Hamas can have no role in Gaza’s future and must decommission its weaponry. Israel must progressively withdraw from the Gaza Strip, under the conditions outlined in UN Security Council Resolution 2803. We stressed the urgent need for the safe, rapid, sustained, and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza and the opening of additional crossings, as well as the rehabilitation of humanitarian infrastructure and the protection of civilians. It is vital that all parties continue to engage constructively on the next steps outlined in the Comprehensive Plan, in pursuit of a political horizon for peaceful and prosperous coexistence, for the Israeli and Palestinian people, that advances Middle East peace and stability. We called for ending terrorist attacks and other actions which increase tensions and the risk of escalation in the West Bank. On Syria, we reaffirmed our strong support for a peaceful and inclusive political transition towards a united, sovereign and stable Syria, ensuring respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all Syrians. We stressed the importance of fully implementing the arrangements reached on the peaceful integration of Northeast Syria and reiterated our commitment to fighting terrorism. We expressed concern over the situation in Southern Syria, calling for the protection of civilians and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also reaffirmed the importance of supporting Syria’s economic recovery and reconstruction to achieve lasting stability and to enhance regional connectivity. Indo-Pacific We emphasised the importance of a free and open Indo-Pacific region which is prosperous and secure, and that protects shared principles including sovereignty, territorial integrity, the rule of law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We reiterated our commitment to upholding freedom of navigation and overflight in the region and called on States to abide by their obligations under international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). We expressed our serious concerns over the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea. We reaffirmed our strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion or any actions that raise tensions and risk escalation. We reiterated that the award rendered by the Arbitral Tribunal on 12 July 2016 is a significant milestone, which is final and legally binding upon the parties to the proceedings. We stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. In the context of China’s increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan, which threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping, we reaffirmed our opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo, particularly by force or coercion, or the threat thereof. We encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-Strait issues through constructive dialogue. We also expressed our support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations. We strongly condemned North Korea’s unlawful nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs and reaffirmed our commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea, in accordance with all relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. We underlined that increased cooperation between Russia and North Korea has serious consequences for European and Indo-Pacific security. We urged North Korea to immediately cease all assistance and to withdraw its troops. We reaffirmed our concern regarding cryptocurrency thefts and cybercrimes committed by North Korea and expressed the need to respond to its unlawful overseas labor program. We urged North Korea to immediately resolve the issue of abductions. We remain deeply concerned by the deterioration of the human rights and humanitarian situation across Myanmar. We reiterated the need for the immediate de-escalation of violence, the unimpeded passage of humanitarian assistance, and a genuine and inclusive democratic process that reflects the will of the people of Myanmar. Sudan We were alarmed by the devastating consequences of the war on the Sudanese people and the growing risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Kordofan. Continued fighting, restrictions on humanitarian access and attacks, including by drones, affecting healthcare facilities, displacement camps and the infrastructure civilians rely on for food are putting lives at risk, which is being compounded by the impact of El Niño. A year after the atrocities in El Fasher, we unequivocally condemned all violations and abuses against civilians, including conflict-related sexual violence against women and girls. We called on all external actors to cease supplying or facilitating armed, logistical, and financial support to the belligerents and to use their influence to encourage the warring parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, lift restrictions on humanitarian access and support de-escalation, and avoid any action that could contribute to the conflict. We underscored that, beyond an immediate cease-fire, a peaceful and durable resolution of the conflict is essential to securing unity and long-term stability in Sudan. In line with the principles stated at the Sudan Ministerial Conference in Berlin in April this year, we reaffirmed that a credible Sudanese civilian-led, inclusive, and transparent political dialogue process that addresses historical grievances and respects Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is critical to securing a lasting peace. We demanded the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces comply with international humanitarian law, engage in negotiations including with the Quad with a view to reaching a permanent ceasefire, and guarantee rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. We reiterated our full support to the work of the Quintet aiming to facilitate such a dialogue, in a process that should run in parallel to and in close alignment with efforts to secure a ceasefire. We call on the wider international community to support these efforts. Horn of Africa We noted with great concern the worsening security situation in the Horn of Africa, specifically between Ethiopia and Eritrea, which bears the risk of regional escalation amid rising cross-border tensions. We underlined the serious consequences further escalation could have for regional stability, already dire humanitarian crises, security and international trade, including in the Red Sea. We called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, pursue diplomatic solutions, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of civilians, especially women and children. We reaffirmed the importance of respecting the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries in the region. In particular, we supported efforts by the United Nations and the African Union to reduce tensions and to facilitate dialogue between the parties. Haiti We supported and welcomed the renewal of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) mandate through March 2027, which aims to assist Haitian forces in restoring security and stability in Haiti. We also welcomed the renewal of the UN sanctions regime, which promotes accountability for individuals and entities who threaten peace, security, and stability in Haiti. We called for international support to strengthen the Haitian National Police and Haitian Armed Forces, uphold the rule of law, and combat impunity. We also called on all security actors operating in Haiti to prioritize the protection of Haitian civilians in all security operations. We stressed the importance of organizing democratic elections in Haiti and noted the postponement of the first round of elections to July 2027. Noting progress made by the government and the Provisional Electoral Council in their work to advance Haiti’s path to elected governance, we underlined the need to safeguard the credibility and integrity of the electoral process and underscored the responsibility of Haitian authorities to ensure their full and impartial implementation of the electoral decree. We called for concrete results that strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and contribute to a credible return to democratic governance. We noted with concerns regarding the participation of sanctioned individuals in the political process, which undermines accountability and public trust. The people of Haiti have a right to determine their future through credible democratic processes and leaders who serve the public interest with integrity. We remain deeply concerned by the ongoing humanitarian crisis, widespread violence, and reports of human rights violations in Haiti. We urged the international community to intensify financial contributions to the UN Trust Fund, recognizing that the success of the UN-mandated hybrid mission depends on sustained multilateral support to resource its operations. We urged critical international support for humanitarian assistance for Haiti, in order to address the multiple crises facing the people of Haiti. We also underscored the importance of laying the groundwork for Haiti’s economic recovery with the support of international financial institutions and other multilateral partners. We welcomed the World Bank’s Compact with the Haitian authorities as a common framework to assess Haitian-led reform efforts and strengthen accountability for results. We committed to working with diverse Haitian and international partners to promote greater coordination and complementarity of efforts. Cuba We expressed our concerns about the profound economic crisis and humanitarian needs facing the Cuban people, including shortages of food, fuel and medicines. We stressed the importance of improving humanitarian aid delivery mechanisms into and throughout Cuba in order to improve the welfare of the Cuban people. We called on the Cuban authorities to pursue and implement significant and meaningful political and economic reforms to advance prosperity, respect for human rights, and the legitimate aspirations of the Cuban people, and to take concrete steps towards multi-party democratic governance, press freedom, and freedom of expression and association. We also called on the Cuban authorities to release all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. We encouraged constructive and inclusive dialogue in order to find a way out of the crisis. Venezuela We acknowledged the will of the people of Venezuela to turn the page on the country’s prolonged political and economic crisis. In this regard, we reaffirmed our full support for the ongoing reconciliation talks that bring together the interim government and the delegation representing the National Assembly elected in 2015 and which have already yielded measurable progress. We called on all parties to continue to engage in good faith on the path leading from the restoration of institutions and the rule of law to the holding of free and fair elections. We emphasised the particular importance of providing guarantees to all parties and civil society organizations to enable their participation in the democratic process. We called for the release of all political prisoners. We acknowledged that Venezuela’s economic recovery is inextricably linked to the political reconciliation process and encouraged investments and commercial deals that help build a more stable and prosperous future for the Venezuelan people. We also offered emergency humanitarian response and civil protection activities following the devastating twin earthquakes on June 24, 2026. UN reform and efficiency of humanitarian assistance Committed to making the UN more efficient and effective, accountable and impactful, we welcomed ongoing efforts under the UN80, as well as humanitarian reform initiatives, including the Humanitarian Reset. These latter initiatives aim to strengthen the humanitarian system through better coordination, mandate delineation, and consolidation of common services and critical enablers, while remaining fully open to all impartial humanitarian actors and in full compliance with international law and the UN Charter. We reiterated the importance of maintaining sustained momentum in driving forward reform at this critical juncture for the UN. We commended the work of the G7 working group on the efficiency of the humanitarian supply chain (LOG+7), which is one of the most strategic drivers to increase the impact of assistance in a context of a significant decrease in financing and worsening of crises. These efforts towards a more integrated supply chain, including the reinforcement of the existing humanitarian hubs and pooling of resources, will help reach a greater proportion of the population in need without budgetary changes, and thereby contributing to address growing humanitarian needs including food insecurity and malnutrition in all its forms. This work will continue within the framework of the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain led by the European Union and through the UN80 integrated supply chain initiative. Food security and nutrition We stressed our commitment to food security and nutrition to address the consequences of conflicts and instability, and to strengthen food systems resilience. We called for continuing action to address the disruptions to food trade in the Black Sea in the context of the war in Ukraine, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the El Niño phenomenon. Together, in 2026, we mobilized 2.5 billion USD of international funding to address the crisis in the Middle East, adding to our long-term commitment to more resilient food systems and fertilizer markets. Forced displacement of people We noted the serious impact of conflict, violence, and instability on affected countries and regions, as well as on broader regional and international security affecting the security of civilian populations. This constitutes a driver of forced displacement and irregular migration, and exposes victims of human trafficking to acute forms of abuse and exploitation. Malicious hybrid activities We condemned persistent malicious hybrid activities by states and non-state actors aimed at undermining the security and stability of the G7 Members and partner countries, through coordinated and deliberate campaigns, including acts of sabotage against critical infrastructure, malicious cyber activities, foreign information manipulation and interference, and the instrumentalization of migration. Such actions risk unintended effects, escalation, and miscalculation. We reaffirmed our determination to act resolutely and in a coordinated manner to address hybrid campaigns, using all available tools to prevent, deter, and respond to these actions, irrespective of their origin, scale and intensity. We stressed the need to reinforce our common efforts and accelerate work on all relevant work strands, in order to strengthen resilience, enhance preparedness, and protect critical infrastructure. Transnational Organized Crime We expressed concern about the increasingly sophisticated methods, violence, and reach of transnational organized criminal groups worldwide, in particular those involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, and migrant smuggling, and underscored the importance of international cooperation to strengthen maritime security, combat illicit trafficking networks, and dismantle these groups. We also recognized that online scams are a form of rapidly growing transnational organized crime that poses a threat to regional and international peace and security, and stressed the need to strengthen collaboration, including with the private sector, as appropriate, and to disrupt online scam networks, which may be linked to other forms of transnational organized crime. Maritime and port security We reaffirmed the absolute necessity of ensuring maritime safety and security, and of safeguarding freedom of navigation worldwide, in accordance with international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), in order to prevent any lasting disruption to global supply chains, particularly with regard to energy, fertilizers and food products, because this can seriously affect vulnerable economies and populations. We recalled the global pledge initiated by the EU of 12 October 2026 on maintaining the integrity of the international law of the sea “No Fees, No Tolls”. We also underlined the need to strengthen the resilience and protection of critical undersea infrastructure, particularly submarine energy infrastructure and telecommunications cables, and their landing stations, including through enhanced international cooperation, information-sharing, redundancy and rapid repair capabilities. We encouraged practical cooperation with industry to improve access to repair vessels, equipment and spare parts, and to facilitate timely authorizations and port access for repairs, consistent with applicable international law and national requirements. In order to strengthen operational cooperation across our key maritime ports or relevant authorities, we, together with Brazil and the Republic of Korea, launched the G7+ Ports Network to Combat Drug Trafficking. This network will help strengthen operational cooperation, the exchange of information and the sharing of best practices to protect our ports from drug trafficking, in coordination and coherence with existing initiatives such as the European Ports Alliance, the European Coalition Against Drugs and the Maritime Safety Committee, and with the support of international organizations, in particular the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. We welcomed the work of the members of the G7++ “Friends of the Gulf of Guinea” group to create opportunities for deeper engagement with the Yaoundé Architecture for strengthening partnerships in the fields of training, capacity-building and joint operations, as well as our judicial cooperation to facilitate the prosecution of traffickers apprehended at sea. We welcomed the work carried out by the members of the G7 and Nordic Baltic 8++ Shadow Fleet Task Force and reiterated our commitment to enhance G7 coordination with partners to further disrupt and deter the global shadow fleet engaged in illegal, unsafe or environmentally perilous activities. Resilience of critical satellite infrastructure We also recognized the need to strengthen the resilience of critical satellite infrastructure, including satellites, ground stations and control centres, and their supporting terrestrial connections and power supplies. We encouraged stronger protection against physical and cyber threats and harmful interference, as well as redundancy and contingency arrangements to maintain essential services. Taking into account the interdependence of undersea, satellite and terrestrial networks, we encouraged cooperation among competent authorities and operators on risk assessment, timely and secure incident information-sharing, and preparedness exercises. Such cooperation should support rapid service restoration, including through complementary connectivity options for essential communications, while safeguarding sensitive information. Frontier models We recognized the opportunities offered by frontier models to advance science and strengthen our economies, while also noting the need to ensure the secure and trustworthy development of these advanced systems and models through adequate safeguards and human-centric adoption, taking into account that they can pose risks, including for society and economic security. We acknowledged that frontier models can be misused by state and non-state malicious actors, including for malicious cyber activities and criminal activities, or to acquire and enhance chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or explosive capabilities. We recognized the importance of strengthening the security and resilience of frontier models to advance innovation, economic prosperity, and national security. The developments and issues are complex. That is why it is key that governments, international organizations businesses and academia engage in discussions on model adoption. We will pursue our discussion to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted frontier model deployment including through efforts started with the Hiroshima AI Process. Economic security and critical minerals We reaffirmed our shared concerns regarding the use of non-market policies and practices and economic coercion, especially on critical minerals and their related dual-use items. We will work towards strengthening our competitiveness and addressing the root causes of our common challenges. We affirmed the importance of the G7 Coordination Platform on Economic Coercion to build a common response to economic coercion and further promote cooperation with partners beyond the G7. We further recognized the importance of maintaining and strengthening of our midstream and downstream industries’ competitiveness, including in relation to critical minerals, by protecting critical technologies and commit to working within the G7 and with partners to coordinate on policy measures for technology control. Recognizing the strategic role of critical minerals value chains for the economic prosperity and security of our countries, and in light of the high market concentration in certain economies in the critical minerals sector, we reiterated the urgency of reducing strategic dependencies and vulnerabilities by diversifying and securing trusted supply chains to build up our collective resilience. In that regard, we recognized the importance of the measures announced at the Evian Summit to ensure critical minerals supply chains resilience and security. We commended the expansion of the G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance which builds on the G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance launched under Canada’s G7 Presidency in 2025. This expanded Alliance and other platforms provide a venue for cooperation within the G7 and with partner countries in order to facilitate discussion, support data-driven decision-making and foster coordination among members to strengthen diversification and resilience of critical minerals value chains. End Text.

title: Spies and silicon chips: Alice Huang’s tangled corporate web
zh_title: 间谍和硅芯片：Alice Huang 错综复杂的企业网络
summary: 总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节模糊不清，几乎令人印象深刻
content:
总部位于新加坡的科技集团 Megaspeed 经营着价值数十亿美元的世界上最先进的人工智能芯片，但法新社访问时，其办公室已是空壳，其员工似乎早在间谍指控传到他们家门口之前就消失了。数据中心公司 MegaSpeed International 的新加坡办事处。照片：Taryn/法新社 Megaspeed 前董事 Alice Huang 本周被指控为中国间谍，被指控在为北京挖掘公司机密时与 Nvidia 联合创始人 Jensen Huang 有染。关于爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的生活细节很模糊，几乎不可能确定她住在哪里、在哪里工作、或者出生时间。但她的影响力无疑是广泛传播的，从不起眼的新加坡办公室，到东南亚庞大的数据中心，再到硅谷闪闪发光的董事会会议室。她与云计算公司 Megaspeed 的关系是丑闻的核心。 Megaspeed 标榜自己是一家处于人工智能革命核心的公司，使用 Nvidia 的先进硅芯片为大型数据中心内的高性能计算提供动力。但它也因一个更隐秘的目的而受到调查。据称，Megaspeed 打着为其东南亚数据中心购买计算机硬件的幌子，通过向中国运送 Nvidia 芯片来帮助北京规避贸易限制。北京方面否认了间谍活动的指控，Megaspeed 表示正在调查其是否遵守了敏感芯片的出口管制。
在位于新加坡商业区中心的 Megaspeed 办公室，锁着的玻璃门后面看不到任何工作人员。邻居告诉法新社，过去几个月他们没有看到任何人进出。同样，在距离新加坡仅一桥之隔的马来西亚柔佛州新开发社区的一家购物中心里，子公司 Speedmatrix 的办公室里也没有员工。 2025 年 5 月 22 日，数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的中国高管 Alice Huang（右）出席 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左）在台北一家餐厅举办的晚宴。照片：法新社照片 / CTI via AFPTV。新加坡警方于 2025 年 2 月对 Megaspeed 和其他几家涉嫌规避或违反出口管制的公司展开调查。作为新加坡调查的一部分，爱丽丝·黄接受了采访。新加坡内政部表示，尽管没有受到任何指控，但她于 2026 年 2 月被禁止进入新加坡，原因是提供不准确信息以“淡化她在 Megaspeed 中的作用”。爆炸性增长 公司记录显示黄直接参与了 Megaspeed 的诞生。记录显示，与她有联系的一家公司于 2023 年初收购了中国视频游戏开发商第七大道国际的新加坡子公司。几乎立刻，7Road 的名称就被抛弃并改为 Megaspeed International。黄在 2023 年 3 月至 2023 年 11 月期间担任 Megaspeed 董事不到一年。
她的到来恰逢命运的巨大变化，Megaspeed 从一家名不见经传的视频游戏制造商转变为亚洲最大的 Nvidia 芯片买家之一。根据 2024 年提交的公司账目，在 12 个月内，Megaspeed 的收入从 0 美元跃升至近 3 亿美元。Megaspeed 自称为“云托管服务提供商”，其资产价值从 3200 万美元飙升至近 30 亿美元。期间。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。只是哦

【原文 English Original】
Singapore-based tech group Megaspeed dealt in billions of dollars’ worth of the world’s most advanced AI chips, but its office was an empty shell when AFP visited, its staff seemingly vanished long before claims of espionage landed at their door. The Singapore office of the data centre company MegaSpeed International. Photo: Taryn/AFP Megaspeed’s former director Alice Huang was this week outed as an alleged Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. Details about Alice Huang’s life are vague, making it almost impossible to pin down where she lives, where she works, or when she was born. But her influence undoubtedly spreads far and wide, from the nondescript Singapore office, to hulking data centres in Southeast Asia, to the gleaming boardrooms of Silicon Valley. Her connection to cloud computing firm Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal. Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the AI revolution, using Nvidia’s advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres. But it is also under investigation for serving a murkier purpose. Under the guise of buying computer hardware for its Southeast Asia data hubs, Megaspeed has allegedly helped Beijing skirt trade restrictions by sending Nvidia chips into China. Beijing has denied allegations of spying, and Megaspeed said it was investigating if it had complied with export controls on the sensitive chips. At Megaspeed’s office in the heart of the Singapore business district, no staff could be seen behind its locked glass doors. Neighbours told AFP they had not seen anyone come or go for the past few months. Likewise in a mall at a newly developed neighbourhood in Johor, the Malaysian region a bridge away from Singapore, no employees were around in subsidiary Speedmatrix’s office. Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP photo/ CTI via AFPTV. Singapore police opened an investigation in February 2025 into Megaspeed and several other companies suspected of circumventing or violating export controls. Alice Huang was interviewed as part of Singapore’s probe. Although no charges were laid, she was barred from the city-state in February 2026 for providing inaccurate information to “downplay her role in Megaspeed”, Singapore’s home ministry said. Explosive growth Corporate records show Huang’s direct involvement in the birth of Megaspeed. A company linked to her acquired the Singapore arm of Chinese video game developer 7Road International in early 2023, the records showed. Almost immediately, the 7Road name was ditched and changed to Megaspeed International. Huang was listed as a Megaspeed director for less than a year, taking the role between March and November 2023. Her arrival coincided with a drastic change in fortunes, as Megaspeed pivoted from a little-known video game maker to one of Asia’s biggest buyers of Nvidia chips. Within 12 months, Megaspeed’s revenue jumped from $0 to almost US$300 million, according to company accounts filed in 2024. Megaspeed — which described itself as a “cloud hosting services provider” — saw the value of its assets skyrocket from $32 million to almost $3 billion over the same period. Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. Just one of Nvidia’s advanced AI computer chips can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Over two years, Megaspeed reportedly traded in upwards of $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. A financial trail weaving through Singapore, Malaysia and the Cayman Islands suggests Megaspeed’s business may have been boosted by a connection to Chinese tech giant Alibaba. Megaspeed has a Malaysian subsidiary that struck a deal in 2024 pledging assets to Apex Enterprise Solutions in Singapore as security in case of contractual breaches. Apex is linked through a parent company to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, a firm registered in the Cayman Islands, Singapore corporate data shows. By that time, Huang was no longer registered as a director at Megaspeed. But Singapore authorities said she remained one of Megaspeed’s “key controllers”. Megaspeed’s ultimate holding company is a Singapore firm called Swiftdata. Singapore businessman Tan Yong Pong — who has previously run printing and graphic design companies — is a director of both Megaspeed and Swiftdata. No one answered when AFP visited Tan’s registered address in eastern Singapore, although dogs could be heard barking behind the door. “They are friendly. I occasionally bump into the lady at the lift landing when she’s walking her dog,” an elderly neighbour told AFP. “But we have not seen them for months.” Awkward questions In June 2025, US investigators turned up at Megaspeed to carry out a “post-shipment verification”, with Huang present, according to Singapore’s home ministry, adding that it was the first time it found out about Washington’s probe. The American flag is raised on the newly-installed flagpole on the South Lawn of the White House on June 18, 2025. Photo: White House, via Flickr. That same day, Huang was interviewed by Singapore police who impounded her passport. By then, she and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang had already been spotted together in public. In one of their early outings together, they were seen mingling at an afterparty following the Computex trade show in Taiwan at the beginning of 2024. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about their relationship well before it exploded into a public scandal, but said Sunday he did not regret not acting on it. “No, I don’t think so. I think — you know, he’s an honorable guy,” Trump said. But the scandal has sparked national security fears. China and the United States are fighting for supremacy in artificial intelligence, and Nvidia’s market-leading products have become a major point of contention. Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models, and the US imposed rules in 2022 to restrict their sales to China. In the past years, Jensen Huang has emerged as the leading tech boss urging  Trump to lift those curbs. In any case, the restrictions appear to have been widely circumvented. Singapore. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. A Chinese university tied to the nation’s defence establishment was able to buy advanced Nvidia chips, according to procurement notices from October and September. Singapore’s probe into Megaspeed is ongoing. Separately, Malaysia said Friday it is investigating the company’s subsidiary Speedmatrix to determine if chips imported into the country had been exported to other jurisdictions. Megaspeed itself said it has retained a US lawfirm to examine its compliance. “Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously,” it said. Tangled webs Alice Huang sits in the middle of a corporate web, connected to myriad shell companies, investment houses and major Chinese technology firms. Corporate records filed in Hong Kong list her as a director of Nanjing Lingxing Technology, which operates the popular T3 ride hailing platform in China. Other notable investors in Nanjing Lingxing Technology include Alibaba and Tencent, as well as state-backed carmakers like China FAW and Dongfeng Motor Group. A corporate CV published by a Chinese investment firm details Huang’s rapid ascent through the ranks of Asian investment banking. She served in a senior role at HSBC sometime around 2012, the resume claims, before moving on to stints at CITIC Securities and Shanghai Hexi Investment. The HSBC headquarters in Central, Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Singapore business filings described her as a Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport. She was born in China’s landlocked Hunan province, which she left to study media in Hong Kong, HK01 media reported. A CCTV reporter wrote on Weibo that she worked with Huang at the Chinese broadcaster, but later deleted the post.

content:
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 证实，它遭受了安全漏洞，黑客在窃取人工智能基础设施提供商 Fireworks AI 的凭证后，通过其市场分发恶意 Claude Code 扩展。
该漏洞还让攻击者可以访问内部系统并窃取客户数据，包括历史人工智能编码代理跟踪，其中包含未经编辑的凭据，这些凭据后来被用来破坏其他服务。
该漏洞在周五发布的一份新事件报告中披露，该报告解释了攻击者如何于 10 月 29 日通过 Cursor 市场分发 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意版本。
此次攻击使多达 5,000 名开发人员面临安装持久 SSH 后门的恶意软件的攻击。
Cursor 是一款基于 Microsoft 开源 Visual Studio Code (VS Code) 的 AI 代码编辑器，允许开发人员使用 AI 助手编写、修改和调试软件。
据 Cursor 称，攻击是在黑客获得存储在 Fireworks AI 上的访问密钥时开始的，Fireworks AI 是一家用于人工智能模型训练和推理的第三方提供商。
攻击者使用暴露的密钥从用于与 Fireworks 共享信息的只读存储桶 Cursor 中复制数据。
该存储桶包含历史 AI 编码代理痕迹，大部分来自 2025 年，是从未启用隐私模式且其数据可用于模型训练的用户收集的。其中一些跟踪包含未经编辑的 API 凭据，允许攻击者访问其他 Cursor 系统。
Cursor 表示，只有不到 0.05% 的用户暴露了编码代理痕迹，而只有不到 0.01% 的客户 API 凭证遭到泄露。
使用暴露的凭据，黑客从 Cursor 的多个软件即服务 (SaaS) 工具中窃取了数据，包括：
已归档的非生产 Cursor 源代码存储库，其中一些包含业务联系信息。
有限的客户支持信息和电子邮件对话。
产品使用指标和客户联系方式。
一些人工智能编码代理对话的摘要。
客户之前与 Cursor 的支持团队共享的凭据。
Cursor 表示，其监控系统检测到未经授权的活动，导致该公司撤销 Fireworks 访问密钥、轮换暴露的凭据，并调查其他未经授权的访问。
随着调查的进展，Cursor 暂时关闭了一些内部和产品服务作为预防措施。
然而，攻击者已经获得了允许他们通过 Cursor 市场分发扩展的凭证。
10 月 29 日，黑客使用该凭据在 Cursor 的 VS Code 扩展市场上发布了 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意副本。
Cursor 解释说：“10 月 29 日，攻击者使用从我们内部系统暴露的数据中窃取的凭证，将 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意、未经授权的副本直接放置在用于服务 Cursor VS Code 扩展市场的缓存上。”
这次攻击没有损害 Anthropic 的合法扩展或 Cursor 使用的扩展市场 Open VSX。
恶意扩展版本 2.1.312 和 2.1.313 在 Cursor 删除它们之前已存在大约 11 小时。

【原文 English Original】
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirmed it suffered a security breach that let hackers distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI.
The breach also let attackers access internal systems and steal customer data, including historical AI coding-agent traces containing unredacted credentials that were later used to compromise additional services.
The breach was disclosed in a new incident report published Friday, which explains how attackers distributed malicious versions of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace on October 29.
The attack exposed up to 5,000 developers to malware that installed persistent SSH backdoors.
Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built on Microsoft's open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), allowing developers to write, modify, and debug software using AI assistants.
According to Cursor, the attack began when hackers obtained an access key stored on Fireworks AI, a third-party provider used for AI model training and inference.
The attackers used the exposed key to copy data from a read-only storage bucket Cursor used to share information with Fireworks.
This bucket contained historical AI coding-agent traces, mostly from 2025, collected from users who had not enabled Privacy Mode and whose data could be used for model training. Some of these traces contained unredacted API credentials, allowing the attackers to access additional Cursor systems.
Cursor says fewer than 0.05% of users had coding-agent traces exposed, while fewer than 0.01% of customers had API credentials compromised.
Using the exposed credentials, the hackers stole data from several of Cursor's software-as-a-service (SaaS) tools, including:
Archived, non-production Cursor source code repositories, some containing business contact information.
Limited customer support information and email conversations.
Product usage metrics and customer contact details.
Summaries of some AI coding-agent conversations.
Credentials that customers had previously shared with Cursor's support team.
Cursor says its monitoring systems detected the unauthorized activity, leading the company to revoke the Fireworks access key, rotate exposed credentials, and investigate additional unauthorized access.
As the investigation progressed, Cursor temporarily turned off some internal and product services as a precaution.
However, the attackers had already obtained a credential that allowed them to distribute extensions through Cursor's marketplace.
On October 29, the hackers used that credential to publish malicious copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace.
"On October 29, using a stolen credential from the exposed data from our internal system, the attacker placed malicious, unauthorized copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension directly on the cache used to serve the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace," Cursor explained.
The attack did not compromise Anthropic's legitimate extension or Open VSX, the extension marketplace Cursor uses.
The malicious extensions, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, were available for approximately 11 hours before Cursor removed them.
As BleepingComputer previously reported, the attackers modified the legitimate Claude Code extension to execute malicious JavaScript that attempted to install persistent SSH backdoors on developers' computers.
The malware collected system information, installed an attacker-controlled SSH key, attempted to enable SSH access, and configured persistence mechanisms to maintain remote access.
However, security researchers found coding errors that likely prevented the backdoor from working on many Windows and macOS systems where SSH was not already enabled.
Cursor estimates that up to 5,000 users who requested affected extension versions during the exposure window may have received the malicious builds.
The company says its production infrastructure, official application releases, customer code repositories, and code and prompts belonging to users with Privacy Mode enabled were not affected.
Cursor says it has moved all inference traffic away from Fireworks, revoked and rotated exposed credentials, rebuilt its extension marketplace, and redeployed its production infrastructure as a precaution.
Customers who installed or updated to the affected Claude Code extension during the attack are advised to follow Cursor's remediation guidance.
The incident comes amid a wave of attacks targeting AI developer platforms that cybersecurity company Wiz has dubbed "Black October".
These attacks targeted development infrastructure to steal authentication credentials, especially those providing access to AI models.
Stolen credentials have been used for unauthorized AI inference, generating substantial charges for affected customers, with some incidents also linked to attempts at AI model distillation.
The attacks have affected numerous companies, including Railway, Northflank, Lightning AI, OpenCode, and Warp.
At Railway, attackers stole customer authentication secrets, which were later used to generate approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges. OpenCode also reported exposed API keys and unauthorized AI usage.
Fireworks AI was also affected, disclosing multiple security breaches in October, including one involving exposed API keys and tokens and another in which attackers accessed development machines through a compromised third-party cloud provider.
The Fireworks incidents also affected other customers, including Notion, which recently disclosed that AI chat transcripts from a small number of workspaces were exposed.

title: Jensen Huang and the end of the ‘lol nothing matters’ era of American politics
zh_title: 黄仁勋和美国政治“哈哈无所谓”时代的结束
summary: 本专栏涉及人工智能行业的各个方面。我的未婚夫在 Anthropic 工作。请在此处查看我完整的道德披露。周四上午，英伟达宣布首席执行官黄仁勋已辞去公司职务。英伟达长期担任首席财务官的科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 将担任首席执行官，同时董事会正在寻找永久替代者。几个小时前，《纽约时报》报道称，黄有第二次婚外关系，这次是与一名下属。截至当天结束时，路透社爆料了第三个。首例报道的与疑似中国间谍艾丽克的恋情新闻
content:
本专栏涉及人工智能行业的各个方面。我的未婚夫在 Anthropic 工作。请在此处查看我完整的道德披露。周四上午，英伟达宣布首席执行官黄仁勋已辞去公司职务。英伟达长期担任首席财务官的科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 将担任首席执行官，同时董事会正在寻找永久替代者。几个小时前，《纽约时报》报道称，黄有第二次婚外关系，这次是与一名下属。截至当天结束时，路透社爆料了第三个。第一个被报道的与中国间谍嫌疑人黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 的恋情的消息导致投资者和其他首席执行官联盟宣布支持英伟达创始人。他们说，没有詹森的英伟达是不可想象的。然而到周四，不可思议的事情变成了现实。黄仁勋离开了他 33 年前在 Denny’s 共同创立的公司，而在 Nvidia 的公告中没有发表任何声明。不可否认，黄的垮台是一个悲剧，因为从很多方面来说，他都是一个美国非凡成功的故事：一个来自台湾的移民，9岁时被送到美国，用了30多年的时间把英伟达变成了世界上最大的公司。该公司在图形处理单元方面的深刻创新，包括使其可用于通用计算的软件，形成了一个庞大的生态系统，成为视频游戏、加密货币和前沿人工智能开发等多种行业的关键。
几乎所有人都认为，黄仁勋夸夸其谈、个人主义的风格对公司的成功至关重要，而公司的成功是具有里程碑意义的。（在他任职期间，英伟达的股票产生了 700,000% 的回报率。）它也适合这些夸夸其谈、个人主义的时代——当然，唐纳德·特朗普总统就是一个例子，但硅谷对创始人的崇拜也是如此。创始人拥有特殊地位，不应受到正常企业治理的约束，这是硅谷一些领先风险投资公司的信条。 Peter Thiel 的创始人基金于 2005 年成立，承诺永远不会将创始人从自己的公司中除名。安德森·霍洛维茨（Andreessen Horowitz）是管理资产规模最大的风险投资公司，它在其网站上承诺“永远不会公开批评任何企业家或初创公司”，并补充说“这样做是一种可被解雇的罪行”。 （不过，该公司有时确实会解雇创始人。）对创始人的崇拜是在一系列备受瞩目的事件之后出现的，在这些事件中，首席执行官因风投的干涉而被赶出自己的公司，最终损害了公司的利益。 Friendster 董事会在对创始人乔纳森·艾布拉姆斯 (Jonathan Abrams) 失去信心后，于 2004 年将其驱逐，之后又更换了几任首席执行官，最终尝试转向视频游戏，但注定失败。
Napster 时代结束后，肖恩·帕克 (Sean Parker) 被解雇了通讯录管理初创公司 Plaxo 的首席执行官，他接任 Facebook 首任总裁，并通过谈判让马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 获得了他至今仍享有的 Meta 投票控制权。最著名的是，苹果董事会将史蒂夫·乔布斯 (Steve Jobs) 赶出了苹果，导致该公司几近崩溃。当乔布斯于 1997 年重返苹果时，他拯救了这家公司——激励一代创始人将自己视为可以在正常业务范围之外运作的神话人物。对创始人的崇拜具有真正的价值，它使得投资者能够进行比以前更大、更长期的赌注。亚马逊、Meta、谷歌、Salesforce、

【原文 English Original】
This column touches on aspects of the AI industry. My fiancé works at Anthropic. See my full ethics disclosure here . On Thursday morning, Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned from the company. Colette Kress, Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer, will serve as CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement.  Hours earlier, the New York Times reported that Huang had been in a second extramarital relationship, this one with a subordinate. By the end of the day, Reuters had broken news of a third .  News of the first reported affair, with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, had led a coalition of investors and fellow CEOs to announce their support for Nvidia’s founder. Nvidia without Jensen was unthinkable, they said. By Thursday, though, the unthinkable had become reality. Huang departed the company he cofounded 33 years ago at a Denny’s without a statement of his own in Nvidia’s announcement.  There’s something undeniably tragic about Huang’s downfall, given that in so many ways his is a story of singular American success: an immigrant from Taiwan, sent to the United States at age 9, over 30 years he turned Nvidia into the world’s biggest company. The company’s profound innovations in graphics processing units, including software that made them useful for general-purpose computing, enabled a vast ecosystem that served as a linchpin for industries as diverse as video games, cryptocurrency, and frontier artificial intelligence development. Almost everyone agrees that Huang’s bombastic, personalistic style has been essential to the company’s success, which has been monumental. (During his tenure, Nvidia’s stock generated a 700,000 percent return .) It was also suited to these bombastic, personalistic times — exemplified by President Donald Trump, of course, but also by Silicon Valley’s cult of the founder.  The idea that founders have a special status and should not be subject to normal business governance is an article of faith at some of Silicon Valley’s leading venture capital firms. Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund launched in 2005 with a promise never to remove a founder from their own company. Andreessen Horowitz, the largest VC firm by assets under management, promises on its website to “never publicly criticize any entrepreneur or startup,” adding that “doing so is a fireable offense.” (The firm does sometimes remove founders, though.) The cult of the founder arose after a series of high-profile incidents in which CEOs were pushed out of their own companies by meddling VCs, to the ultimate detriment of the business. Friendster’s board pushed out founder Jonathan Abrams in 2004 after losing confidence in him, only to cycle through a series of CEOs before ultimately attempting a doomed pivot into video games. Post-Napster, after Sean Parker was fired as CEO of contacts-management startup Plaxo, he took a job as the first president of Facebook — and negotiated for Mark Zuckerberg to have the voting control over Meta that he continues to enjoy today. Most famously, Apple’s board pushed Steve Jobs out of Apple, leading to the company’s near-collapse. And when Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, he saved the company — inspiring a generation of founders to see themselves as mythical figures who could operate outside the normal bounds of business. There is real value in the cult of the founder, which has enabled bigger and longer-term bets than investors would previously entertain. Amazon, Meta, Google, Salesforce, and Netflix are among the tech giants that thrived under their original leadership. Y Combinator, which backed Stripe, Dropbox, Airbnb, and other generation-defining Silicon Valley companies, succeeded by making early bets on talented founders and not burdening them too much with meddlesome boards. For all the value that this approach has generated, though, it brought with it at least two major problems. One was that, as tech became an ever-larger part of the economy, the once-plucky founders who needed protection from overreaching VCs themselves became oligarchs: billionaires, centi-billionaires, and in Elon Musk’s case, a sometime trillionaire. The richer their companies became, the more successfully they used their power to lobby for their own interests. They established and defended monopolies, or near-monopolies, crushing competitors and narrowing the choices available to everyone else.  Meanwhile, the belief that they knew better than their investors expanded over time into a conviction that they knew better than the public, too. In social-media posts and interviews with journalists that grew rarer and more combative, they began to talk about threats to their wealth and authority as if they were threats to progress itself — and worked tirelessly to make sure their interests prevailed. Huang offered a vivid example of this phenomenon. Having legitimately played a key role in the technology behind the AI boom, he minimized any talk of the risks it might bring with it. Asked about the potential for loss-of-control scenarios in 2023, he told The New Yorker : “I know how it works, so there’s nothing there.” (He went on to say that AI functions similarly to a microwave.)  In his September interview with Ezra Klein , Huang dismissed predictions of catastrophe as irresponsible and argued that safety requires only better engineering and testing. To him, it was a technical problem that could be solved by companies moving even faster — and buying more Nvidia chips with which to do it. He brought a similar sense of grievance to his campaign against export controls. There are difficult tradeoffs involved in deciding to what extent chip sales to US adversaries should be restricted. Over time, denying China access to the upside of AI risks provoking significant conflict. At the same time, selling state-of-the-art chips to Chinese labs risks the prospect that ever-more powerful AI systems escape US control and are ultimately used against it.  Huang, who was reportedly terrified that his GPUs would be commoditized by the Chinese and so worked tirelessly to keep them within Nvidia’s own ecosystem, repeatedly resisted acknowledging that the tradeoffs even existed. When Dwarkesh Patel pressed him on the issue this year , Huang explicitly linked Nvidia’s fate to America’s. “Why would you want the United States to give up the world?” he asked. Later, he dismissed Patel’s framing of the risks as “childish.” To Huang, protecting Nvidia’s sales had become a patriotic obligation; the possibility that the US would benefit from a more measured approach to tech exports seemed almost impossible for him to entertain. The second big problem with Silicon Valley’s cult of the founder, and the flip side of entrusting flawed human beings with near-total power over their enterprises, is what investors call key-man risk . When hundreds of billions of dollars are at stake, it’s irresponsible for a company to have a single point of failure. And yet before news of Huang’s affairs broke, he was a 63-year-old man with more than 60 direct reports and apparently no succession plan. (He reportedly told colleagues he planned to run Nvidia until he was 120 years old.) When a company is generating 700,000 percent returns, no one wants to hear from the corporate-governance nags pointing out that one of the world’s most valuable companies is operating without a Plan B. Huang’s downfall shows why they should: you never know when behavior that was apparently already an open secret within some corners of Nvidia will spill into public view, destroying hundreds of billions of dollars worth of value and implicating an entire federal agency in a chip-smuggling scandal that now looks to extend well into 2027.  It would have been no slight to Huang’s accomplishments over the past decade for a board member to insist that Nvidia identify and groom a bench of successors. In fact, had he and the board ensured that a successor was prepared to take the reins, they would have won praise. (Tim Cook’s silky smooth handoff of the CEO job to John Ternus this year makes for a dramatic point of comparison; perhaps that's why Trump now wants Cook for Nvidia CEO.) Unfortunately for Nvidia, and the wider economy that has increasingly come to rely on it, no such precautions were taken. It must have been easy, in the era of Trump and Musk, to assume that accountability had become a thing of the past. To believe any company that is too big to fail must be run by a CEO too big to get in trouble. (Little wonder that Trump reportedly called Huang on Tuesday and urged him to keep his job, no matter how the CEO’s indiscretions may have compromised national security.) But the blue tsunami of this month’s midterm elections suggests that the “lol nothing matters” era of US business and politics may be coming to an end. It has become all too clear that with few exceptions, the ultrawealthy are rarely looking out for anyone’s interests but their own. In the end, like so many American giants before him, Huang was brought down by his sex drive. But the real scandal is that he thought only he could run the company he founded, and now the rest of us have to live with the consequences. A MESSAGE FROM OUR SPONSOR Who gave that agent permission? title: Beijing’s Taiwan ‘Reunification’ Dreams Are Fanciful
zh_title: 北京的台湾“统一”梦是痴人说梦
summary: 中国北京的台湾“统一”梦想是幻想 台北可能会对北京变得更加友好，但台湾人珍惜自己的主权。 （安东尼·华莱士/法新社，盖蒂图片社）唐纳德·特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平都已采取措施，防止台湾问题成为双边关系紧张的主要根源。在今年特朗普和习近平的两次峰会上，他们的共同目标尤其明显。然而，尽管北京最近采取了和解态度，但没有迹象表明中华人民共和国（PRC）已经放弃了长期的立场。
content:
中国北京的台湾“统一”梦想是幻想 台北可能会对北京变得更加友好，但台湾人珍惜自己的主权。 （安东尼·华莱士/法新社，盖蒂图片社）唐纳德·特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平都已采取措施，防止台湾问题成为双边关系紧张的主要根源。在今年特朗普和习近平的两次峰会上，他们的共同目标尤其明显。然而，尽管北京最近采取了和解态度，但没有迹象表明中华人民共和国放弃了吞并台湾并结束其民主、事实上的独立国家地位的长期目标。习近平政权似乎正在采取双管齐下的战略来实现这一目标：北京对由官方支持独立的民进党控制的现任台湾政府维持不妥协的、有时甚至是军事威胁的政策；与此同时，中华人民共和国官员大量暗示，北京愿意对民进党更为温和的对手、2008年至2016年统治台湾的国民党采取不那么对抗的姿态。北京已经向国民党领导人郑立文伸出了政治橄榄枝，特别是在她2026年4月访问大陆期间。
布鲁金斯学会非常驻高级研究员迈克尔·波兹南斯基 (Michael Poznansky) 和印度太平洋安全研究所非常驻高级研究员伊恩·伊斯顿 (Ian Easton) 在《外交政策》 10 月 6 日的一篇文章中认为，美国领导人需要研究不流血吞并的可能性，即台北民选政府缔结一项条约，有效地将台湾领土割让给中华人民共和国。这种被称为“不战而胜”或“和平统一”等委婉说法的战略是北京更希望的结果。华盛顿对此毫无准备。习近平和其他中华人民共和国领导人无疑更愿意通过政治和经济手段实现台湾与大陆的统一。使用军事力量来这样做将是非常危险且不可预测的。事实上，这样的做法可能会导致与该岛主要军事保护国美国和日本的战争。中国领导人长期以来提出“一个国家，两种制度”的模式作为统一的模式。台湾将成为统一的中国的一部分，但不会受到北京的控制。从本质上讲，所承诺的一国两制安排类似于中国领导人在1997年将香港的所有权从英国移交给中华人民共和国时签署的协议。香港政治自治的规定甚至被写入基本法并保障50年。
台湾的一国两制模式将包括更大的承诺自治权，包括军事事务上的自治权。此外，与香港协议不同的是，中华人民共和国当前的政策没有规定台湾自治地位的结束日期。尽管如此，北京不太可能仅通过更大的政治和经济影响力来成功结束台湾事实上的独立。 2020 年 6 月，中华人民共和国对香港实施安全镇压，北京在台湾人眼中的信誉受到严重损害。该领土承诺的自治权被大幅缩小，几乎变得毫无意义。媒体大亨黎智英和其他直言不讳的民主人士

【原文 English Original】
China Beijing’s Taiwan ‘Reunification’ Dreams Are Fanciful Taipei may become friendlier to Beijing, but the Taiwanese cherish their sovereignty. (ANTHONY WALLACE/AFP via Getty Images) Both President Donald Trump and China’s leader Xi Jinping have taken steps to prevent the Taiwan issue from becoming a major source of tension in bilateral relations. Their joint goal was especially evident during the two summit meetings between Trump and Xi this year. Despite Beijing’s recent conciliatory approach, however, there is no indication that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has relinquished its long-term goal of absorbing Taiwan and ending its status as a democratic, de facto independent state.  Xi’s regime appears to be pursuing a two-pronged strategy to achieve that objective: Beijing sustains an uncompromising, sometimes even militarily menacing, policy toward the current Taiwanese government, which is controlled by the officially pro-independence Democratic Progressive Party (DPP); at the same time, PRC officials drop abundant hints that Beijing would be willing to adopt a less confrontational posture toward the DPP’s more moderate rival, the Kuomintang Party (KMT) that last governed Taiwan from 2008 to 2016. Beijing has already extended political olive branches to the KMT leader Cheng Li-wun, especially during her visit to the mainland in April 2026.  In an October 6 article in Foreign Policy , Michael Poznansky, a nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, and Ian Easton, a senior nonresident fellow at the Institute for Indo-Pacific Security, contend that U.S. leaders need to examine the possibility of a bloodless annexation, whereby an elected government in Taipei concludes a treaty effectively ceding Taiwan’s territory to the People’s Republic of China. Such a strategy, known by euphemisms like “winning without fighting” or “peaceful reunification,” is Beijing’s preferred outcome . And Washington is unprepared for it. Xi and other PRC leaders undoubtedly would prefer to achieve Taiwan’s reunification with the mainland through political and economic means. Using military force to do so would be highly dangerous and unpredictable. Indeed, such a course would probably lead to war with the United States and Japan, the island’s principal military protectors. PRC leaders have long proposed the formula of “one country, two systems” as a model for reunification. Taiwan would become part of a reunited China, but it would not be controlled from Beijing. In essence, the promised one country, two systems arrangement is similar to the agreement that Chinese leaders signed in 1997 when possession of Hong Kong was transferred from Britain to the PRC. The provision for Hong Kong’s political autonomy was even written into its Basic Law and guaranteed for 50 years. The one country, two systems model for Taiwan would include even greater promised autonomy, including on military affairs. Moreover, unlike the agreement regarding Hong Kong, current PRC policy does not specify an end date for Taiwan’s autonomous status. Nevertheless, Beijing is unlikely to succeed in ending Taiwan’s de facto independence solely through greater political and economic influence. Extensive damage to Beijing’s credibility with the Taiwanese occurred when the PRC executed a security crackdown on Hong Kong in June 2020 . The territory’s promised autonomy was so drastically narrowed as to become virtually meaningless. The media mogul Jimmy Lai and other vocal democracy activists subsequently received long prison sentences, and a suffocating atmosphere of coerced political conformity settled over the once ideologically vibrant city.  Taiwan’s population was watching, and most Taiwanese did not like what they saw . Indeed, the Hong Kong lesson was a major factor in the DPP’s subsequent surge in political power.  Granted, current President Lai Ching-te of the DPP has dissipated much of that gain because of corruption within his administration, as well as his own authoritarian abuses. Many Taiwanese also worry about Lai’s extremely hardline, confrontational rhetoric and policies toward Beijing. Yet there is a crucial difference between a growing desire by Taiwanese voters to rein in DPP excesses and a willingness to abandon Taiwan’s status as a de facto independent country. Numerous opinion polls have confirmed that no more than a tiny percentage of Taiwanese favor reunification with the totalitarian, one-party state across the strait. The hostile reaction to the PRC’s crackdown on Hong Kong indicated that the Taiwanese are determined not to let their island suffer a similar fate. Even most KMT supporters do not want to see Taiwan become Beijing’s puppet or their party to become subsumed into the PRC. If Xi and other PRC leaders are content with seeing a more conciliatory, less confrontational government emerge in Taipei, they have a very good chance of achieving their objective. That benign outcome is especially likely if they are simultaneously willing to reduce the PRC’s military presence in and around the Taiwan Strait.   But if they continue to press for reunification (even solely by peaceful means) they are likely to be disappointed. Indeed, even if Beijing pursued a more limited goal of transforming Taiwan into an obedient, albeit still nominally self-governing, client under the KMT, such an effort would likely fail.  In her March 3 Foreign Affairs article, Cheng Li-wun, the KMT leader, conveyed her party’s orientation rather pointedly: As Beijing and Washington compete for influence in the Pacific, how Taiwan manages cross-strait relations affects whether the region remains peaceful and stable. Many observers assume that Taiwan must choose to align itself with one side or the other. But this binary framing is misleading. Taiwan is strongest when it preserves space to pursue its own needs, not when it becomes a frontline outpost for one country or a subordinate partner to the other. There is not a yawning gap between the views of most KMT leaders and those of the more sensible elements of the DPP regarding policy toward Beijing. Lai, though president, is among the more extreme (and sometimes recklessly assertive) pro-independence party activists. Voters may well reject that faction in the next national election in favor of the KMT, but such an outcome would not signal a popular mandate for Taipei to embrace an appeasement policy toward the PRC. It is appropriate for U.S. policymakers to carefully monitor developments, but there is no need to panic nor to conjure improbable worst-case scenarios involving a clever PRC ploy to conquer Taiwan via a political offensive. The post Beijing’s Taiwan ‘Reunification’ Dreams Are Fanciful appeared first on The American Conservative .

title: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress

被罢免的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋同意在国会作证
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋同意在国会宣誓作证。黄仁勋因有报道称他与一名涉嫌为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染而被赶出了公司。
彭博社报道称，众议院外交事务主席布莱恩·马斯特（R-FL）告诉记者，黄在几位高级议员威胁要传唤他后同意出庭。
预计作证将在感恩节前进行。马斯特表示，会议将闭门进行，但会录制视频并进行转录。三个国会机构计划参加：马斯特担任主席的众议院外交事务委员会、众议院中国小组和众议院情报小组。
马斯特此前曾与黄发生过公开冲突，尤其是在出口管制方面。但他表示，其中的利害关系超出了任何一项政策争端。 “詹森和我一直存在很大分歧，因为你们中的一些人已经了解出口管制，但英伟达对美利坚合众国来说是一家非常重要的公司，”马斯特说。
他补充说，尽管黄面临着审查，但他并不打算损害公司本身。 “我不想看到英伟达受到任何伤害，但他有一些非常严肃的问题需要回答，”马斯特说。
黄先生离开英伟达之前，有报道称黄先生与一名涉嫌为中国情报机构工作的女性有关系。黄在这段关系中可能披露或讨论的内容预计将成为立法者出现在三个委员会面前时提出的问题的核心。
Breitbart News 对黄仁勋被罢黜进行了广泛报道。该公司自己的股东正在就丑闻造成的损失起诉这家科技巨头：
Schall, Brown & Schwartz律师事务所率先就英伟达中国间谍丑闻展开调查。随后罗森律师事务所提起了集体诉讼。
该诉讼称，黄仁勋和英伟达在这种关系引起的国家安全担忧方面误导了股东，并且这种疏忽人为地推高了英伟达的股价。诉状称：“由于被告的不当行为和不作为，以及公司证券市值的急剧下跌，原告和其他集体成员遭受了重大损失和损害。”
英伟达表示已对黄发起独立调查。在有报道称黄为“外国情报工作的目标”后，该公司董事会展开调查，英伟达股价随之下跌。北京否认了这一指控。

Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress
Jensen Huang, the former Nvidia CEO who was pushed out of the company following reports he had an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, has agreed to testify before Congress under oath.
Bloomberg reports that House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast (R-FL) told reporters that Huang agreed to appear after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
The testimony is expected to happen before Thanksgiving. Mast said it will take place behind closed doors, though it will be recorded on video and transcribed. Three congressional bodies plan to take part: the House Foreign Affairs Committee, which Mast chairs, the House China panel and the House Intelligence panel.
Mast has clashed publicly with Huang before, particularly over export controls. But he said the stakes go beyond any one policy dispute. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said.
He added that he isn’t looking to damage the company itself, even as Huang faces scrutiny. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer,” Mast said.
Huang’s departure from Nvidia followed reports of a relationship with a woman suspected of working on behalf of Chinese intelligence. What Huang may have disclosed or discussed during that relationship is expected to be central to lawmakers’ questions when he appears before the three committees.
Breitbart News has reported extensively on Jensen Huang’s ouster. The company’s own shareholders are suing the tech giant over losses caused by the scandal:
The law firm of Schall, Brown & Schwartz was the first to launch an investigation of Nvidia over the Chinese spy scandal. The class-action lawsuit was then filed by the Rosen Law Firm.
The lawsuit claims Huang and Nvidia misled shareholders about the national security concerns the relationship raised, and that the omission artificially propped up Nvidia’s share price. “As a result of Defendants’ wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages,” the complaint states.
Nvidia has said it launched an independent investigation into Huang. The company’s board opened its inquiry after reports described Huang as “the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” and Nvidia shares fell in the aftermath. Beijing has denied the allegation.

星期日, 15 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
维多利亚港游泳促使香港作出特别交通安排
约4,000名游泳运动员将于11月15日参加维多利亚港游泳比赛，从湾仔金紫荆广场公众码头出发，至尖沙咀天星码头结束。湾仔北及尖沙咀将实施特别交通及运输安排
2026 年 11 月 15 日，香港时间 00:38 · 更新于 11 月 15 日，04:29 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
约4,000名泳手将于11月15日上午参加维港泳赛，由湾仔金紫荆广场公众码头出发，终点为尖沙咀天星码头。湾仔北及尖沙咀将实施特别交通及运输安排，水上的士及渡轮服务于活动期间暂停。
金紫荆广场外的博览道东一段路段，包括落客区，将于中午 12:30 至下午 1:00 左右暂时封闭。由于湾仔及尖沙咀的登岸台阶关闭，来往尖东及中环的水上的士服务将取消上午10时40分、上午11时20分及中午12时10分由尖沙咀东开出的班次。
来往湾仔至尖沙咀的渡轮服务将于首班航班暂停至上午 11:00。来往中环至红磡的渡轮服务将于上午 11 时 10 分之前取消第一趟班次。
运输署表示，水上的士及渡轮服务将视乎受影响港口地区的实际重新开放时间而恢复。过海巴士 961 号线的终点站将于下午 1:00 前首班巴士迁往湾仔游泳池外的港湾径。城巴H3线位于博览道东近金紫荆广场的巴士站亦将暂停服务。

Victoria Harbour swim prompts special transport arrangements in Hong Kong
About 4,000 swimmers will take part in the Victoria Harbour swim on 15 November, starting from the Golden Bauhinia Square public pier in Wan Chai and finishing at the Tsim Sha Tsui Star Ferry Pier. Special traffic and transport arrangements will be implemented in Wan Chai North and Tsim Sha Tsui, wi
15 Nov 2026 at 00:38 HKT · updated 15 Nov, 04:29 · 1 min read
About 4,000 swimmers will take part in the Victoria Harbour swim on the morning of 15 November, starting from the Golden Bauhinia Square public pier in Wan Chai and finishing at the Tsim Sha Tsui Star Ferry Pier. Special traffic and transport arrangements will be implemented in Wan Chai North and Tsim Sha Tsui, with water taxi and ferry services suspended during the event.
A section of Expo Drive East outside Golden Bauhinia Square, including the drop-off area, will be temporarily closed from 12:30am to about 1:00pm. Due to the closure of landing steps in Wan Chai and Tsim Sha Tsui, the water taxi service between Tsim Sha Tsui East and Central will cancel departures from Tsim Sha Tsui East at 10:40am, 11:20am and 12:10pm.
The ferry service between Wan Chai and Tsim Sha Tsui will be suspended from the first sailing until 11:00am. The ferry service between Central and Hung Hom will cancel departures from the first sailing until 11:10am.
The Transport Department said water taxi and ferry services will resume depending on the actual reopening time of the affected harbour areas. The terminus of cross-harbour bus route 961 will be relocated to Harbour Drive outside Wan Chai Swimming Pool from the first bus until 1:00pm. The Citybus route H3 bus stop on Expo Drive East near Golden Bauhinia Square will also be suspended.

content:
天气转凉，香港十七家煲仔饭餐厅值得一试 |中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 15 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
天气转凉，香港十七家煲仔饭餐厅值得一试
随着天气转凉，香港岛、九龙和新界 17 家煲仔饭餐厅指南，从米其林必比登推介精选到邻里最爱餐厅。
随着天气转凉，发现香港最好的煲仔饭比以往任何时候都更容易，我们以连续叙述的形式列出了香港 17 个最佳地点的地理目录，以指导您的美食之旅。
以香港岛为起点，铜锣湾充满活力的餐饮中心是 Yorucho 的所在地，位于登龙街 28 号圆塔 16 楼，专营现代日韩融合煲仔饭。在邻近的湾仔，食客可以选择位于汤申道105至111号哈佛商业大厦一楼的LAI's Kitchen，以丰富的自家炼制猪油而闻名，或位于皇后大道东183号合和中心六楼的米其林必比登美食推荐的船记，供应传统手工粤式煲仔饭。
继续向西，位于西环皇后大道西 263 号和益大厦地下 1 号店的均记煲仔饭仍然是街坊们的最爱，而位于坚尼地城北街 25 号地下的双喜则使用火山石炉来制作完美的锅巴。位于岛东侧的兆华厨房，位于筲箕湾爱秩序湾道15号爱秩序湾街市熟食中心CF1及3档位，提供超过30种创意搭配。
穿过九龙，旺角熙熙攘攘的街道上有两个独特的场地。位于弥敦道 575 号嘉登中心五楼的香港老街，将桌边煮的煲仔饭与火锅搭配；位于花园街 18 号飘柔阁地下 4 至 6 号铺的艾山煲仔饭则供应火辣的湘式炒饭。
再往南，位于油麻地庙街 15 号的怀旧庙街兴记酒楼至今仍是历史悠久的热点。往九龙东边走，永记酒家位于慈云山毓华街12号地下A至B铺，以其引人注目的火焰玫瑰色酒壶而闻名。
新蒲岗是主要的煲仔饭中心，包括位于景福街 87 号的江爷家，以及位于天后流里街 9 号地下的分店，以及位于延庆街 56 号地下的美味煲仔饭。附近的深水埗基隆街 187 号底层，Chikayan Hotpot Rice 供应经济实惠的明火煲仔饭。位于九龙区的泰锅 (Thai Pot) 位于观塘观塘道 414 号一太中心 10 楼，供应定制煲仔饭。
在新界，荃湾拥有两个独特的选择。位于后地坊30号宝成大厦地下1号铺的江胡兆昌以其可定制的猪油饭而备受好评，而内地连锁店金昌记煲仔饭则在富华街9号地下L号铺推出了特色鳗鱼炒蛋煲仔饭。最后，在屯门，元宵餐厅位于屯顺街1号屯门市广场一期三楼3230号铺，提供优质、高端的海鲜煲仔饭，为这份终极冬季指南画上完美句号。

Seventeen claypot rice spots to try in Hong Kong as weather turns cool
A guide to 17 claypot rice restaurants across Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and the New Territories, from Michelin Bib Gourmand picks to neighbourhood favourites, as cooler weather arrives.
As cooler weather arrives, discovering Hong Kong's best claypot rice is easier than ever with a geographical directory of the city's top 17 spots, written in continuous narrative form to guide your culinary journey.
Starting on Hong Kong Island, the vibrant dining hub of Causeway Bay is home to Yorucho, located on the 16th floor of Circle Tower at 28 Tang Lung Street, which specialises in modern Japanese-Korean fusion claypots. In neighbouring Wan Chai, diners can choose between LAI's Kitchen, situated on the first floor of the Harvard Commercial Building at 105 to 111 Thomson Road, known for its rich house-rendered lard, or the Michelin Bib Gourmand-recommended Ship Kee on the sixth floor of Hopewell Centre at 183 Queen's Road East, which serves traditional handcrafted Cantonese claypots.
Heading west, Kwan Kee Claypot Rice at Shop 1 on the ground floor of Wo Yick Mansion on 263 Queen's Road West in Sai Wan remains a legendary neighbourhood favourite, while Sheung Hei on the ground floor of 25 North Street in Kennedy Town uses volcanic stone-heated stoves for perfect rice crusts. On the eastern side of the island, Siu Wah Kitchen offers more than 30 creative pairings at Stalls CF1 and 3 of the Aldrich Bay Market Cooked Food Centre on 15 Aldrich Bay Road in Shau Kei Wan.
Crossing over to Kowloon, the bustling streets of Mong Kok host two unique venues. Hong Kong Old Street, located on the fifth floor of Callton Center at 575 Nathan Road, pairs its tableside-cooked claypot rice with hotpot, while Ai Shan Claypot Kee at Shops 4 to 6 on the ground floor of Rejoice Court on 18 Fa Yuen Street serves fiery Hunan-style stir-fries over rice.
Further south in Yau Ma Tei, the nostalgic Temple Street Hing Kee Restaurant at 15 Temple Street remains a historic hotspot. Moving towards the eastern side of Kowloon, Wing Kee Restaurant at Shop A to B on the ground floor of 12 Yuk Wah Crescent in Tsz Wan Shan is famous for its dramatic flame-rose wine pots.
San Po Kong is a major claypot hub, featuring Kong Yeah Home at 87 King Fuk Street, which also has a branch on the ground floor of 9 Lau Li Street in Tin Hau, and Delicious Claypot Rice on the ground floor of 56 Yin Hing Street. Nearby in Sham Shui Po, Chikayan Hotpot Rice serves budget-friendly, open-flame claypots on the ground floor of 187 Ki Lung Street. Rounding out Kowloon, Thai Pot serves made-to-order claypots on the tenth floor of One Pacific Centre at 414 Kwun Tong Road in Kwun Tong.
In the New Territories, Tsuen Wan boasts two exceptional options. Kong Wu Siu Jaan at Shop 1 on the ground floor of Po Shing Mansion on 30 Hau Tei Square is highly regarded for its customisable lard-infused rice, while the mainland chain Kam Chaang Kee Claypot Rice brings its speciality eel and scrambled egg claypots to Shop L on the ground floor of 9 Fu Wah Street. Finally, in Tuen Mun, Lantern Restaurant serves premium, high-end seafood claypots at Shop 3230 on the third floor of Tuen Mun Town Plaza Phase 1 at 1 Tuen Shun Street, completing this ultimate winter guide.
