content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!

content:
2025年5月22日，台北国际电脑展期间，Megaspeed前中国高管黄乐(右)在台北一家餐厅参加由英伟达前首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋(左，身穿黑色背对摄像头)主持的晚宴。(视频截图)
美国芯片巨头英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)与疑似中国间谍黄乐(Alice Wong)的婚外情风波，意外将美国对华芯片出口监管的难度和漏洞推上台面。
新加坡注册的Megaspeed及其前中国籍高管黄乐曾成功购入价值数十亿美元的英伟达先进芯片,这些芯片如何通过所谓的“新加坡洗白”流入中国？将芯片部署在第三地数据中心，再远程向中国企业出租算力，是否已成为规避美国出口禁令的灰色地带？
随着事件发酵，美国国会多个议员已经呼吁进一步收紧对华芯片管制，专家们预测，相关操作空间也恐将受到压缩。
新加坡内政部(Ministry of Home Affairs)星期四(11月12日)晚间发布的一份声明，进一步揭露了Megaspeed令人生疑的运作。
新加坡警方和海关早在去年2月就对Megaspeed等多家公司及其主要负责人，包括时任董事长兼执行长的黄乐在内，就其涉嫌在购买服务器时做虚假申报以及其他相关违法行为展开调查。新加坡当局说，他们并非调查她是否涉及间谍活动。
结果显示，Megaspeed购入的伺服器，中转新加坡后再出口至马来西亚，期间未流入新加坡本地市场。目前警方还在追查这些伺服器运抵马来西亚后，是否违反对新加坡海关的申报，或甚至已被转运他国。
新加坡警方称其一度谘询美超微公司(Supermicro)，但有过走私芯片到中国的美超微合作意愿不高，美国当局提供的资讯也有限。
声明还说，去年6月24日，美国商务部工业与安全局(BIS)在黄乐陪同下，展开对Megaspeed装运伺服器后的实地核查，这是新加坡首次获知Megaspeed和黄乐遭美方锁定。
新加坡警方当日也同步录取黄乐的口供，且因她未在新加坡长住，依法扣押其护照以确保她配合后续调查。警方认定，黄乐于调查期间，提供不实信息且企图淡化其在Megaspeed的角色，但最后因证据不足，仅对她提出严厉警告，并于今年2月26日归还她的护照，并禁止她再次入境，黄乐也于同日离境。
美国之音以电邮致函Megaspeed进一步谘询，但截稿前未获回应，三度致电其新加坡总部电话，总机自动应答“电话不通”后即遭挂断，不禁令人质疑其正常运营现况。
纽约做空机构Culper Research早于今年5月就发布报告称，中国科技企头阿里巴巴是Megaspeed背后的金主，尤令人咋舌的是，Megaspeed的总资产从2023年的约3,300万美元，一年内就暴增90倍至2024年的近30亿美元，而且从默默无闻，一跃成为英伟达在亚太区的最大芯片买家。
根据新加坡工商注册资料，Megaspeed前身是2015年注册成立的7Road International，即中国游戏公司第七大道，2023年3月才更名为Megaspeed International。
Megaspeed现由在新加坡注册的Swiftdata全资拥有，Swiftdata成立于2023年10月，自称其为提供云算力和伺服器的服务公司，而非传统的数据中心建设和营运商。
分析人士认为，Megaspeed恐为空壳公司，但其“洗白”后的新加坡法人企业身分可规避美国禁令，向英伟达等美企大肆采购AI高级芯片。
台北智库科技、民主与社会研究中心(DSET)的经济安保组海外研究员曾稚骅曾稚骅说:“它(Megaspeed/新加坡)就是一个中转站、一个节点，这些(芯片)甚至都没有进到新加坡本地的市场，就直接出口，透过Aivres去采购(组装)，把它放到马来西亚跟印尼等地(的数据中心)，再把算力回租给阿里巴巴或其他中企，也有部分(芯片)疑似直接流回中国。”
Aivres原为中国伺服器巨头浪潮集团(Inspur)的海外子公司，美国于2023年将浪潮打入黑名单后，其美国子公司并更名为Aivres，至今未遭美国列名，继续在硅谷运营。
他说，Megaspeed的迂回操作对英伟达的客户认证(know your customers, KYC)造成挑战，也增加美国跨海进行终端用户查核(end-user check, EUC)的难度，尤其新加坡一再重申中立立场，不执行他国单边的出口管制，对美国芯片监管的配合度或有限。
不过，新加坡当局也坚称，绝不包庇外企利用与新加坡的关联，以不实手法规避他国出口管制的行径。
《黄仁勋传(The Thinking Machine)》一书作者、美国籍科技记者史蒂芬·维特（Stephen Witt）在接受《纽约时报》播客节目采访时表示，Megaspeed另设在马来西亚的数据中心也是其对华走私芯片的中转站，这是业界心照不宣的秘密。
他指出，业内推测两大可能手法，一是高级芯片运抵大马数据中心后，标签随即被撕除并换上伪造标签，真假调包后，循后门走私途径运抵中国；二是在大马数据中心建置算力机房，远端转租给中企使用。
维特表示，境外设空壳公司正是规避美国出口管制的典型走私伎俩。
以今年3月遭美国起诉的美超微走私案为例，内部人员就对装满英伟达芯片的外箱动过手脚，用吹风机热风软化胶水，撕除原厂出货标签后，再贴上假标签掩人耳目。
若Megaspeed循美超微模式非法转运AI芯片至中国，相关人士恐面临美国司法部的追诉。不过，若是后者算力转租的模式，美国目前似乎无法可办，唯美国各界已呼吁，严查Megaspeed或将其与Aivres打入黑名单。
对此，Megaspeed星期四发布声明称，将配合美国政府和BIS，全面清查旗下图形处理器(GPU)，以具体行动证明营运合规。
该公司接任黄乐的现任新加坡籍董事长暨执行长陈永邦(James Tan Yong Pong)强调，Megaspeed高度重视遵守美国出口管制法律的义务，将合规视为基本优先事项，也已委托美国知名律所独立查核，并全面配合美国政府相关机关的合规要求。
多年来，中国企业利用“新加坡洗白”的方式，将业务、控股结构或总部“出海”转移至新加坡，以隐藏与中国的连结并降低地缘政治风险，或借由新加坡的国际信誉进行“品牌或身份洗白”。
不过，此策略已引来新加坡人士的诟病，壳牌公司(Shell)亚太区国际/政府关系总监林瑞光就曾公开呼吁，新加坡应从政策上避免留下“脏水”的“新加坡洗白”，并建议来到新加坡的外企“浸泡”融入本地。
新加坡国立大学政治系副教授庄嘉颖也说，贸易中间人的角色让新加坡商有利可图，但不管是洗芯片，还是之前帮缅甸和北韩规避制裁买军火，当局应正视这种洗白手法对新加坡带来的商誉损失和风险，例如遭二级制裁(secondary sanction)的风险。
庄嘉颖告诉美国之音:“新加坡洗白这种行为，之前大国角逐没有那么剧烈……华盛顿或北京可能会有一些埋怨，(但)不会做什么。可是现在两边对于彼此的疑心更大，所以他们可能更愿意去制裁第三方。”
他说，美国对新加坡二级制裁的工具包括，限制新加坡对美投资的金流或提高审核门槛、或提高对新加坡产品的海关查验程度，甚至解除新加坡护照的美国免签优惠待遇等。
不过，台北研究人员曾稚骅说，随着黄仁勋风暴掀开芯片采购的可能“洗芯片”弊端，未来美国对华芯片禁令恐升级，也会压缩“新加坡洗白”的空间。
黄仁勋的婚外情丑闻曝光后，美国国会两院两党议员表示将立法加强芯片出口管控，并推动将有关限制措施写入必须尽快通过的年度《国防授权法案》(NDAA)。
曾稚骅说:“洗芯片、新加坡洗白这事，它未来的空间应该只会越来越小了，因为现在外部要检视新加坡或东南亚国家的压力只会越来越多，如KYC的压力等等，这个(洗芯片)空间本来就会很少。”
国际调研机构Counterpoint Research位于印度孟买的研究副总裁尼尔·沙（Neil Shah）以电邮接受美国之音采访时表示，Megaspeed惹议后，在新加坡注册的AI、云服务公司和经销商，未来恐面临更冗长的监管稽核，包括落实KYC审查等程序，这对规模较小或新设的主机托管业者带来冲击，整个亚太区域的企业订单处理也将放缓，以便查明芯片或算力负载的最终流向。
不过，他说，新加坡电信(Singtel)等既有业者或将受惠，因为相较来历不明的中间商，监管机关与供应商将更倾向直接与已上市、营运透明的电信业者合作。
尼尔·沙研判，当地企业未来也恐积极寻求英伟达以外的供应来源，如测试超威(AMD)及其他客制化芯片供应商的替代方案，以免于承受额外审查。

中美战略稳定未到水深火热
习近平和特朗普在北京同意建立战略稳定的“建设性”关系（在新窗口中打开），并于 9 月在白宫重申了这一方案（在新窗口中打开），近六个月后，两国军队再次进行了对话。然而，在十月的最后一周，中国海军和海岸警卫队船只在日本南部海峡到棉兰老岛附近海域活跃。
这些事实并不矛盾。该框架从未承诺冻结军事竞争，并且根据其实际承诺来判断，它取得的进展不大。问题更窄也更严重：现有的渠道不匹配，可能会发生危险的遭遇。无论意图如何，其结果都是双边平静与地区压力并存。
从承诺的事情开始。根据北京峰会的消息，两军同意“尽快”缔结一份关于危机沟通和预防的备忘录（在新窗口中打开）。白宫情况说明书没有提及此事（在新窗口中打开），据报道，一位美国官员表示（在新窗口中打开）没有讨论该主题。尽管如此，指挥层的接触已经恢复：美国印太司令在加拿大会见了负责台湾海峡的中国同行（在新窗口中打开）。
9月份解放军在台湾周边的空中活动仍低于去年的水平。尽管活动较 8 月有所反弹，但据台湾安全监测机构统计， 9 月份的飞机出动次数为 255 架次，比 2025 年 9 月减少了 43%（在新窗口中打开）。海上压力呈现出不同的景象：10 月 31 日，北京宣布海岸警卫队在台湾东部巡逻（在新窗口中打开），台北对此提出质疑。因此，较少的出动次数提供了不完全的限制措施。
日历现在很重要。
该框架最有力的防御是危机管理使竞争对手能够保持威慑力，同时防止事故升级。美国太平洋陆军仍将 2027 年视为战备基准（在新窗口中打开），尽管路透社 10 月 1 日援引未具名消息人士的话说，美国官员认为 2028 年之前采取军事行动的可能性越来越小（在新窗口中打开）。然而，低于战争门槛的压力仍在继续。 10 月 23 日，台湾海岸警卫队警告说，中国民兵和海岸警卫队的协调行动（在新窗口中打开）正在加大对台湾、日本和菲律宾的压力。

A Chinese Coast Guard vessel’s crew film a Philippine supply boat near Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea, 5 March 2024 – one of regular confrontations between the two countries’ vessels in the area (Ezra Acayan/Getty Images)
US–China strategic stability doesn’t reach the water
Renewed military dialogue is a step forward, but the channels do not yet reach the coast guards and allies where maritime incidents are most likely.

|US–China strategic stability doesn’t reach the water
US–China strategic stability doesn’t reach the water
Nearly six months after Xi Jinping and Donald Trump agreed in Beijing to build a “constructive” relationship of strategic stability (Opens in new window), a formula they reaffirmed at the White House in September (Opens in new window), their militaries are talking again. Yet in the last week of October, Chinese navy and coast guard ships were active from Japan’s southern straits to the waters off Mindanao.
These facts are not a contradiction. The framework never promised to freeze military competition, and judged against its actual commitments it is making modest progress. The problem is narrower and more serious: the channels that exist do not fit together where dangerous encounters can occur. Whatever the intent, the effect is that bilateral calm and regional pressure coexist.
Start with what was promised. According to Beijing’s summit readout, the two militaries agreed to conclude a memorandum (Opens in new window) on crisis communication and prevention “as soon as possible”. The White House fact sheet did not mention it (Opens in new window), and a US official reportedly said (Opens in new window) the subject was not discussed. Command-level contact has nonetheless resumed: the US Indo-Pacific commander met his Chinese counterpart (Opens in new window) responsible for the Taiwan Strait in Canada.
PLA air activity around Taiwan was still below last year’s level in September. The Taiwan Security Monitor counted 255 sorties in September, 43% fewer than in September 2025 (Opens in new window), although activity rebounded from August. Maritime pressure presents a different picture: on 31 October, Beijing announced coast guard patrols east of Taiwan (Opens in new window), which Taipei challenged. The lower sortie count, therefore, offers an incomplete measure of restraint.
The calendar now matters.
The strongest defence of the framework is that crisis management allows rivals to maintain deterrence while preventing accidents from escalating. US Army Pacific still treats 2027 as a readiness benchmark (Opens in new window), although news agency Reuters reported on 1 October, citing unnamed sources, that US officials considered a military operation before 2028 increasingly unlikely (Opens in new window). Pressure below the threshold of war nevertheless continues. On 23 October, Taiwan’s coast guard warned that coordinated Chinese militia and coast guard operations (Opens in new window) were increasing pressure on Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines.
The harder problem is scope. On 27 October, three Chinese warships and a coast guard ship passed together through Japan’s Osumi Strait, the first time Japan’s defence ministry has disclosed (Opens in new window) the two services travelling together through Japanese waters. Further south, the Liaoning carrier group sailed around the Philippines and did not answer Philippine radio challenges (Opens in new window), although Manila said there was no cause for alarm (Opens in new window). By 28 October, Taipei counted 53 Chinese vessels, 34 of them warships (Opens in new window), between southern Japan and the Philippines.
The Liaoning ran a similar loop (Opens in new window) in October 2024. Ship movements alone do not prove coercion. But the US intelligence community did expect Chinese pressure on Japan to intensify (Opens in new window) through 2026, while US–China channels do not directly connect the vessels involved.
A 2024 exercise between the US Coast Guard and Philippine Coast Guard (Elijah Murphy/DVIDS)
Regional channels do exist. Japan and China opened a defence hotline in 2023 (Opens in new window), and Manila and Beijing agreed in 2024 (Opens in new window) to improve maritime communications, including a future coast guard link. In August, The Interpreter reported that the Japan–China hotline had barely been used (Opens in new window) since its first call in May 2023. Manila said in March that amendments to its coast guard agreement were under discussion (Opens in new window). The gap is not an absence of channels but their coverage, reliability and coordination. A US–China memorandum alone cannot establish procedures for Chinese coast guard captains and Philippine or Japanese commanders when their ships meet.
Two further gaps compound the problem. The first is meaning. Xi has defined stability as including competition within proper limits (Opens in new window), and within days of the summit Beijing’s foreign ministry invoked the leaders’ consensus on Taiwan (Opens in new window). A US military official described Washington’s aim as enabling “both strategic stability and deterrence by denial (Opens in new window)”. Washington views allied exercises as credible deterrence; Beijing can portray them as breaching that consensus.
The second is implementation. Nuclear risk offers another test. US and Chinese officials met at least three times this year (Opens in new window) on the margins of the five nuclear powers’ dialogue, with Washington seeking more advance notice of missile tests. The reported meetings establish engagement, but not a shared launch-notification procedure.
The calendar now matters. Trump is expected in Shenzhen (Opens in new window) for APEC on 18–19 November, and Xi in Miami for the G20 on 14–15 December (Opens in new window).
Two indicators deserve attention. The first is operational: whether both governments agree on the memorandum’s purpose and scope, sign it, and use its procedures when an interception goes wrong. The second is whether the PLA’s November–December peak drill season (Opens in new window) passes without a large exercise around Taiwan. Neither would prove the framework caused restraint, but together they would suggest stability is becoming practice rather than language.
The region should also look beyond the bilateral line. Incidents involving coast guards and allies can also escalate. Extending rules for unplanned encounters to coast guards, and linking allied, regional and US–China channels, would do more for stability than another summit communiqué. Without that, the formula will have stabilised the conversation, not the competition. High-level stabilisation will remain incomplete where maritime incidents are most likely to occur.

# AUKUS on track, even ‘ahead of schedule’ for some parts, admiral says

The USS Colorado will serve as the first submarine assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West in support of AUKUS Pillar I.

By [Diana Stancy](https://breakingdefense.com/author/dstancy/) on November 12, 2026 1:12 pm

WASHINGTON — The US, United Kingdom and Australia are on schedule — and even further along than expected in some aspects — in implementing the trilateral [AUKUS agreement](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/aukus-partners-test-autonomous-systems-as-europe-weighs-maritime-surveillance-needs/) established in 2021, the commander of Submarine Forces for the US Pacific Fleet said today.

“The most consequential allied initiative is AUKUS, which is on plan and in several areas ahead of schedule,” Rear Adm. Chris Cavanaugh said during the Submarine League Annual Symposium. “I see progress in AUKUS every day.”

The trilateral deal [comprises Pillar I](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/aukus/), which is focused on providing Australia with Virginia-class nuclear-powered submarines by 2032, [and Pillar II](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/05/aukus-partners-sign-agreement-on-underwater-drones-speed-up-sub-plan/), where the nations are working together to jointly develop and field advanced military capabilities.

It’s not clear which areas of AUKUS are ahead of schedule. However, Cavanaugh pointed to the reactivation of Submarine Squadron 3 in the spring in support of standing up Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) based out of Royal Australian Navy base HMAS Stirling as evidence of progress on the AUKUS deal. Establishing SRF-West is a Pillar I priority enabling the US and the UK to provide a rotational presence of nuclear-powered fast-attack submarines — up to four from the US and one from the UK — at HMAS Stirling.

Further, the three countries announced in October that the US’s Virginia-class submarine Colorado would serve as the first submarine assigned to SRF-West, starting late next year. The vessel arrived in Australia last month as well to complete a “scheduled, monthlong maintenance period” before returning next year to establish SRF-West, [according to the Pentagon](https://www.war.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4635507/navy-submarine-arrives-in-western-australia-for-scheduled-maintenance-period/).

“They’ll return at the end of next year and establish their first rotational force there,” Cavanaugh said. “These aren’t just milestones, we’re really building a capacity and a capability there that’s going to benefit all three of our nations. At the same time, we’re accelerating innovation to expand our undersea advantage.”

Cavanaugh’s comments also come after the US, UK, and Australia concluded a naval exercise off the coast of California dubbed Maritime Big Play, which the UK’s Royal Navy described as the three countries’ “largest ever demonstration of uncrewed and autonomous technology” in support of AUKUS Pillar II. In particular, the Royal Navy said that the drill aimed to capitalize on more than 40 technologies spanning from manned, unmanned, and “multi-domain autonomous” systems” from the three countries.

Additionally, the US Navy said in a news release the exercise’s objective was to “achieve milestones in integrating mature robotics and autonomous systems within AUKUS coalition maritime operations.”

summary: 6 分钟阅读来源：TkKurikawa，Getty Images 中国政府正在通过人工智能驱动的大数据挖掘计划密切关注海外华人。在某些情况下，该计划正在帮助政府设计针对人工智能（AI）行业高层人士的影响力行动。自人工智能热潮开始以来，世界领导人一直在探索如何利用它来巩固自己的权力。虽然华盛顿的重点一直是短期人工智能企业——[追踪移民](https://therevolvingdoorproject.org/tracking-uses-of-ai-in-the-trump-administration/)
content:
6 Min Read

资料来源：TkKurikawa，来自 Getty Images

中国政府正在通过人工智能驱动的大数据挖掘计划密切关注海外华人。在某些情况下，该计划正在帮助政府设计针对人工智能（AI）行业高层人士的影响力行动。

自人工智能热潮开始以来，世界领导人一直在探索如何利用它来巩固自己的权力。虽然华盛顿的重点一直放在短期人工智能项目上——[追踪移民](https://therevolvingdoorproject.org/tracking-uses-of-ai-in-the-trump-administration/)和政治抗议者、确定要削减的社会服务等——但中国共产党(CCP)一直在建设更持久的东西：一个数据中心，促进从社交媒体和其他公共来源进行大规模网络抓取，将结果输入机器学习算法，并输出可操作的结果北京官员的情报。
这是根据泄露给中国监管机构 NetAskari 的文件得出的。在与 Dark Reading 和 Sky News UK 分享的[报告](https://netasari.substack.com/p/ef03ebf1-9615-4422-97c8-86183629af60?postPreview=paid&updated=2026-11-08T09:30:29.111Z&audience=only_paid&free_preview=false&freemail=)中在该出版物中，NetAskari 详细介绍了一项在直接的政府公关与令人讨厌的监视之间取得平衡的计划。有时，数据收集是围绕[剑桥分析风格](https://www.darkreading.com/cybersecurity-analytics/how-to-access-the-voter-information-dirt-cambridge-analytica-has-on-you)有针对性的宣传活动而设计的。在更邪恶的情况下，它被用来识别政治和[经济利益领域](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/4-chinese-apts-taiwan-semiconductor-industry)中的个人，他们有一天可能成为间谍活动中的好间谍或不知情的资产。

相关：[恶意Linux植入模仿亚洲邮件安全产品](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/malicious-linux-implants-mimic-asian-mail-security)
NetAskari 分析师在接受 Dark Reading over Signal 采访时解释道：“一个具有相当不民主倾向的外国正在开展广泛的人工智能分析和信息抓取操作，以寻找影响其他国家内部社会、经济和政治格局的方法。” “这个系统特别针对海外华人，看看是否可以利用[外国公民]来实现这些雄心，即使他们可能没有意识到这一点，这是相当令人震惊的。”

## 中国密谋针对芯片行业的重要人物

11 月 8 日，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋——世界上最重要行业中为数不多的最重要人物之一——给他的员工发了电子邮件，承认与一名新被揭露的间谍有染。国家安全部 (MSS) 特工爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 将 Nvidia 半导体转移到中国，在那里它们被禁止，并将首席执行官的情报转交给中共。

在国安部领导黄的同时，统战部 (UFWD) 采取了自己的、不那么引人注目的方法来应对破坏台湾[半导体行业](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/semiconductor-cybersecurity-tsmc-semi-consortium/753133/)的挑战。

据 NetAskari 报道，UFWD 的主要游戏是在国内外的[影响力行动](https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerability-threats/bundestag-bungle-political-microtargeting-of-facebook-users-draws-ire)。其任务包括测量和

【原文 English Original】
6 Min Read

Source: TkKurikawa via Getty Images

The Chinese government is keeping tabs on ethnic Chinese people abroad via an AI-powered Big Data mining program. In some cases, the program is helping the government design influence operations targeting high-ranking individuals in the artificial intelligence (AI) industry.

Since the AI boom began, world leaders have been feeling out how to exploit it to cement their power. While Washington's emphasis has been on shorter-term AI ventures — [tracking immigrants](https://therevolvingdoorproject.org/tracking-uses-of-ai-in-the-trump-administration/) and political protestors, identifying social services to cut, etc. — the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has been building something more durable: a data center that facilitates gargantuan Web scraping from social media and other public sources, feeds the results into machine learning algorithms, and outputs actionable intelligence for the apparatchiks in Beijing.

That's according to documents leaked to China watchdog NetAskari. In a [report](https://netaskari.substack.com/p/ef03ebf1-9615-4422-97c8-86183629af60?postPreview=paid&updated=2026-11-08T09:30:29.111Z&audience=only_paid&free_preview=false&freemail=) shared with Dark Reading and Sky News UK ahead of publication, NetAskari detailed a program that balances straightforward government PR with unsavory surveillance. Sometimes the data gathering has been designed around [Cambridge Analytica-style](https://www.darkreading.com/cybersecurity-analytics/how-to-access-the-voter-information-dirt-cambridge-analytica-has-on-you) targeted propaganda campaigns. In more nefarious cases, it has been used to identify individuals in political and [economic spheres of interest](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/4-chinese-apts-taiwan-semiconductor-industry) who might one day make good spies or unwitting assets in spy campaigns.

Related:[Malicious Linux Implants Mimic Asian Mail Security Products](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/malicious-linux-implants-mimic-asian-mail-security)

"A foreign nation with rather undemocratic tendencies is running an extensive, AI-charged analysis and information-scraping operation to find ways to influence other nations' internal social, economic, and political landscapes," a NetAskari analyst explains in an interview with Dark Reading over Signal. "That this system is particularly aiming at the Chinese diaspora, to see if [foreign citizens] can be used to further these ambitions, even if they might not be aware of it, is rather shocking."

## Chinese Plots Against Chip Industry VIPs

On Nov. 8, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang — one of the few most important people in the most important industry in the world — emailed his staff, admitting to an affair with a newly outed spy. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) agent, Alice Huang, redirected Nvidia semiconductors to China, where they're banned, and translated intelligence from the CEO to the CCP.

While the MSS ran Huang, the United Front Work Department (UFWD) took its own, less dramatic approach to the challenge of breaching Taiwan's [semiconductor industry](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/semiconductor-cybersecurity-tsmc-semi-consortium/753133/).

The UFWD's main game is [influence operations](https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerabilities-threats/bundestag-bungle-political-microtargeting-of-facebook-users-draws-ire), at home and abroad, according to NetAskari. Its mission includes gauging and shaping media narratives about China abroad, engaging Chinese diaspora communities — to their benefit or detriment, depending on the situation — and, in certain cases, attempting to gain influence over powerful or otherwise useful individuals and organizations in China and abroad.

Related:[UAE, Saudi Arabia Face Onslaught of Increasingly Complex Cyberattacks](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/uae-saudi-arabia-face-onslaught-of-increasingly-sophisticated-automated-cyberattacks)

In this instance, the UFWD appears to have been scoping out ethnic Chinese individuals involved in the semiconductor industry. A leaked report titled "Profiles of Ethnic-Chinese Leading Talent in the Chip Field, Their Circle Characteristics, and Work Recommendations" identifies executives of the Taiwanese AI company Skymizer, high-performing students at a top Taiwanese research university, and an AI research center director at Microsoft, among others, as individuals of note. It then details strategies for getting closer to these VIPs, like "leverage non-official organizations — hometown associations, alumni associations, professional societies — for relationship-building and cooperation."

The system used to generate this report is called the "Overseas Chinese Affairs Big Data Platform."

## The Overseas Chinese Affairs Big Data Platform ("Smart Eye")

The platform's brain is a 500-square-meter Big Data laboratory at Jinan University in Guangzhou, built to comfortably house rows of server racks and at least 100 employees.

Related:[Cybercriminals Hack Brazilian Government Servers to Host Phishing Sites](https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/cybercriminals-hack-brazilian-government-servers-host-phishing-sites)

Basically, it's built to ingest massive amounts of online information about overseas Chinese communities, identify people, relationships, and public sentiments, and convert it all into actionable reports for CCP leadership, according to NetAskari.

Social media provides much of the content. The platform scrapes liberally from platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and X, plus Chinese platforms like Weibo and WeChat. As a rule, the actual scrapers are run on machines located in foreign countries. As with Chinese hacking campaigns more broadly, the machines doing the crimes are also shielded behind [rotating proxy networks](https://www.darkreading.com/cybersecurity-operations/chinese-orb-networks-conceal-apts-make-tracking-iocs-irrelevant). The goal of this obfuscation, one leaked document explains, is to “ensure the security of data collection and prevent the collection system from being traced and discovered" by targeted platforms.

The data then makes its way to China for processing. Foreign languages are translated into Chinese, keywords are extracted, and meaningful links are drawn. UFWD then cross-references these data with preexisting records of notable people identified as being involved in the media, sciences, politics, etc., as well as blacklisted and "two-faced people." These two sources feed a "business system" — the layer that seems to draw meaningful connections about public sentiments, the results of influence operations, and more.

Sometimes, the final reports outputted by this multitiered system simply concern public relations trends. Sometimes they've been used to identify ethnic Chinese individuals of note around the world — be they Taiwanese engineers, social media influencers, or something in between — and unearth strategies for how to utilize them to further the ends of the Chinese Communist Party.

## Using AI to Expand CCP Influence

Overall, the NetAskari analyst describes the Overseas Chinese Affairs Big Data Platform as "a worldwide dragnet that uses open source intelligence (OSINT) and Big Data analysis to identify and find potential collaborators, partners, and affiliates that the UFWD can work with to further their goal [of] extending the Communist Party's influence abroad and creating a 'China-friendly' environment in other nations' political, economic, and social settings."

It's nothing the UFWD wasn't doing before, to be sure. Instead, the analyst adds, "What used to be done manually, at a much slower speed, is now supercharged via AI and modern technology."

That, ultimately, is the rub. The leaked documents contain only outdated references, from 2021, about how machine learning (ML) and [natural language processing](https://www.techtarget.com/news/What-is-natural-language-processing-NLP/834259/) (NLP) algorithms fit into this picture. It's unclear whether, and how, more modern large language models have been incorporated into — and potentially supercharged — the system. The better the AI gets, the more wide-ranging and granular the Overseas Chinese Affairs Big Data Platform can become, with real consequences for people who may not know they are being targeted by a foreign nation.

"A surveillance state can't accept that its own citizens are escaping to other nations, outside the reach of Beijing's grasp. For the best part of the last 20 years, most people had the luxury to ignore this part of the Chinese state. Often practical and physical limitations restricted Chinese organiations to expand too quickly abroad or even get a foothold. But with remote methods like the ones we have seen applied in the Big-Data center of Jinan University, these 'natural boundaries' don't apply anymore," the analyst laments.

"Pair it now with ever-growing globalization, China's stepping out onto the world stage, and crises of democracy in many Western nations, and it is not hard to see why such operations should concern even average citizens in the US or Europe," he says. "Even if they have no personal ties to China."

## About the Author

[![Image 2: Nate Nelson](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blt8edb70f1c73f8a5a/6978c3c26fdea754c9f2e2e9/Nate_Nelson_bio_pic_2-crop_2.jpg?width=400&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale)](https://www.darkreading.com/author/nate-nelson)

Contributing Writer

Nate Nelson is a journalist and award-winning scriptwriter. In addition to Dark Reading he writes for Darknet Diaries, the most popular show in cybersecurity across all media.

He began his career as a freelancer, ghostwriting Forbes and CNBC op-eds for executives in tech and finance. Then he transitioned to journalism at Threatpost, where he covered cybersecurity news and trends. Throughout those years he co-created a cybersecurity podcast, Malicious Life, which in its day climbed into the Top 20 technology podcasts charts on Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

He holds degrees from New York University and Bard College. As a born and bred New Yorker, he enjoys a superiority complex, but is polite enough to keep it to himself.

|谈到日本，中国很难想清楚
谈到日本，中国很难想清楚
自日本首相高市早苗于 2025 年 11 月承认对台湾使用武力“可能对日本构成威胁生存的局面”以来，中日关系已陷入深度冻结一年多，这种言辞暗示日本将进行军事干预。
中国迅速做出反应，发起猛烈批评，甚至声称（在新窗口中打开）日本计划重返1930年代的军国主义并重新殖民台湾。北京和东京之间的政治接触、文化联系、旅游和贸易（包括中国出口的稀土磁铁和具有潜在军事用途的物品）都被中断。
中国没有表现出软化立场的迹象。 2026年11月6日，外交部发言人再次要求日方“纠正在台湾问题上的错误言行，在历史问题上采取正确态度，形成客观理性的对华认知”。
日本首相高市早苗于 2025 年 11 月承认，对台湾使用武力“可能对日本构成生存威胁” (@takaichi_sanae/X)
从某种程度上来说，高一的言论并不出奇，尽管比日本领导人通常更坦率。美国政界人士也曾说过类似的话。但当谈到日本时，中国却很难思考清楚。其反应的强度可以用几个因素来解释：
高市是一位新领导人（当时上任不到三周），女性，具有鹰派声誉。北京希望尽早确立主导地位，并在可能的情况下迫使其让步。
当谈到台湾时，日本引起了特别的敏感。 1895年清朝被日本击败，割让台湾成为日本殖民地。
动荡的中美关系最近趋于稳定，为北京惩罚东京提供了较低风险的环境。
北京反对并希望削弱日本目前增加国防开支和增强自身能力的努力（回应中国自身的大规模军备建设）。
日本并没有做出任何让步。东京冷静地坚守立场，同时为对话敞开大门。
中国没有表现出继续前进的兴趣。它长期以来一直将日本1930年代侵略的遗产作为双边压力点，利用东京在承认其过去方面的尴尬，并敦促韩国和现在的俄罗斯等其他国家加入。
中国的宣传机器在回音室中运作。它擅长针对受害者，但不适合自我意识或自我纠正。关于军国主义死灰复燃的言论已经结束

|When it comes to Japan, China finds it hard to think straight
When it comes to Japan, China finds it hard to think straight
China–Japan ties have been in deep freeze for more than a year now since Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi acknowledged (Opens in new window) in November 2025 that the use of force against Taiwan “could constitute a survival-threatening situation” for Japan, a form of words implying Japan would intervene militarily.
China reacted quickly, launching a campaign of vehement criticism, even claiming (Opens in new window) Japan was planning to return to the militarism of the 1930s and recolonise Taiwan. Political contact between Beijing and Tokyo was disrupted, as were cultural ties, tourism and trade, including Chinese exports of rare earth magnets and items with potential military uses.
China shows no sign of softening its position. On 6 November 2026, its Foreign Ministry spokesperson reiterated (Opens in new window) demands that Japan “correct the erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question, adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China”.
Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi acknowledged in November 2025 that the use of force against Taiwan “could constitute a survival-threatening situation” for Japan (@takaichi_sanae/X)
On one level, what Takaichi said was unremarkable, albeit more candid than is usual for a Japanese leader. US politicians have said similar things. But China has difficulty thinking straight when it comes to Japan. The intensity of its reaction can be explained by several factors:
Takaichi was a new leader (in office less than three weeks at the time), female, with a hawkish reputation. Beijing wanted to establish early dominance and, if possible, force a backdown.
Japan arouses particular sensitivities when it comes to Taiwan. It was the Qing Dynasty’s defeat by Japan in 1895 that ceded Taiwan to become a Japanese colony.
The volatile China–US relationship had recently stabilised, providing a lower risk environment in which Beijing could punish Tokyo.
Beijing opposes and hopes to weaken Japan’s current efforts (responding to China’s own massive military buildup) to increase defence spending and enhance its own capabilities.
No Japanese backdown has materialised. Tokyo has calmly stood its ground, while leaving open the door for dialogue.
China shows no interest in moving on. It has long sustained the legacy of Japan’s 1930s aggression as a bilateral pressure point, exploiting Tokyo’s awkwardness in acknowledging its past, and prodding South Korea and now others, like Russia, to join in.
China’s propaganda machinery operates in an echo chamber. It is adept at targeting a victim, but not suited to self-awareness or self-correction. Its rhetoric about resurgent militarism is overblown and ridiculous. The Japanese leaders who ought to have done more in facing up to the past have long since departed. It is futile to expect their successors to go any further, especially when their accusers hint at revenge while concealing their own more contemporary atrocities.
Beijing may have decided to wait Takaichi out. This is not without risk: while Japanese prime ministers usually turn over within two years, there are exceptions, notably Shinzo Abe, whose policy and ideological mantle Takaichi has inherited. Who is to say that Beijing’s pressure campaign will not serve to strengthen her politically? In the meantime, with a weakened US administration, Beijing would better win over this important neighbour, rather than humiliate it.
The upcoming regional summits – East Asia (16–17 November), APEC (18–19 November) and G20 (14–15 December) – offer potential for an initial rapprochement between leaders. The East Asia Summit might be more likely, since China is represented there by its premier, rather than its president, allowing President Xi Jinping to keep his distance from a potentially unproductive encounter. Otherwise, no immediate circuit-breaker is in sight.
A highway without off-ramps is no better than a cul-de-sac.
Words matter. Just because something is true does not mean it needs to be said, especially by a national leader. There are less damaging ways for Tokyo to convey to Beijing its determination regarding security in its immediate region. Takaichi’s explicitness was unnecessary and an unforced misstep.
A highway without off-ramps is no better than a cul-de-sac. Beijing’s hardline rhetoric may play well domestically, but its intransigence seems to rule out the kind of accommodation it claims to seek with Japan. Backdowns are difficult for any government, especially in a democracy. Japan–China ties look set to remain permanently prickly.
Graham Fletcher is Senior Fellow for East Asia at the Lowy Institute and a former Australian Ambassador to China.

title: Shen, Chiang lay out transportation, urban renewal plans for Taipei

summary: 沉蒋制定台北交通、市区更新计划 - 聚焦台湾2026选举/沉蒋制定台北交通、市区更新计划 要启动文字转语音服务，请先同意以下隐私政策。民进党台北市长候选人沉彪马（右）与国民党现任市长蒋万安（左）。中新社台北11月14日电 (中新社)民进党台北市市长候选人沈伯洋与国民党现任议员蒋万安在电视上阐述首都交通及城市更新计划
content:
沉蒋制定台北交通及城市更新计划 - 聚焦台湾
2026年选举/沉蒋制定台北交通及市区更新计划
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
民进党台北市长候选人沉彪马（右）与国民党现任市长蒋万安（左）。 CNA 合成照片
中新社台北11月14日电 民进党台北市市长候选人沉伯洋和国民党现任市长蒋万安周六在电视政策发布会上阐述了首都交通和城市更新计划。
为了缓解台北的交通拥堵，沉建议将电动 YouBikes 纳入 T-Pass 计划，该计划提供无限次乘坐公共交通的服务，每月费用为新台币 1,200 元（36.48 美元）。
沉说，这些自行车可以帮助居民完成最后一段通勤，节省他们从地铁站步行到目的地的时间，并鼓励更多地使用公共交通。
沉还建议更好地整合现有的自行车道，并在基隆河上建设两座“自行车桥”，以扩大台北现有自行车道网络的覆盖范围，并鼓励更多人使用该市的自行车共享计划。
民进党台北市长候选人沉彪马在周六的电视政策演讲后向媒体发表讲话。中央通讯社照片2026年11月14日
此外，沉表示，他将探索将目前非电动YouBikes提供的30分钟免费乘车时间延长至电动车型的可能性，在前两个小时内，用户每30分钟需花费20新台币。
与此同时，蒋提出了新台币399元的月票，让台北和新北居民无限次乘坐公交车，并表示这将解决公交车通勤计划的缺点，使约30万人受益。
谈到住房和台北大量的老化住宅，沉建议成立一个“旧楼延寿”小组，让居民轻松获得有关其房屋的信息，包括地震安全系数、管道是否需要更换、建筑物符合哪些无障碍设施以及屋顶如何美化等。
对于陷入停滞的城市更新项目，沉提出了他所谓的“无限城市更新”倡议，根据该倡议，市政府将在计划更新的老化建筑附近的政府拥有的土地上建造一座新建筑，并将其居住者搬迁到那里，实质上是用新房换旧房。
沉说，根据该提案，政府将接管旧房产的所有权，从而赋予其更大的杠杆作用来加速城市更新项目。它还可以将这些单位出租给新父母、年轻人或在科技行业工作的居民，同时努力与坚持住的住户就项目细节达成协议。
与此同时，蒋介石表示，自他上任以来，启动城市更新项目的门槛已从至少90%的业主降低到75%。
周六，台北市市长蒋万安在电视上发表政策演讲后。中央通讯社照片2026年11月14日
为了进一步加速城市更新，蒋表示，他打算将门槛降低至50%，让市政府主动主导潜在项目，解释业主权益，并促进讨论

2026 ELECTIONS/Shen, Chiang lay out transportation, urban renewal plans for Taipei
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (right) and incumbent Chiang Wan-an (left) of the KMT. CNA composite photo
Taipei, Nov. 14 (CNA) Democratic Progressive Party Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) and incumbent Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) of the Kuomintang (KMT) laid out their transportation and urban renewal plans for the capital at a televised policy presentation Saturday.
To alleviate traffic congestion in Taipei, Shen proposed integrating electric YouBikes into the T-Pass program, which offers unlimited rides on public transportation for a monthly fee of NT$1,200 (US$36.48).
The bikes, Shen said, could help residents cover the last stretch of their commutes, saving them the walk from metro stations to their destinations and encouraging greater use of public transportation.
Shen also proposed better integrating existing bicycle trails and building two "bicycle bridges" across the Keelung River to extend the reach of Taipei's current bicycle trail network and encourage more people to use the city's bikeshare program.
DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen speaks to the press after a televised policy presentation on Saturday. CNA photo Nov. 14, 2026
In addition, Shen said he would explore the possibility of extending the 30 minutes of free rides currently offered on non-electric YouBikes to electric models, which cost users NT$20 for every 30 minutes during the first two hours.
Chiang, meanwhile, proposed a NT$399 monthly pass offering Taipei and New Taipei residents unlimited bus rides, saying this would address the shortcomings of the T-Pass program for bus commuters and benefit about 300,000 people.
Turning to housing and Taipei's large number of aging residential buildings, in particular, Shen proposed forming an "old building life extension" team to give residents easy access to information about their homes, including seismic safety coefficients, whether pipelines need replacing, what barrier-free facilities their buildings are eligible for, and how their rooftops could be beautified.
For stalled urban renewal projects, Shen proposed what he called the "infinite urban renewal" initiative, under which the city government would build a new building on government-owned land near an aging building slated for renewal and relocate its occupants there, essentially exchanging new homes for aging ones.
Under the proposal, Shen said, the government would take over ownership of the old properties, giving it greater leverage to accelerate urban renewal projects. It could also rent out the units to new parents, young people or residents working in the technology sector while working to reach agreements with holdout occupants on the details of the projects.
Chiang, meanwhile, said that since he took office, the threshold for initiating an urban renewal project had been lowered from at least 90 percent of property owners to 75 percent.
Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an after a televised policy presentation on Saturday. CNA photo Nov. 14, 2026
To further accelerate urban renewal, Chiang said he intended to lower the threshold to 50 percent, allowing the city government to take the initiative in leading potential projects, explaining property owners' rights and benefits, and facilitating discussions among homeowners once half of them had agreed to proceed with urban renewal.
Chiang said his administration was also working on a "large-block urban renewal" initiative targeting sites of more than 3,000 square meters near waterfront areas and metro stations.
Under the initiative, the base floor area ratio would be increased from 225 percent to 300 percent, providing greater incentives for residents and allowing them to receive a larger share of the redeveloped properties, he said.
Chiang, Shen ramp up campaigns ahead of local elections
Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) and his Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) challenger Puma Shen (沈伯洋) stepped up their campaigns Saturday, with Chiang staging a large-scale rally and march and Shen organizing a music festival ahead of Nov. 28's local elections.
KMT, DPP candidates for Kaohsiung mayor court voters at TV forum
The Kuomintang (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) candidates for Kaohsiung mayor clashed over city funding at a televised policy forum Saturday, even as both pledged to carry on parts of outgoing Mayor Chen Chi-mai's (陳其邁) agenda.
New Taipei mayoral candidates Lee, Su outline visions at policy forum
New Taipei mayoral candidates Lee Shu-chuan (李四川) and Su Chiao-hui (蘇巧慧) outlined contrasting visions for the city Friday, with Lee pledging to carry on major infrastructure projects and Su calling for more balanced development across its districts.

November 18, 2026, and November 19, 2026.

content:
從黑海到台海：烏克蘭智庫首度為台灣提出防衛藍圖，實戰經驗能複製嗎？ - 報導者 The Reporter
烏克蘭智庫 「塞爾彭斯國際安全中心」（SCIS）2026年10月發布《台灣的黑海戰略藍圖：烏克蘭海軍非對稱作戰的啟示》，報告包含以台灣兩個攻擊無人艇「快奇」與「奮進魔鬼魚號」，跟烏克蘭的「海寶貝」（Sea Baby）與「MAGURA V5」進行比較。圖為2025年10月17日，烏克蘭安全局展示的多用途無人艇「海寶貝」。（攝影／Kyrylo Chubotin／Ukrinform／NurPhoto via Getty Images）
10月19日，烏克蘭的獨立安全智庫 「塞爾彭斯國際安全中心」（Serpens Center for International Security, SCIS），首次發布以台灣為主的報告：《台灣的黑海戰略藍圖：烏克蘭海軍非對稱作戰的啟示》（The Black Sea Blueprint for Taiwan: Ukraine's Naval Lessons in Asymmetric Warfare）。這是他們首次將烏克蘭的無人艇經驗，應用在他們不熟悉、條件大相逕庭，但全球關注潛在戰爭風險的台灣海峽。
報告封面放著台灣，43頁的研究內容，從無人艇採購的數量、部署、操作員訓練，到戰時生產鏈的自給與移轉；SCIS也針對台灣海峽的氣候、水文、海象等條件，以及台灣在國際政治外交面臨的限制和可能性，提出在不對稱作戰上應用的建議。
自2022年俄羅斯全面入侵烏克蘭以來，國際上不乏比較烏克蘭與台灣局勢的學術報告與媒體報導，但因烏克蘭在外交上仍持「一中政策」，加上烏克蘭無人機產業鏈的關鍵零件命脈受中國把持，即便是獨立智庫等非官方單位進行交流合作，兩國間也相當謹慎。
烏克蘭付出極大代價換來的近5年實戰經驗，SCIS智庫的深入研究，是否有被台灣借鏡的可能？
塞爾彭斯國際安全中心（Serpens Center for International Security）前身為蛇島研究所（Snake Island Institute）。2022年俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭期間，位在黑海的蛇島一度遭俄軍攻占，幾個月內烏克蘭重新控制該島，史稱蛇島戰役；研究所也以此命名，專注在黑海的安全研究。
共同創辦人布查茨基（Catarina Buchatskiy）在《台灣的黑海戰略藍圖》的報告開頭寫下：
「今天烏克蘭的作戰能力已與4年前截然不同。烏克蘭在全球安全架構中的定位已從（戰場上的）受援者轉為貢獻者⋯⋯這份報告是我們烏克蘭作為安全知識與策略輸出國的初步嘗試。」
2023年，布查茨基與另一位專家赫里岑科（Maryna Hrytsenko）共同創立了SCIS。布查茨基曾在美國胡佛研究所（Hoover Institution）從事無人機戰爭的研究，擔任過基輔經濟學院（Kyiv School of Economics）的資深國防創新總監；赫里岑科則曾擔任烏克蘭國會的國家安全顧問，頻繁從事外交遊說。SCIS成立後，特別專注在烏克蘭的不對稱作戰、無人載具的供應鏈和黑海的戰略研究。
兩人的背景讓SCIS在短短幾年內得到國內外智庫、媒體與多國政府的關注。起初，SCIS並沒有特別想研究烏克蘭以外的地區，但當國際戰場不斷延伸，美國的外交政策不斷轉變，他們也重新思考自己的定位。
「光只研究烏克蘭戰場或俄羅斯是不夠的，」布查茨基說，長期以來烏克蘭依賴美國提供軍事援助，而現任美國總統川普（Donald Trump）的態度經常變化，烏克蘭必須了解美國在外交上的決策，「美國高度關注台海議題，自然成了我們的第一步。因為美國的決策，也會進一步影響到烏克蘭的安全。」
SCIS在報告中特別強調，團隊並非印太地區的專家，無意對台海具體走向做出任何預測，但希望將這幾年烏克蘭第一線的實戰經驗、無人載具產業從無到有的發展過程，提供給台灣參考。
「我們試圖傳達的是，對美國各地現在或是未來可能的戰場，包括亞太區、台灣，烏克蘭戰場上的科技和知識應用，都是非常重要的關鍵，」布查茨基説。
烏克蘭智庫塞爾彭斯國際安全中心（SCIS）2026年10月發布的《台灣的黑海戰略藍圖》，訪談了烏克蘭無人水面艇的操作人員、製造商還有特種部隊，報告也參考了大量公開資料，例如美國權威智庫蘭德公司（RAND Corporation）關於解放軍海上及兵力部署的研究、美國海軍戰爭學院「海上戰略中心」（Center for Maritime Strategy）的相關報告，以及分析美國的戰略暨國際研究中心（CSIS）在2023年針對台海衝突的兵棋推演。
報告主要有4位撰寫者、4位編輯，其中兩位有美國退役海軍背景──包含海軍少將歐康納（Cathal O'Connor），曾擔任第三遠征打擊部隊指揮官和第11兩棲中隊指揮官，具有豐富的西太平洋及兩棲作戰經驗。
2026年6月，他們的分析員也來到台灣，參加由國家智庫「科技、民主與社會研究中心」（DSET）所舉辦的2026供應鏈韌性戰略國際高峰會，了解台灣無人載具產業面上的機會和困境。
2026年11月4日，於台南市舉辦的MATURE Taiwan DSET 最新報告〈打造台灣無人艇艦隊：台灣無人艇產業發展、國際合作與烏克蘭啟示〉發表會。（攝影／黃政嘉）
《台灣的黑海戰略藍圖》首先分析烏克蘭在黑海成功與失敗的經驗，接著將台海周邊水文海象、解放軍可能的登陸點列出，也針對台灣目前兩個攻擊無人艇的型號「快奇」（NCSIST Kuai Chi）與「奮進魔鬼魚號」（Endeavor Manta），跟烏克蘭的「海寶貝」（Sea Baby）與「MAGURA V5」進行比較。
烏克蘭第一艘無人艇原型，是從2022年5月，一位工程師改裝的一艘漁船開始。
在幾次的測試與改裝後，同年10月29日，烏克蘭以7艘無人艇搭配9艘無人機，聯合攻擊俄羅斯黑海艦隊，部分突破港口防線，破壞至少一艘俄羅斯的掃雷艦。
儘管該次行動並未擊沉任何俄軍軍艦，卻成為烏克蘭發展無人艇技術與戰術的重要里程碑。到2024年，他們已能用造價約27萬美元（約新台幣885萬元）的無人艇，擊沉價值6,000萬至7,000萬美元（約新台幣19.7億至22.9億元）的俄羅斯軍艦。
烏克蘭證明即使缺乏傳統海軍，仍能透過小型無人載具，在黑海上威脅世界海軍第三強的俄羅斯，以低成本、可消耗的不對稱作戰戰略，快速更新技術與戰術，在5年內完成多次的成功襲擊。
「無人船」與「無人艇」在中文使用上並無嚴格統一的尺寸界線，一般而言，「無人船」涵蓋的船舶類型較廣，「無人艇」則多用於指稱體積較小、機動性較高的水面載具。兩者在軍事應用上通常都屬於無人水面載具（Unmanned Surface Vehicle, USV），可透過遠端遙控或自主航行執行任務。
本文討論的烏克蘭海上攻擊載具，主要以「無人艇」稱之；另也保留受訪者使用「無人船」的用詞。
，是可以達到不對稱作戰的效益，」台灣科技、民主與社會研究中心（DSET）政策分析師方怡然指出。
方怡然表示，烏克蘭的不對稱作戰，阻止敵方自由使用特定海域，是一個台灣值得好好學習的案例。DSET也在11月2日，從台灣的角度，發表相似題目的研究。
烏克蘭的報告，首先提出兩邊戰場情境本質上的差異。第一，最大的差別，就是烏克蘭與多個國家陸路接壤，在開戰以後，還可以從其他國家獲得資源；但台灣是一座島嶼，物資設備無法自由進出，戰前的儲備就變得格外重要。
第二，兩邊的海象和氣候有極大的不同。黑海相對平靜，大多數成功的無人艇作戰行動，都發生在波高低於2公尺的海況下；但台灣海峽的作業環境遠比黑海嚴苛，全年大部分時間浪高更大，季節性季風與強勁洋流持續存在，適宜作業的天氣窗口
原文為Weather Window，常用於離岸風電、海上鑽探、船隻航行或高空工程中，指一段適合執行特定戶外或海上作業的「黃金時間段」，牽涉到風速與風向、波浪資訊、海流與潮汐及許多天氣條件的預報。
第三，則是敵人的實力。報告提到，俄羅斯基本上沒有發展自己的無人艇。但中國則是世界海軍第二強，解放軍的艦隊，也是特別針對跨海作戰所設計，包括兩棲攻擊艦、船塢登陸船等。此外，解放軍也有可能學習烏克蘭的經驗，使用無人艇作為攻擊。
2026年11月2日，台灣海洋科技暨無人載具展在台南安平港實機演示，圖為美國公司STR8 Industries開發的「幽靈尾跡」（Ghostwake）。（攝影／馬雨辰）
根據這些差異，報告提出幾大重點。第一是台灣海峽的惡劣氣候，時常被判定是一項劣勢，但多位烏克蘭第一線的無人艇操作員表示，惡劣氣候反而是無人艇的絕佳掩蔽，能幫助避開敵人的攻擊，也提升中國解放軍登陸的挑戰；第二是無人艇的放置與部署，以及在戰爭情況下，台灣作為孤立的島嶼，如何讓生產線具有轉移與調度的韌性。
第三，報告建議台灣需要快速工業化無人艇的生產，才能撐起有效的不對稱作戰，抵抗解放軍的大型傳統軍艦。
「其中最讓我擔心的，就是台灣無人艇的生產能力，」布查茨基説。她解釋，不對稱作戰重點，是以低成本的無人艇攻擊高成本的敵人傳統軍艦。台灣的情況，重點不在擊沉，而是打亂對手的節奏，爭取更多友軍來支援的時間。根據報告分析，烏克蘭在黑海發動一次攻擊，時常需要投入10艘無人艇，有時更多，這還不包括搭載其他無人機等的平台。
即便如此，每一次攻擊也不代表作戰成功，50%的耗損率都是可接受的範圍。中國解放軍的軍艦，預計擁有比俄羅斯更成熟的性能，並有強大且多層次的防禦體系──這表示台灣的作戰可能會比烏克蘭在黑海作戰時，承受更高的耗損率。報告計算，根據美國智庫戰略暨國際研究中心（CSIS）2023年的兵推，解放軍可能損失113～138艘軍艦，台灣若要採「以量換質」策略達成此戰術目的，可能需部署約5,000艘無人艇。
台灣近年借鏡烏克蘭的經驗，持續擴大海上無人系統的研發與採購。目前國防部提出1,320艘小型單程攻擊無人艇的採購需求，但還未正式招標；加上台灣的政治文化影響預算與執行，都可能導致採購時程拖延，或是與昂貴的傳統載台競爭經費，這些都是布查茨基擔心的原因。
但布查茨基擔心的這一點，也是台灣安全專家意見分歧最大的一點。
方怡然表示，台海與黑海情況相差很多，很難直接推算台灣所需的無人艇數量；另外，短時間大量生產，無人艇的存放位置和方式也是挑戰；再加上局勢變動與科技發展速度之快，軟體系統可能很快過時。所以台灣目前是採每年漸進式採購，而非一次到位。
另一種方式，則是先造好船殼，「像是做麵包時先做好麵糰一樣，」等到真的危機爆發時，業者可以在短時間內，加裝新的軟體，來因應當前局勢。方怡然認為，台灣在生產能力上，船殼設計與製造是完全沒問題，像是台灣國際造船（簡稱台船）、龍德造船等，都有多年的造船經驗。另一方面，通訊、導航、感測、自動避障系統等的技術整合，是台灣正在努力追趕的部分；即使開發這些系統，也需要不斷做測試更新，台灣的無人系統才有辦法達到AI自主。
目前台灣的做法，是與國外廠商合作軟體的開發。所以像台船就在今年與美國自主系統公司Havoc宣布建立合作夥伴關係；中山科學研究院（簡稱中科院）目前也已經與3家美國水面／水下無人載具廠商
即為MARTAC、Saronic和Anduril。
簽訂合作備忘錄，合作的部分像是在感測通訊、AI自主系統等的整合。
「這部分台灣有沒有辦法盡快達成AI自主，還是一個未知數，」方怡然坦承。
另外淡江大學國際事務與戰略研究所副教授林穎佑則提出，報告中較少著墨的人員培訓細節。
「就像買了一台車，你也要有人懂得怎麼開車，開車技術如何，」林穎佑表示，當無人艇生產到一定的數量，也要有足夠的無人艇操作員訓練場，但目前這在台灣的討論仍然不多。
布查茨基也承認這點的重要性。她建議台灣能盡快確定採用的平台，並將其納入訓練體系，因為關鍵在於人員能否正確使用這些技術。烏克蘭的做法是，派遣操作人員接受為期數週甚至數月的培訓，訓練出一支很強的隊伍，並且給予他們能發令部署的權限，讓他們能夠充分利用這些系統。烏克蘭之所以能取得顯著成效，很大程度是因為像這樣的「去中心化」運作模式。
她也強調，這些系統操作起來非常直觀，跟打電動很像，人們很快就能掌握基本操作邏輯。
2025年8月14日，烏克蘭國防部情報總局帖木兒特種部隊的成員前往位於黑海的蛇島執行任務。（攝影／Roman Pilipey／AFP）
台灣的軍事專家也強調，雖然黑海與台海條件迥異，烏克蘭在黑海的實戰經驗，有幾點仍能給台灣非常重要的啟發。
第一個是快速迭代。這裡指的是，烏克蘭已經建立出一套從前線士兵到後勤產業之間，有效率的回饋機制。他們開發一套高度整合的戰場管理系統，統整烏克蘭不同作戰單位的情資，即時掌握敵軍位置、部隊動向與防區邊界，整合陸海空等多領域數據，讓指揮官可直接以這個平台分配任務，也讓產業端能即時了解前線的需求。
第二點，是烏克蘭多功能運用無人艇。除了直接攻擊，烏克蘭的無人艇也有運輸、監測、反水雷等功能。一艘無人艇，也可以搭載無人機，或是無人地面載具運輸等不同的載台。
「像樂高一樣組合起來，面對不同的作戰需求，這是我覺得烏克蘭最棒的經驗，台灣必須要學習的部分，」方怡然說。國防安全研究院（INDSR）國防戰略與資源研究所所長蘇紫雲也認同，烏克蘭在戰場上快速的反制能力，是值得學習之處。例如，據烏克蘭軍事情報部門所稱，2024年，他們在一艘無人艇上配載導彈，創下首次無人艇在黑海擊落直升機的紀錄。
第三點，不論是台灣還是烏克蘭，仍然強調持久戰。方怡然解釋，無人艇不是光數量達到就好，很重要的是要思考：無人艇放哪裡、怎麼放？以及如何面對做好後卻已經過時、不符合戰場的需求？她建議，台灣要開始盤點無人艇產業的地圖，比如說哪些公司，是可以在戰時轉換做無人艇的零件，才能在危機爆發時，具有產業鏈快速轉移與調整的韌性。無人機產業目前已知全台有267家相關廠商，相較之下，無人艇的供應鏈，盤點還沒有很明確。
除了實務上可能的對照，台灣的專家也表示，這篇報告的刊出本身就具有代表性。
蘇紫雲在看完報告之後向《報導者》表示：「他們把黑海無人船使用成功的經驗，投射到台灣海峽，反映出歐洲、特別是烏克蘭，開始認知到中國跟俄羅斯這種極權國家是真正的威脅。即使烏克蘭可能還會擔心中國持續支援俄羅斯，仍然選擇發布這份報告，展現出民主國家之間共同的安全意志。」
2026年11月2日，副總統蕭美琴於台南市安平港參觀2026台灣海洋科技暨無人載具展。（攝影／馬雨辰）
這份報告的重點，也反映出烏克蘭期待與台灣、亞太盟友有更多的合作。但布查茨基同樣理解，台灣與烏克蘭的關係確實很複雜。
「作為獨立的智庫，我們了解到，有許多台灣方想要幫助烏克蘭，想要跟烏克蘭夥伴有更多的合作；我們看見台灣的（無人載具）產業，非常積極想要在烏克蘭無人機與零件的生產鏈上，成為中國的替代方案。但我們也理解，任何可能在政治上被解讀的選邊站，對烏克蘭政府還有前線作戰都會有很大的影響。所以烏克蘭還是要維持外交上的平衡，」布查茨基説。
她所提到對前線作戰的影響，是直接攸關前線士兵的生存。即使烏克蘭積極將產業在地化，但如馬達、天線、導航晶片、熱感測器、鋰鹽等零件，仍仰賴中國。根據SCIS另一份關於無人機產業鏈的報告，自2022年以來，中國實施關於無人載具的每項出口限制，都直接波及烏克蘭戰場。影響包括零件價格一夜之間翻3倍、關鍵零件短缺，或因此拖延到運送的時間。
雖然中國的出口限制也應包括俄羅斯，但烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskyy）在2025年直接公開指控，中國停止向烏克蘭及其他歐洲國家出售無人機，卻持續供應無人機給俄羅斯。並有證據證實，中國在俄羅斯境內設有無人機零件的生產線。
「烏克蘭的國防工業基礎仍然高度仰賴中國，任何的破壞都會對我們產生重大影響，」布查茨基説。
顧及到台烏複雜的關係，在產業面上，目前台灣主要是透過第三方來與烏克蘭合作，克服政治上的限制。例如無人機，主要透過波蘭、捷克和美國等國的廠商或協會做中介；無人艇的部分，目前主要和美國廠商合作。《報導者》詢問中科院與烏克蘭無人艇廠商的接觸，中科院表示，「與烏國相關合作是屬國與國事項，無權責回覆。」在烏克蘭創立的無人艇製造商U Force，11月初受邀參加「2026台灣海洋科技暨無人載具展」，在台南安平港實機演示，但目前還未與台灣廠商簽訂任何合作備忘錄。
學術方面，布查茨基坦言，即使是非官方組織，她目前也還沒有看到其他烏克蘭的智庫，有如此公開針對黑海與台海之間安全戰略框架做研究。
但作為有別於官方的獨立智庫，布查茨基期待可以打破外交困境，做想做的研究。她也希望告訴台灣的讀者：
「防禦本身代價非常高，面對持續不斷攻擊你的對手，更是能量的消耗，不僅會造成人員傷亡，還會耗費龐大的金錢與資源，這種對抗很快就會在各方面將你拖垮⋯⋯面對實力懸殊很大的敵人，我們透過慘痛的教訓理解到，你必須極為謹慎地規劃有限資源，並且精準地管理預算，在不造成資源耗盡和人力損失的前提下，如何盡可能從一開始就建構有效的防禦力量，至關重要。」「而你也將會看到我們愈來愈多這樣的報告，不論是在印太，還是在西半球，或是非洲大陸，我們會持續地做。因為我們認為，烏克蘭正在經歷的，不只是單純抵抗俄羅斯而已，而是全世界與烏克蘭同盟的國家，都可以從中學到適合他們的經驗。這是我們真正希望做的事。」

title: NATO Is Not the Right Forum to Discuss China
zh_title: 北约不是讨论中国的合适论坛
summary: 北约不是讨论中国的正确论坛——美国外交官在奥列什基的调解再次暴露了中国乌克兰外交的局限性：所罗门群岛的故事 中国的开放式人工智能在肯尼亚遇到了最后一英里的问题 为什么昂山素季仍然是“完美人质” 台北选民二十多年来没有选择独立或统一，孟加拉国的一个不变因素是政治暴力 朝鲜在俄乌战争中的表现 中国的同伴经济：花钱请人陪我玩 印度是在扩大对朝鲜伊斯兰活动的控制
content:
外交官：北约不是讨论中国的合适论坛
美国斡旋奥列什基事件暴露中国乌克兰外交局限性
来来回回：所罗门群岛的故事

20多年来，孟加拉国的一个不变问题就是政治暴力
朝鲜在俄罗斯-乌克兰战争中的局势
中国的陪伴经济：花钱请人陪我玩
印度是否正在扩大对克什米尔伊斯兰教活动的控制？
新法律最终会结束亚洲工厂的侵犯人权行为吗？
美国、澳大利亚、日本、新西兰和韩国的国防部长出席 2026 年 1 月 22 日在比利时布鲁塞尔举行的第 194 届北约军事委员会国防部长会议上的“印度-太平洋伙伴”会议。
中国对北约的看法多年来没有改变。在北京，该联盟被视为冷战的残余，本应在苏联解体后解散，就像华沙条约一样。与俄罗斯一样，中国并不将北约视为防御性联盟，而是威胁全球稳定的进攻性联盟。这方面的例子包括连续的东扩和北约的所谓域外干预。在这方面，北京经常提到北约1999年干预前南斯拉夫期间对中国驻贝尔格莱德大使馆的（意外）轰炸。此外，北京与莫斯科一样认为，北约东扩无视俄罗斯的安全关切，对俄罗斯施加了压力。因此，中国也认为北约应对莫斯科的先发制人的军事行动（例如在乌克兰）负责，这些行动被视为自卫行为。
在中国看来，将中国列入北约议程（首先是2019年，然后是2022年的战略构想）表明该组织正在准备向亚洲扩张，或者有建立“亚洲北约”的计划。因此，在北京眼中，俄罗斯现在扮演着北约与亚太地区之间缓冲区的角色。中国分析人士认为，如果没有这个缓冲，北约就会出现在亚洲，对中国构成严重的安全威胁。
无论北约认为中国对联盟的看法多么奇怪和夸张，该组织都不应该忽视它，并且应该考虑解决中国的担忧。即使中国并不真正相信北约向亚洲扩张，而只是将其作为一种政治工具——例如支持俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争以及表达对西方的负面情绪的借口——北约仍然值得考虑利用其论坛讨论中国是否真的对北约有帮助。
众所周知，将中国列入北约议程的想法源于美国。中国在唐纳德·特朗普担任美国总统的第一个任期内首次在北约框架内被提及并非巧合。众所周知，欧洲盟国过去（现在仍然）不愿意在北约框架内关注中国，主要原因有三个。首先，俄罗斯入侵乌克兰清楚地表明，对联盟构成迫在眉睫的安全威胁的是俄罗斯，而不是中国。
其次，北约以《华盛顿条约》为基础，在该文件规定的地理区域内开展活动。艺术

The chiefs of defense of the United States, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea attend a session on “Partners in the Indo-Pacific” at the 194th NATO Military Committee in Chiefs of Defense session in Brussels, Belgium, Jan. 22, 2026.
China’s view of NATO has not changed for years. In Beijing the alliance is seen as a remnant of the Cold War that should have been dissolved after the collapse of the Soviet Union, in the same way as the Warsaw Pact. Like Russia, China does not see NATO as a defensive alliance but rather as an offensive one that threatens global stability. Examples of this include its successive eastward enlargements, and NATO’s so-called out-of-area interventions. In this regard, Beijing often refers to NATO’s (accidental) bombardment of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade in 1999 during the intervention in the former Yugoslavia. Furthermore, Beijing shares Moscow’s perception that NATO’s enlargements toward the East exert pressure on Russia by ignoring its security concerns. Thus China shares the view that NATO is to blame for Moscow’s preemptive military actions (such as in Ukraine), which are seen as acts of self-defense.
In the Chinese perception the inclusion of China on the NATO agenda – first in 2019 and then in the Strategic Concept in 2022 – suggests that the organization is preparing to expand into Asia, or that there is a plan to establish an “Asian NATO.” Therefore, in Beijing’s eyes, Russia now plays the role of a buffer zone between NATO and the Asia-Pacific region. Without this buffer, Chinese analysts believe, NATO would already be present in Asia, posing a serious security threat to China.
No matter how strange and exaggerated NATO finds the Chinese perspective on the alliance, the organization should not ignore it and should consider addressing Chinese concerns. Even if China does not truly believe in NATO’s expansions to Asia and is merely using this as a political tool – for example, an excuse to support Russia in its war against Ukraine and express its negative feelings toward the West – it would still be worthwhile for NATO to consider whether it is actually helpful for the alliance to use its forum to discuss China.
It is widely known that the idea of putting China on NATO’s agenda originated in the United States. It is no coincidence that China was first mentioned within the NATO framework during Donald Trump’s first term as U.S. president. It is also common knowledge that European allies were (and still are) reluctant to focus on China within the NATO framework for three main reasons. First, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has made it clear that Russia, not China, is an imminent security threat to the alliance.
Second, NATO, which is based on the Washington Treaty, operates within the geographical area specified in the document. Article 6 refers to the “North Atlantic area north of the Tropic of Cancer” as NATO’s area of activities.
Third, China is perceived in Europe as a challenge, or even a threat, but mostly an economic one, rather than a (direct) hard security one, even when its support for Russia is considered. It is also well known that the fact that China is still seen by NATO as a “challenge” rather than a “threat” (see the NATO Strategic Concept wording) is thanks to the European allies who have been trying to curb U.S. demands and reduce China’s importance to the alliance.
I would argue that making China a topic of discussion for NATO would be counterproductive for the alliance. First, it would reinforce or validate Beijing’s real or imagined concerns about the organization expanding into Asia. Even though NATO is geographically restricted, China uses the fact that it is part of the Strategic Concept to highlight that the alliance is expanding toward Asia and poses a real threat to Beijing.
NATO constantly explains that it does not intend to have a presence in Asia because this would contradict the Washington Treaty. The only thing it is considering is exchanging views with the “Indo-Pacific Four” (IP4) and other Asian countries on the security situation in the Asia-Pacific region, with a focus on cyber issues, etc. However, China does not believe this is true.
China also does not accept NATO’s explanation that when U.S., French, British, German, or other vessels conduct freedom of navigation operations (FONOPs) in Asia, they are not NATO ships. These operations are carried out on a country-by-country basis without any “blessing” from NATO. China is eager to exploit these FONOPS as political tools against the West, and it’s easy to do so. Few distinguish between NATO operations and national ships when it is simpler to put them all into the NATO basket. And China just does that.
Finally, discussing China within the context of NATO is a noticeable diversion of attention from the real threat to the alliance – that is Russia.
There are quite a few other formats in which China as a hard security actor could be discussed instead of NATO. The European Union seems to be the best option, when it comes to the European countries, at least. The EU has been discussing China not only in terms of its economic challenges and threats, such as deindustrialization, which could result in job losses and social instability in Europe, but also in terms of hard security. There are many examples of the EU taking a harder stance on China to defend Europe. China poses a hard security threat to Europe due to its support for Russia, resulting in Chinese companies being added to the EU’s sanction packages against Russia, albeit in small numbers. China could also be discussed in both bilateral and multilateral formats such as transatlantic discussions, talks with ASEAN and its members, the G7, and others.
Continuing to discuss China in the NATO format may reinforce Beijing’s negative perception of the organization, significantly reducing the scope for potential cooperation with Beijing in order to mitigate threats to NATO from such China’s political friends as Russia, Iran, and North Korea. Rather than arguing that China poses a challenge to the alliance, it would be better to engage in regular dialogue with Beijing and try to convince China – although this would be no easy task – to soften its negative opinion of NATO. The alliance should emphasize that NATO’s existence benefits China by deterring Russia from starting a war with NATO allies that could be catastrophic for China.

content:
公投重燃台湾“无核祖国”政策争论 - 聚焦台湾
公投重燃台湾“无核祖国”政策争论
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月14日电 一名结束台湾“无核家园”政策的支持者周六表示，重启反应堆可以为可再生能源的发展赢得时间，而一名政府代表则质疑是否有必要进行公投，因为现行法律已经在进行重启评估。
两人在 11 月 28 日公投（恰逢地方选举）之前由中央选举委员会组织的五场电视论坛中的第二场发表了讲话。此次投票询问选民是否支持政府结束“无核家园”能源政策，利用核电振兴经济。
中华经济研究院绿色经济中心副研究员陈中舜对这一提议表示支持，他表示，由于可再生能源发展低于预期，台湾对天然气的依赖变得过于严重。
“台湾现在最缺的不是目标，也不是技术，而是时间。”陈说。
陈认为，人工智能数据中心和先进芯片工厂的建设速度可以比主要电力基础设施更快。他援引核工业的估计称，反应堆可能在 18 个月到三年内重新启动，有助于满足对可靠、负担得起和低碳电力的需求，同时台湾扩大可再生能源发电能力。
陈表示，他支持继续投资可再生能源，并将核电视为实现电力结构多元化的一种方式。他说，重启二号和三号核电站也将减少台湾对液化天然气运输的依赖。
经济部副部长赖建信反对这一提议，他表示，随着核电占发电量的比例下降，台湾经济增长，出口增加。
“核电并不是经济的灵丹妙药，”赖表示，他指的是产业升级和台湾供应链的实力。
赖表示，政府仍然对核电持开放态度，国营的台湾电力公司（台电）已经在评估现有核电站是否可以根据修订后的法律安全地恢复运营。检查包括寻找因多年暴露于辐射或腐蚀而造成的损坏。
赖说：“公投不能取代法律要求的严格审查，也不能免除对设备结构安全的科学验证。”
这张中央通讯社档案照片中的活动人士抗议核能
赖说，即使二号和三号电厂被发现安全并且重启获得公众认可，它们的总发电量也只相当于台湾目前发电量的10%左右。他补充说，任何决定都必须解决核废料处理问题。
台湾于 2025 年 5 月 17 日关闭了马鞍山核电站最后一个运行的反应堆，履行了执政的民进党 (DPP) 长期以来逐步淘汰核电的承诺。
赖清德总统3月21日表示，经济部已判定马鞍山及新北万里区二号核电站具备启动重启程序的条件，台电正在准备下一步工作。

Referendum reignites debate over Taiwan's 'non-nuclear homeland' policy
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 14 (CNA) A supporter of ending Taiwan's "non-nuclear homeland" policy argued Saturday that restarting reactors could buy time for renewable energy to develop, while a government representative questioned the need for a referendum when restart assessments were already underway under existing law.
The two spoke at the second of five televised forums organized by the Central Election Commission ahead of the Nov. 28 referendum, which coincides with local elections. The ballot asks voters whether they support the government ending the "non-nuclear homeland" energy policy and using nuclear power to revitalize the economy.
Speaking in favor of the proposal, Chen Jong-shun (陳中舜), an associate research fellow at the Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research's Center for Green Economy, said Taiwan had grown too reliant on natural gas as renewable energy development fell short of expectations.
"What Taiwan lacks most right now is neither goals nor technology, but time," Chen said.
AI data centers and advanced chip plants can be built faster than major power infrastructure, Chen argued. Citing nuclear industry estimates, he said reactors could be restarted in 18 months to three years, helping meet demand for reliable, affordable and low-carbon electricity while Taiwan expands its renewable capacity.
Chen said he supported continued investment in renewables and saw nuclear power as a way to diversify the electricity mix. Restarting the No. 2 and No. 3 nuclear power plants would also reduce Taiwan's reliance on shipments of liquefied natural gas, he said.
Vice Minister of Economic Affairs Lai Chien-hsin (賴建信), arguing against the proposal, said that Taiwan's economy had grown and its exports risen as nuclear power's share of electricity generation declined.
"Nuclear power is not a cure-all for the economy," Lai said, pointing to industrial upgrading and the strength of Taiwan's supply chains.
The government remained open to nuclear power, Lai said, and state-run Taiwan Power Co. (Taipower) was already assessing whether existing plants could safely resume operations under the amended law. The checks include looking for deterioration caused by years of exposure to radiation or corrosion.
"A referendum cannot replace the rigorous reviews required by law, nor can it dispense with scientific verification of the structural safety of equipment," Lai said.
Activists protest against nuclear energy in this CNA file photo
Even if the No. 2 and No. 3 plants were found safe and their restart gained public acceptance, their combined output would be equivalent to only about 10 percent of Taiwan's current electricity generation, Lai said. He added that any decision would also have to address nuclear waste disposal.
Taiwan shut down its last operating reactor at the Maanshan Nuclear Power Plant on May 17, 2025, fulfilling a longstanding pledge by the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) to phase out nuclear power.
On March 21, President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said the Ministry of Economic Affairs had determined that Maanshan and the No. 2 Nuclear Power Plant in New Taipei's Wanli District met the conditions to begin the restart process and that Taipower was preparing the next steps.
The president cited rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence, the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and growing geopolitical risks, while reaffirming his support for renewable energy.

# Blount Island honors 26 civilians for nearly 600 years of combined service

9 Nov 2026| Dustin Senger Marine Corps Blount Island Command

[PRINT](https://www.bic.marines.mil/DesktopModules/ArticleCS/Print.aspx?PortalId=188&ModuleId=41294&Article=4644726)

[SHARE](https://www.addtoany.com/share#url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bic.marines.mil%2FNews%2FArticle%2FArticle%2F4644726%2Fblount-island-honors-26-civilians-for-nearly-600-years-of-combined-service%2F&title=Blount%20Island%20honors%2026%20civilians%20for%20nearly%20600%20years%20of%20combined%20service%20%3E%20Marine%20Corps%20Blount%20Island%20Command%20%3E%20Article)

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. --
From a former commanding officer to a specialist who keeps Navy ship-to-shore equipment ready, 26 civilian employees received awards Nov. 6 at Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island in Jacksonville, Florida. The honorees, mostly veterans, had a combined 585 years of service.

[![Image 2: Blount Island honors 26 civilians for nearly 600 years of combined service](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Nov/09/2004025138/600/400/0/261106-M-FX029-1255.JPG)](https://www.bic.marines.mil/News/Article/Article/4644726/blount-island-honors-26-civilians-for-nearly-600-years-of-combined-service/#pop10475982)

 U.S. Marine Corps Col. David Merles, commanding officer of Blount Island Command, presents a 35-year service award Nov. 6, 2026, to Matt Crabill, deputy commanding officer, at Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island, Florida. Crabill previously commanded both the installation and Blount Island Command as a Marine colonel. He was one of 26 civilian employees Merles recognized for a combined 585 years of service. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Jonathan Wright)

 U.S. Marine Corps Col. David Merles, who commands the installation and Blount Island Command, applauded the recipients and thanked the service members and civilians gathered for the ceremony. The awards recognized service milestones from 10 to 35 years.
Darryl Dean, a Navy positioning equipment specialist, was one of six employees who marked 30 years of service.

Four employees reached 35 years. Matthew Crabill, a former Marine colonel, once commanded both organizations and now serves as their civilian deputy commanding officer. Navy positioning director William Fish, supply analyst Bernard Lyons and equipment specialist Darwin Thode II also reached the milestone.

At Blount Island, veterans put their military experience to work as civilian employees and contractors. As service members rotate through the installation, those veterans and their colleagues help the command keep equipment ready for Marines to draw from ships and sites overseas.

Department of Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
[Docket No. APHIS-2026-1189]
Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, USDA.
Request for approval of a new information collection; comment request.
In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, this notice announces the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service's intention to request approval of a new information collection for implementation of vaccination for highly pathogenic avian influenza in zoos and animal sanctuaries.
We will consider all comments that we receive on or before January 15, 2027.
You may submit comments by either of the following methods:
Federal eRulemaking Portal: Go to www.regulations.gov. Enter APHIS-2026-1189 in the Search field. Select the Documents tab, then select the Comment button in the list of documents.
Postal Mail/Commercial Delivery: Send your comment to Docket No. APHIS-2026-1189, Regulatory Analysis and Development, PPD, APHIS, 5601 Sunnyside Ave., #AP760, Beltsville, MD 20705.
Supporting documents and any comments we receive on this docket may be viewed at www.regulations.gov or in our reading room, which is in room 1620 of the USDA South Building, 14th Street and Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC. Normal reading room hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except holidays. To be sure someone is there to help you, please call (202) 799-7039 before coming.
For information on the effort to support HPAI vaccination in zoos and animal sanctuaries, contact Dr. Steven Rekant, Public Health Veterinary Medical Officer, APHIS, Veterinary Services, Strategy and Policy, 5601 Sunnyside Ave., Beltsville, MD 20705; (971) 263-3734; Steven.rekant@usda.gov. For more information on the information collection reporting process, contact Ms. Sheniqua Harris, APHIS' Paperwork Reduction Act Coordinator, at (301) 851-2528 or email APHIS.PRA@usda.gov.
Title: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza: Administration of Vaccine in Zoos.
OMB Control Number: 0579-XXXX.
Type of Request: Approval of a new information collection.
Abstract: Under the Animal Health Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 8301 et seq.), the Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to protect the health of U.S. livestock by preventing the introduction and interstate spread of serious diseases and pests of livestock and for eradicating such diseases from the United States when feasible. This authority has been delegated to the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS).
Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is an extremely infectious and fatal form of avian influenza, particularly in poultry. An HPAI outbreak can have significant consequences for livestock, wildlife, and producers' livelihoods, as well as significant impacts on international trade (especially in poultry and poultry products).
APHIS is expanding its efforts to combat HPAI with vaccination by initiating a program to cooperate with State animal health officials to allow zoos and similar facilities to vaccinate animals in their care against HPAI. This program establishes conditions for zoos and animal sanctuaries to receive and administer vaccine; the information collected will enable APHIS and State animal health officials to determine facility eligibility and ensure that vaccination activities are conducted safely and in compliance with Federal and State requirements.
To participate, facilities must submit an HPAI Vaccination Plan demonstrating compliance with APHIS criteria, including oversight by a USDA-accredited Category II veterinarian; appropriate recordkeeping and individual animal identification; adequate biosecurity; and separation of vaccinated animals from specified domestic poultry species. The plan must justify the need for vaccination, describe vaccine administration and inventory control procedures, outline biosecurity protocols, animal identification, document veterinary monitoring, describe medical recordkeeping, and address procedures for animal transfers or disposition.
Once approved, facilities may obtain licensed HPAI vaccine from manufacturers, who are required to maintain shipment records. Facilities must retain detailed vaccination and inventory records, conduct required testing through National Animal Health Laboratory Network laboratories, submit annual reports, and provide a final summary report upon completion of vaccination activities. Failure to comply with requirements may result in suspension or revocation of authorization.
We are asking the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to approve our use of these information collection activities for 3 years.
The purpose of this notice is to solicit comments from the public (as well as affected agencies) concerning our information collection. These comments will help us:
(1) Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
(2) Evaluate the accuracy of our estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
(3) Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and
(4) Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, through use, as appropriate, of automated, electronic, mechanical, and other collection technologies; e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses. ( printed page 73515)
Estimate of burden: The public burden for this collection of information is estimated to average 1.043 hours per response.
Respondents: Facility management personnel at zoos and animal sanctuaries, accredited veterinarians, nonprofit wildlife facilities, and State animal health authorities, as well as vaccine manufacturers responsible for shipment recordkeeping.
Estimated annual number of respondents: 160.
Estimated annual number of responses per respondent: 6.
Estimated annual number of responses: 960.
Estimated total annual burden on respondents: 1,001 hours. (Due to averaging, the total annual burden hours may not equal the product of the annual number of responses multiplied by the reporting burden per response.)
All responses to this notice will be summarized and included in the request for OMB approval. All comments will also become a matter of public record.
Done in Washington, DC, this 21st day of October 2026.
Administrator, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.
