# 柏林的《日报》：黄仁勋事件可能会损害北京的利益

德国媒体如何看待英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职及其影响？

发表时间： 14/11/2026 - 23:10

 11 分钟 浏览时间

 A renúncia de Jensen Huang, cofundador e presidente executivo da Nvidia há 33 anos, provocou uma crise em uma das empresas mais valiosas. REUTERS - Dado Ruvic

 作者： [柏林特约记者 丹兰](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E6%9F%8F%E6%9E%97%E7%89%B9%E7%BA%A6%E8%AE%B0%E8%80%85-%E4%B8%B9%E5%85%B0/ "柏林特约记者 丹兰")

广告

继续浏览后续

海德堡《莱茵-内卡河报》（RHEIN-NECKAR-ZEITUNG）表示：黄仁勋因自己的感情生活而栽了跟头。他与一名疑似中国间谍的女性有染，这件事已经具有政治层面的影响，并使美国在与其长期竞争对手中国的关系中陷入不利境地。毕竟，如果全球市值最高的科技企业迅速崩盘，这就成了一个具有国家重要性的重大问题。

柏林《每日镜报》（DER TAGESSPIEGEL）认为：黄仁勋的婚外情已经演变成一个棘手的问题，不仅影响美国政治和世界经济，也影响数百万在股市投资、为退休生活积累财富的人。因为黄仁勋并不是一个普通人。他曾是人工智能热潮围绕其旋转的那颗太阳。在争夺人工智能领域主导地位的竞赛中，各国将自己的未来押注在少数几家企业身上，而这些企业又将命运寄托在少数权势显赫的企业领导人身上。这种权力高度集中是危险的。至少，美国人还可以要求黄仁勋到国会接受质询。而德国甚至连这一点都做不到。然而，美国发生的事情对德国而言绝不是一场遥远的风波。今年10月，黄仁勋曾在柏林与德国总理默茨并肩出席活动，并警告德国在人工智能领域已经落后。他甚至立即提出了解决方案：德国联邦政府与英伟达达成了人工智能合作伙伴关系，并投入数亿欧元，让初创企业能够租用算力，而这些算力所需的芯片则由英伟达提供。

《南德意志报》（SÜDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG）就黄仁勋与美国政府之间的关系表示：多年来，黄仁勋一直与华盛顿围绕向中国出口高性能芯片的限制措施发生争执，直到他辞职。这场争执很可能恰恰使他对中国情报机构特别具有吸引力。黄仁勋认为，出口管制是一个严重的错误。他或许是对的。华盛顿剥夺了英伟达从中国人工智能热潮中大规模获利的机会。然而，美国在阻止中国获得英伟达芯片方面，取得的成效却远没有那么理想。

柏林的《日报》（taz）问道：黄仁勋倒台对中国意味着什么？在中国，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋涉嫌间谍事件被当作一场胜利来庆祝。但从长远来看，这场丑闻可能反而会损害北京的利益。黄仁勋的这段感情关系是否真的涉及北京国家安全部门的行动，目前仍然没有定论。但对于许多中国人来说，艾丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）无疑是一位爱国的造反者。她被认为帮助自己的祖国获得了英伟达的高性能芯片。此外，这位42岁的女性与中国开国领袖毛泽东来自同一个省份，这一点也进一步增添了她的传奇色彩。然而，艾丽丝·黄真的成功了吗？初步来看，这件事的影响具有很大的两面性。事实上，已经辞职的英伟达创始人与一名涉嫌间谍活动的女性之间的恋情，曾一度导致华尔街相关市场蒸发超过5000亿美元的企业市值。此外，全球最重要的人工智能企业在可预见的未来也将明显受到削弱。毕竟，英伟达在很大程度上是围绕黄仁勋这位具有非凡个人能力的领导者建立起来的。所有这些似乎都表明，中国政府在策略上取得了一场胜利，因为北京正试图在科技领导权的竞争中超越美国。但与此同时，中国自身遭受的直接损失也相当巨大。因为当美国股市截至周五已经基本恢复稳定时，中国科技股的抛售潮却仍在持续。仅阿里巴巴和腾讯这两家中国领先的互联网巨头，合计市值就已经蒸发了超过750亿美元。中国可能面临痛苦的长期后果。英伟达丑闻使中国工业间谍活动的风险再次成为公众高度关注的焦点，其关注程度是近年来前所未有的。与此同时，在华盛顿，无论是民主党还是共和党内部的对华强硬派，目前都获得了强有力的支持。黄仁勋事件为这些强硬派提供了有力的论据，使他们能够要求进一步收紧美国对华技术出口管制。然而，艾丽丝·黄是否真的是间谍，受到专家质疑。舒德蒙（Desmond Shu）分析认为：“我怀疑，艾丽丝·黄首先是一名商业中间人，她为其他商业利益集团办事，而不一定是中国情报机构的特工。”舒德蒙在21世纪初曾作为房地产开发商活跃于北京，并与中国所谓的“红色贵族”有过交往。如今，他流亡英国，成为一名批评中国共产党的人士。他认为，艾丽丝·黄更接近中国所说的“白手套”，即受企业家或政府官员委托，负责促成一些敏感交易，同时掩盖真正幕后操纵者身份的人。换句话说，这类人往往充当利益集团的代理人，在台前处理事务，而真正的决策者则隐藏在幕后。

# 法国奢侈品最大市场从中国转向美国

中国市场曾是奢侈品行业的主要增长引擎，然而，近年来中国房地产市场的持续低迷以及股市表现疲软，削弱了中国国内需求，如今中国市场已经成了奢侈品销售的最大拖累。

 8 分钟 浏览时间

 Photo prise le 25 octobre 2010 à Paris montrant la façade d'un magasin de luxe d'Hermès, groupe qui vient de mettre fin à un contentieux vieux de 4 ans avec l'autre groupe de luxe français LVMH. AFP Photo/ Miguel Medina

 作者： [法广](https://www.rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E6%B3%95%E5%B9%BF/ "法广")

广告

继续浏览后续

奢侈品行业龙头LVMH于10月12日公布的财报数据显示，第三季度业绩不如预期，主要因为大中华区消费疲软，导致第三季度除日本外的亚洲市场销售额重挫5%。

不过，中国市场放缓之际，美国、欧洲及日本市场的韧性表现，部分抵消了中国市场疲软带来的冲击。法国的路威酩轩（LVMH）和爱马仕（Hermès）等奢侈品集团近几年来在美国迅速扩张，并取得成效。专家预计，对于一些奢侈品集团来说，美国可能会取代中国，成为其最大的单一市场。

据《金融时报》报导，过去五年里，LVMH、爱马仕、开云集团（Kering）和历峰集团（Richemont）等奢侈品巨头纷纷在美国扩张，将投资触角伸向了纽约第五大道（Fifth Avenue）或加州的比弗利山庄（Beverly Hills）罗迪欧大道（Rodeo Drive）等传统奢侈品核心区之外，在奥斯汀（Austin）、斯科茨代尔（Scottsdale）、普林斯顿（Princeton）和纳什维尔（Nashville）等地开设了门店。

从目前来看，这些投资至少对部分奢侈品集团而言已见成效。爱马仕在7月份发布的半年度财报中指出，按固定汇率计算，2026年上半年，其美洲地区营收增长了15.3%，增速位居各地区之首。LVMH集团在10月份表示，其第三季度在美国市场的销售额持续增长。

并非所有奢侈品牌都在美国市场取得了成功，比如开云集团的可比销售额在2023年和2024年分别下降22%和11%。但大中华区消费疲软带来的冲击更为明显。中国曾经是爱马仕最大的单一市场，但目前中国市场环境“非常困难”。相反，爱马仕今年第三季度继续扩大在美国的零售布局，7月在圣地亚哥翻新扩建原有门店后重新开业，8月和9月又分别在芝加哥郊区和纽约布鲁克林区的威廉斯堡开设新店。

在美国各地扩张业务，帮助奢侈品集团抵消在中国市场销售额下滑的影响。随着人工智能（AI）的发展推动华尔街股市繁荣，奢侈品集团正试图从中捕捉由此产生的新财富。

据《金融时报》报导，德意志银行（Deutsche Bank）零售与奢侈品行业分析师亚当‧科克伦（Adam Cochrane）表示：“只要股市带来的‘财富效应’持续存在，未来三至五年内，美国奢侈品市场的表现预计将继续优于全球奢侈品市场的整体表现。”他预计，美国有望取代中国，成为LVMH和历峰集团在全球最大的单一奢侈品市场。目前中国占全球奢侈品消费总额的30%。

美国总统特朗普发起的“关税战”也促使一些法国奢侈品品牌在美国本土进行生产布局。自2019年（特朗普第一任期）起，路易威登（Louis Vuitton）便开始在德克萨斯州的阿尔瓦拉多（Alvarado）生产皮革制品，并表示到2027年将增设第二家工坊。

随着五角大楼最终完成对美国在欧洲的军事态势的审查，一项相对较小的承诺值得避免预算削减：即在北约科索沃部队服役的约 600 名美国士兵。他们几乎没有参与关于旅和数十亿美元项目的辩论，但他们在巴尔干地区保持了来之不易的和平，将他们撤出几乎什么也挽救不了，同时让莫斯科获得了廉价的战略胜利。驻科部队于 1999 年 6 月在北约指挥下部署，此前北约轰炸了南斯拉夫，以制止斯洛博丹·米洛舍维奇领导的塞尔维亚军队对阿尔巴尼亚人的暴力行为。科索沃于2008年宣布独立，但塞尔维亚在俄罗斯和中国的支持下仍然拒绝承认。欧洲态势评估是一项合法的活动。在多年来敦促欧洲盟国承担更多常规防御之后，特朗普政府正确地提出了一些尖锐的问题，即美国军队在哪些方面可以增加独特的价值，以及在适当的时间发展其能力和能力的情况下欧洲可以在哪些方面加强。但驻科部队是一项美国角色不易被取代的任务，因为它既是政治性的，也是军事性的，而且错误的决定可能会导致欧洲东南侧的不稳定。从威胁开始。即使在乌克兰遭受重大损失的同时，弗拉基米尔·普京也没有放弃破坏欧洲稳定的努力。巴尔干地区是欧洲的软肋，是一个备受青睐的舞台：煽动成本低廉，是一个分散西方对乌克兰注意力的地方。
莫斯科长期以来一直利用塞尔维亚作为破坏科索沃稳定的杠杆。2017年，一列俄罗斯制造的火车开往科索沃北部，这是一次带有“科索沃是塞尔维亚”口号的滚动挑衅。俄罗斯在科索沃附近运营着一个所谓的人道主义中心，该中心被怀疑充当俄罗斯情报站。塞尔维亚与俄罗斯密切的情报联系使莫斯科能够接触到准备挑衅的当地民族主义力量。 2023年，科索沃北部警察遭到武装袭击，普里什蒂纳将此归咎于塞尔维亚支持的武装分子，这加剧了人们对与俄罗斯结盟的行为体利用紧张局势的担忧；今年早些时候，俄罗斯外交部长警告称，“欧洲中心正在酝酿一场重大爆炸性局势”。紧张局势一再爆发。 2023年5月，塞尔维亚抗议者与科索沃警察发生冲突，造成90多名北约维和人员受伤，促使塞尔维亚提高军事戒备级别。那年 9 月，在巴尼斯卡发生的一次袭击中，全副武装的塞族枪手杀死了一名科索沃警察，并将自己关在一座修道院里，这表明当地的冲突可以多么迅速地演变为地区危机。危险还没有过去。塞尔维亚强人亚历山大·武契奇承认在10月25日的塞尔维亚议会选举中落败，但贝尔格莱德的外交政策方向尚不确定，人们担心其对科索沃的看法不会改变。

【原文 English Original】
As the Pentagon finalizes its review of U.S. force posture in Europe, one relatively small commitment deserves protection from the budget axe: the roughly 600 American troops serving in NATO’s Kosovo Force. They barely register in a debate about brigades and billion-dollar line items, but they keep a hard-won peace in the Balkans, and pulling them out would save almost nothing while handing Moscow a cheap strategic win. KFOR was deployed in June 1999 under NATO command, after the alliance bombed Yugoslavia to stop the violence perpetrated by Slobodan Milosevic’s Serbian forces against ethnic Albanians. Kosovo declared independence in 2008, but Serbia, backed by Russia and China, still refuses to recognize it. The Europe posture review is a legitimate exercise. After years of urging European allies to shoulder more of their own conventional defense, the Trump administration is right to ask hard questions about where American forces add unique value and where Europe can step up given suitable time to develop their capabilities and capacities. But KFOR is a mission in which the American role is not easily replaced, because it is as much political as military, and where a wrong call risks instability on Europe’s southeastern flank. Start with the threat. Even while absorbing heavy losses in Ukraine, Vladimir Putin has not given up on destabilizing Europe. The Balkans, Europe’s soft underbelly, are a favored arena: cheap to stir, a place to distract Western attention from Ukraine. Moscow has long used Serbia as a lever against Kosovo’s stability. In 2017, a Russian-made train was sent toward northern Kosovo, a rolling provocation that bore the slogan “Kosovo is Serbia.” Russia runs a so-called humanitarian center near Kosovo that is suspected of serving as a Russian intelligence station. Close Serbian-Russian intelligence ties give Moscow access to local nationalist forces prepared for provocations. In 2023, an armed attack on Kosovo police in the north, which Pristina blamed on Serbian-backed militants, heightened fears that Russian-aligned actors were exploiting the tension; earlier that year, Russia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs warned that “a major explosive situation is brewing in the heart of Europe.” Tensions have repeatedly flared. In May 2023, clashes between Serb protesters and Kosovo police injured more than 90 NATO peacekeepers and prompted Serbia to raise its military alert level. That September, an attack in Banjska, where heavily armed Serb gunmen killed a Kosovo police officer and barricaded themselves in a monastery, showed how quickly a local flare-up can become a regional crisis. The danger has not passed. Serbian strongman Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia’s Oct. 25 parliamentary election, but Belgrade’s foreign-policy direction is uncertain and there are concerns that its views on Kosovo will not change. In October, Russia’s ambassador to the UN warned that the situation in Kosovo “remains persistently tense and is literally teetering on the brink.” Still, Kosovo and Serbia have remained at peace since 1999, in large part because of KFOR. In the words of a bipartisan group of U.S lawmakers, the force functions as “a political deterrent to those seeking to stoke ethnic violence.” An American drawdown from KFOR may embolden nationalist agendas in Kosovo and Serbia as well as separatist ambitions in Republika Srpska, the Serb-dominated region in nearby Bosnia. The American presence in KFOR is valued precisely because it is American. U.S. troops have anchored KFOR since its creation, and Washington currently leads Regional Command East, a position of real operational weight, not symbolism. The U.S. has traditionally provided the 600 or so American troops—often Army National Guardsmen—an economy-of-force mission with minimal cost or effect on the U.S. Army’s ability to execute missions elsewhere around the globe. The mission accounts for less than 1 percent of the total U.S. troops in Europe. KFOR’s value becomes plain when contrasted with Operation Althea in neighboring Bosnia. EUFOR, an EU-led force with roughly 1,500 troops, has struggled to respond decisively to repeated provocations by Republika Srpska leader Milorad Dodik, who’s backed by Moscow and Belgrade. EU ambassadors rejected Bosnian appeals to help enforce an arrest warrant against him in 2025, citing political risk. Dodik has openly mocked EUFOR’s patrols. Lacking an American anchor and a unified chain of command willing to act, EUFOR has too often had to manage crises rather than deterring them. KFOR, by contrast, has demonstrated it can surge forces when tested, providing genuine deterrence. After the 2023 Banjska incident, NATO increased its peacekeeping presence in Kosovo. Serbia drew down its border deployment, ending the crisis. The Pentagon is right to ask what the value of an American military presence is worth. For KFOR, the answer is plain: a few hundred U.S. troops are successfully maintaining a quarter-century-long peace that Russia would love to see unravel. Lawmakers from both parties already understand that. The Pentagon should, too, and keep KFOR intact. Mark Montgomery, a retired U.S. Navy rear admiral, serves as a senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ (FDD), where Ivana Stradner is a research fellow. ]]>

内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100于10月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，号称是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片。国家级政策文件传统上避免直接讨论RISC-V，但今年9月，《电子信息制造业“十五五”规划》宣布，要求推进RISC-V研发和产业化，开发人工智能（AI）RISC-V芯片。 RISC-V 为自力更生带来了明显的好处，并且芯片可以进行调整，包括针对军事用例进行优化。
然而，中国的分析师担心芯片的“玻璃天花板”，甚至国家 IT 替代计划也指出，在政府系统中用于替代外国技术的 RISC-V 芯片的份额“可以忽略不计”。 10月19日，深圳芯片制造商进迭时空与香山处理器团队在第六届RISC-V中国峰会上推出了新型46核服务器芯片V100。[1]其制造商宣称其是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片（21世纪经济报道，10月19日；科技日报，10月20日）。 RISC-V 是一种开源指令集架构 (ISA)，是处理器运行的语言。与全球几乎所有计算机和手机中使用的 Arm 或 Intel x86 等专有 ISA 不同，任何人都可以使用 RISC-V，无需支付许可费或需要其他权限。由英国和美国公司制造的 Arm 和英特尔处理器必须遵守这些国家政府实施的许可和出口管制。相比之下，RISC-V 主要由 RISC-V International 监管，这是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，旨在避免此类漏洞。最近推出的服务器芯片代表了中华人民共和国（PRC）该行业更广泛的趋势。
北京最初在 2010 年代中期开始将 RISC-V 视为对抗西方技术霸权并扩大其在新兴技术领域结构性力量的一种方式（中国简报，2023 年 12 月 15 日）。此后，北京通过国家主导的政策支持鼓励其发展，从城市层面开始，逐步上升到国家层面。尽管这些芯片的功能仍然落后于西方竞争对手，但它们越来越多地部署在数据中心的服务器中，而不仅仅是嵌入消费设备中。从市政厅到五年计划 2023年以来，地方层面对RISC-V的支持已经明确，特别是在上海、北京和深圳等一线城市（中国简报，2023年12月15日）。北京经济技术开发区的目标是到 2030 年使 RISC-V 产业价值超过 500 亿元人民币（70 亿美元），据一些估计，届时全国市场将达到约 2200 亿元人民币（210 亿美元）（北京市政府，2025 年 1 月 3 日；中国日报）

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is expanding its use of RISC-V, an open-source chip design standard, as well as its influence over the international nonprofit organization that manages it. This follows growing fears in recent years of being cut off from chips designed by Western industry leaders such as Arm and Intel. PRC firms are now creating RISC-V chips not just for consumer devices but for servers and data centers, even though they are less powerful than proprietary chips. The V100, launched in October and co-created by a state-backed entity, is billed as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards. National-level policy documents have traditionally avoided discussing RISC-V directly, but in September, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to advance RISC-V research, development, and industrialization, and to develop RISC-V chips for artificial intelligence (AI). RISC-V brings clear benefits for self-reliance, and the chips can be adapted, including being optimized for military use cases. Analysts in the PRC worry, however, about a “glass ceiling” for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible.” On October 19, Shenzhen-based chipmaker SpacemiT (进迭时空) and the state-backed XiangShan (香山) processor team launched the V100, a new 46-core server chip, at the sixth RISC-V Summit China.  [1] Its makers bill it as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards ( 21st Century Business Herald , October 19; Science and Technology Daily , October 20). RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), which is the language that processors run on. Unlike proprietary ISAs, such as Arm or Intel’s x86 that are used in almost all of the world’s computers and phones, anyone can use RISC-V without paying a license fee or requiring other permissions. Arm and Intel processors, made by British and U.S. companies, must abide by licensing and export controls put in place by those countries’ governments. By comparison, RISC-V is mainly overseen by RISC-V International, a Switzerland-based nonprofit that avoids such vulnerabilities. The recently unveiled server chip is representative of broader trends in the sector within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Beijing initially began to view RISC-V as a way to counter the West’s technological hegemony and extend its structural power in emerging technologies in the mid-2010s ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Since then, it has encouraged its development through state-led policy support, starting at the city level and moving up to the national level. Although the chips’ capabilities remain behind those of Western rivals, they are increasingly being deployed in servers for data centers, not just embedded in consumer devices. From City Halls to the Five-Year Plan Since 2023, local-level support for RISC-V has been explicit, especially in first-tier cities like Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Beijing’s Economic-Technological Development Area aims for a RISC-V industry worth more than renminbi (RMB) 50 billion ($7 billion) by 2030, at which point the national market will reach around RMB 220 billion ($21 billion), according to some estimates ( Beijing Municipal Government , January 3, 2025; China Daily , October 22). National-level documents have tended instead to use the term “open source” to implicitly refer to RISC-V. In mid-September, however, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to “advance the research, development, and industrialization of RISC-V” (推进第五代精简指令集 (RISC-V) 研发与产业化), and to support RISC-V artificial intelligence (AI) and embedded system chips ( Ministry of Information and Industry Technology , September 15).  [2] Server Ambitions, Smartphone-Class Silicon RISC-V’s strength so far has been in cheaper control chips for appliances and cars, but newer chips signal data center servers as an emerging use case. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calls the open-source XiangShan core the most powerful of its kind in the world ( China Daily , March 26). Beyond the latest processor from SpacemiT and XiangShan, Alibaba now offers a server-class design, the C950, that it says performs on par with Apple’s M1 chip, which it released in 2020, on a standard performance test ( The Register , March 25). Engineers usually judge how well a core is designed via a two-step process. First, they run an industry-standard test, which times how long a processor takes to complete a set of tasks, and turns that time into a score. Second, they divide the score by the core’s clock speed, which is the number of steps it takes each second, measured in gigahertz (GHz). The result measures how much work a core does in each step (see Figure 1). On this metric, PRC progress is substantial: XiangShan’s cores have roughly doubled since 2021. Measured at the speeds they actually run, the best cores in the SpacemiT/XiangShan processor are well behind Nvidia’s leading Grace server processor, and those produced by Arm and Intel (see Figure 2). Alibaba’s C950, which it licenses to other chipmakers, comes close to or beats Grace based on the firm’s internal testing. RISC-V is a standard for general-purpose processors, and is not usually used for the graphics chips (GPUs) that run most complex AI models ( Jon Peddie Research , December 29, 2025). By SpacemiT’s own ratings, its chip’s computing power is between 50–90 percent of Nvidia’s similarly priced Jetson Orin Nano Super, which is used in robots and drones. Its AI engine also falls short of the minimum Microsoft sets for “AI PCs” (see Figure 3).  [4] RISC-V, therefore, does little to address Beijing’s lack of compute. RISC-V Buys Assurance and Customization RISC-V offers the PRC with two benefits: the assurance of sustainable access, and adaptability for military purposes, which would be risky use-cases for employing Western chips. The fear of being cut off from access to chips has been acute since Huawei learned in 2019 that its access to Arm’s designs could be suspended ( BBC , May 22, 2019). As an open-source architecture, RISC-V can be modified and tailored to user requirements. In some instances, however, this has allowed it to be adapted for military purposes. A team at Information Engineering University, an institution affiliated with the People’s Liberation Army, was able to customize command for data encryption to a small RISC-V chip, accelerating encryption by about seven times with only about two percent more circuitry.  [5] These benefits are another part of the reason why the PRC has pushed to deepen its influence over RISC-V at the international level. Chinese firms now hold half of the 24 top-tier memberships in RISC-V International ( RISC-V , accessed November 3). U.S. firms are deepening their stake in the RISC-V ecosystem too. Nvidia said in July 2025 that its CUDA software, the backbone of AI computing, would support RISC-V processors, and Qualcomm bought the RISC-V server designer Ventana in December 2025 ( The Register , July 21, 2025; Qualcomm , December 10, 2025). Conclusion Beijing continues to emphasize RISC-V to advance technological self-reliance and resilience. Although it is starting to use RISC-V chips in servers and data centers, the chips function at well below the capabilities of the most advanced processors. Analysts in the PRC have worried about a “glass ceiling” (玻璃天花板) for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program (信创) has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible (微乎其微)” ( Sina Finance , April 7). It is nevertheless too soon to dismiss the hype over the PRC’s RISC-V development. RISC-V currently also enjoys support from U.S. companies. This makes the international standards that govern RISC-V an important battle ground in the competition to shape this arena of open-source technology. It remains unclear, however, whether the United States will seek to build a U.S.-led ISA ecosystem or discourage U.S. and allied firms from taking part in Chinese-led RISC-V projects. Neither option is cost-free, although if Washington does not take action, a key part of the semiconductor supply chain could end up being controlled by Beijing. Notes [1] A core is the part of a processor that reads and carries out software instructions. [2] The plan was released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and the National Development and Reform Commission, but grew out of work by eight agencies that drafted the country’s first national guidance on RISC-V in 2025 ( Reuters , March 3, 2025). [3] For Figure 2, panel A estimates the real speed of a single core by multiplying its points per gigahertz by the clock speed at which it actually ships, and shows the result relative to a core in Nvidia’s Grace server processor (set at 100). Intel and AMD do not publish comparable SPECint2006 figures, so their desktop cores are set equal to Arm’s Cortex-X925, which independent testing by Chips and Cheese found to be within the margin of error of the fastest AMD and Intel cores on the newer SPECint2017 test ( Chips and Cheese, March 3 ). Panels B and C compare whole server chips. The first is the number of cores. Each core works on its own task, so more cores means more work at once. The second is memory speed, or bandwidth: how many gigabytes of data a chip can move to and from its memory each second. In large data-center jobs this is often the real limit, because even a fast core sits idle while it waits for data. The lower panels of Figure 2 compare other measures of performance for entire server chips. The V100 has 46 cores; Nvidia’s Grace has 72; and the top Intel and AMD server chips have 128–192. The V100 also moves data to and from memory at about half their speed. It draws far less power, however, at 120 watts, compared to about 250 for Grace and 500 for the Intel and AMD chips ( GitHub , accessed October 27). [4] Figure 3 measures AI performance in trillions of simple calculations per second (TOPS). Since AI models run on vast numbers of such calculations, higher TOPS values translate to faster AI. The left panel divides TOPS by the power a chip draws, in watts, to show energy efficiency, which matters most in battery-powered robots and drones. The right panel shows raw TOPS for laptop chips. Companies quote TOPS in different ways that can double or even quadruple the headline number, so the chart puts every chip on the same basis. Even if the SpacemiT processor reaches 30 TOPS, this is still short of Microsoft’s bar of 40. By The Register’s estimate, even Alibaba’s best design would roughly match Apple’s M1 ( The Register , March 25). [5] Zhang Xiaolei, Dai Zibin, Guo Pengfei, et al., “Design and Verification of a RISC-V-Based AES Cryptographic Acceleration Engine [基于RISC-V的AES密码加速引擎设计与验证],” Application of Electronic Technique [电子技术应用] 49, no. 2 (2023): 39–44. Results are from FPGA prototypes built on the open-source Hummingbird E203 core. The post RISC-V Open-Source Chip Push Puts Strategy Over Capability appeared first on Jamestown .

“道德红线”？世界正处于自主武器革命的风口浪尖
11 月 9 日，TYTAN Technologies 在慕尼黑开设自主拦截无人机新生产工厂，展示了 TI-04 无人机模型。法新社-即时

巴黎 — — 由人工智能驱动的致命自主武器将给战争带来革命性的变化，但目前还没有适当的监管或法律框架来管理这项新技术。
周一在日内瓦联合国召开的会议将讨论如何限制和禁止此类武器，一些人称之为杀手机器人。
但一些分析人士怀疑《特定常规武器公约》（CCW）的讨论能否跟上快速变化的武器的步伐。
以下是会议召开前的三个关键问题。
日内瓦安全政策中心全球和新兴风险主管让-马克·里克利（Jean-Marc Rickli）表示，致命自主武器系统（LAWS）“可以在执行这些任务时识别、选择和攻击目标，而无需人类操作员的干预”。
自主武器早已存在。法国国际关系研究所地缘政治技术中心的劳尔·德鲁西-罗什贡德表示，杀伤人员地雷“是一种自主武器，当有人踩到它时它就会爆炸”。
但随着人工智能增强无人机的扩散，此类武器现在“能够选择和攻击未预先确定的目标，无需人工干预即可适应环境，”里克利说。
因此，潜在监管机构面临的关键问题在于确定人类对使用此类武器的决定的控制程度。
美国在使用自主武器时提到了“适当水平的人类判断”。
法国坚持认为人类必须参与决策循环，并禁止“致命自主武器系统”（LAWS），但允许“部分自主”系统，即PLAWS。
法国国防部国防人工智能局 (AMIAD) 副局长、少将文森特·塞巴斯蒂安 (Rear Adm. Vincent Sebastien) 表示：“军事指挥官的‘适当控制’始终能够确保人类的作用，这个概念的范围会根据系统的重要性和作战环境而有所不同。”
联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯和红十字国际委员会主席米里亚娜·斯波尔贾里奇在八月份的一份联合声明中警告说：“我们现在正危险地接近跨越道德红线：机器自动瞄准人类。”
但分析人士表示，日内瓦的讨论虽然很重要，但只会触及问题的一部分。
如今，人工智能在分析和定位中的使用越来越多，导致人类的作用逐渐减弱。
里克利表示，日内瓦议程的范围“非常狭窄”。
“它未能涵盖战场上人工智能的全部问题”——人工智能的使用正在扩大的领域，特别是在目标生成方面。
他说，这一点在今年美以对伊朗的战争中就可见一斑，“美国人每天对伊朗境内的目标进行攻击多达 1000 个”。
“目标定位和决策支持系统存在许多问题和不可接受的风险，”德鲁西-罗什贡德补充道。 “这场辩论的一部分涉及已经广泛部署的系统

‘A moral red line’? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution - The Japan Times
‘A moral red line’? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution
A model of the TI-04 drone is displayed during the opening of the new production facility for autonomous interceptor drones by TYTAN Technologies in Munich on Nov. 9. | AFP-JIJI
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Paris – Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence are set to revolutionize warfare but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology.
A conference starting Monday at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some.
But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons.
Here is a look at three key questions ahead of the conference.
Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy.
Autonomous weapons have long existed. An anti-personnel mine “is an autonomous weapon in the sense that it explodes when someone steps on it,” said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the Centre for Geopolitics of Technology at the French Institute of International Relations.
But with the proliferation of AI-enhanced drones, such weapons are now “capable of selecting and engaging a target that was not predetermined, adapting to their environment without human intervention,” said Rickli.
So the critical issue for potential regulators lies in determining the level of human control over the decision to employ such a weapon.
The United States refers to “appropriate levels of human judgment” in the use of autonomous weapons.
France maintains that a human must remain in the decision-making loop and bans “lethal autonomous weapons systems” (LAWS) but permits “partially autonomous” systems, known as PLAWS.
“The human role is always ensured through what is termed ’appropriate control’ by a military commander — a concept that varies in scope depending on the system’s criticality and the operational context,” said Rear Adm. Vincent Sebastien, deputy director of the French defense ministry’s Agency for Defence Artificial Intelligence (AMIAD).
“We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, and International Committee of the Red Cross President Mirjana Spoljaric warned in a joint statement in August.
But analysts said the Geneva discussions, while important, will touch only part of the issue.
Today, the diminishing role of humans is being driven by the growing use of AI in analysis and targeting.
Rickli said the scope of the agenda in Geneva is “very narrow.”
“It fails to encompass the full range of issues surrounding AI on the battlefield” — an area where its use is expanding, particularly in target generation.
He said this was seen in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran this year “where the Americans engaged as many as 1,000 targets per day” inside Iran.
“There are a host of problems and unacceptable risks associated with targeting and decision-support systems,” added de Roucy-Rochegonde. “Part of this debate concerns systems that are already widely deployed on the battlefield.”
“What kind of human supervision is required to ensure that the operator is genuinely exercising their own judgment rather than simply providing a rubber stamp for the machine’s recommendations?” she asked.
The autonomous weapons to be discussed in Geneva are not yet in widespread use, although analysts have noted that they have been deployed by Russia in its invasion of Ukraine as well as U.S. attacks in Iran.
But the spread is inevitable.
“Autonomy will very quickly become a reality on the battlefield,” warned Sebastien.
“Autonomous weapon systems are not part of a distant future — a race towards greater autonomy in weapons systems is already well underway,” Guterres and Spoljaric said in their statement.
Yet significant doubts and dangers remain, Dario Amodei, head of the AI giant Anthropic, warned this year: “Today, frontier AI systems are simply not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons.”
But ultimately, the incentive for major powers is too strong.
Swarms of autonomous drones — which “aim to neutralize an adversary through saturation” — would be highly effective, and some states view them as a crucial strategic advantage, said Rickli.
In January, the Chinese defense ministry described swarms of autonomous drones as the “new face of warfare.”
“In an era of sharp military competition, the first state to normalize fully autonomous lethal strikes will reset expectations for everyone else,” said Gerald Mako, a research affiliate of Cambridge University in the Small Wars Journal.

中新社罗马11月14日电 台湾政府已向意大利北部城市克雷莫纳捐赠10万欧元（110,520美元），以支持8月风暴后的重建工作。
台湾驻意大利米兰代表处处长林赞南周四（当地时间）出席在克雷莫纳市政厅举行的捐赠仪式，由市长安德里亚·维尔吉利奥主持。
出席仪式的还有副市长 Francesca Romagnoli、市议会主席 Luciano Pizzetti、市秘书 Gabriella Di Girolamo 和市议会第四生产活动委员会主席 Marcello Ventura。
林在致辞中表示，同样面临极端天气和台风等自然灾害的台湾，对克雷莫纳的经历感同身受。
他表示，这10万欧元的捐款旨在帮助该市灾后重建。
林补充说，极端天气不分国界，希望意大利支持台湾有意义地参与联合国气候变化框架公约（UNFCCC），以便双方共同应对气候变化。
维尔吉里奥代表克雷莫纳及其居民感谢台湾政府的慷慨支持，并表示风暴损坏了学校、房屋和企业。
他表示，这笔捐款将用于恢复公共绿地，包括重新种植树木和修复受损的公园和花园。
文图拉表示，此次捐赠是台湾与克雷莫纳加强合作的具体成果，展示了国际友谊如何转化为对当地社区的切实援助。
UNFCCC第31届联合国气候变化框架公约缔约方大会(COP31)将于2026年星期一至11月20日在土耳其安塔利亚举行。台湾不是UNFCCC缔约方，无法正式参与谈判。

Taiwan donates 100,000 euros to Italian city for post-storm reconstruction
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Lin Tsan-nan (left), director general of Taiwan's representative office, and Cremona City Mayor Andrea Virgilio. Photo courtesy of Taiwan's representative office in Milan, Italy
Rome, Nov. 14 (CNA) Taiwan's government has donated 100,000 euros (US$110,520) to Cremona, a city in northern Italy, to support reconstruction efforts following a storm in August.
Lin Tsan-nan (林讚南), director general of Taiwan's representative office in Milan, Italy, attended a donation ceremony on Thursday (local time) at Cremona City Hall, hosted by Mayor Andrea Virgilio.
Also attending the ceremony were Deputy Mayor Francesca Romagnoli, City Council President Luciano Pizzetti, City Secretary Gabriella Di Girolamo and Marcello Ventura, president of the City Council's Fourth Commission on Productive Activities.
Lin said in his speech that Taiwan, which also faces natural disasters caused by extreme weather and typhoons, can empathize with Cremona's experience.
He said the 100,000 euro donation was intended to help the city rebuild after the disaster.
Lin added that extreme weather knows no national boundary and that he hoped Italy would support Taiwan's meaningful participation in the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) so the two sides could jointly address climate change.
Virgilio thanked Taiwan's government on behalf of Cremona and its residents for the generous support, saying the storm had damaged schools, homes and businesses.
He said the donation would be used to restore public green spaces, including replanting trees and repairing damaged parks and gardens.
Ventura said the donation was a concrete outcome of efforts to strengthen cooperation between Taiwan and Cremona, demonstrating how international friendship could translate into tangible assistance for local communities.
UNFCCC's 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) is to be held in Antalya, Turkey, from Monday to Nov. 20, 2026. Taiwan is not a party to the UNFCCC and is excluded from formal participation in the negotiations.

content:
资料照片：委内瑞拉卡比马斯(Cabimas)，马拉开波湖畔的一台抽油机。(2026年1月27日)
美国国务院星期四(11月12日)发布一份报告称，今年前九个月，国务院经手了超过120亿美元来自委内瑞拉石油及其他资源的收入，并将这笔资金几乎全部返还给了委内瑞拉。
华盛顿通过一套金融机制来管理这些收入。该机制是在2026年1月尼古拉斯·马杜罗(Nicolás Maduro)被捕后建立的。这些资金的管理属于与代总统德尔西·罗德里格斯(Delcy Rodríguez)领导的过渡政府所达成协议的一部分。
根据协议条款，委内瑞拉出售石油及其他资源所得的资金将进入一个由美国财政部管理的账户，这些资金的用途须经美国财政部批准。
根据该安排，资金被存入一个由美方管理的账户中。随后，委内瑞拉中央银行会提出领取这些资金的请求，而美方官员则需决定是否予以放行。
报告称，该机制旨在促进委内瑞拉自然资源收益的透明度、问责制以及负责任的管理。
美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio) 本星期在巴黎举行的七国集团(G7)外长会议期间向记者发表谈话时，强调了委内瑞拉政治过渡进程所取得的进展，并表示美方期望在建立新的司法和选举机构方面，能遵守关键的时间节点。
“所以，我认为我们进展良好。我们必须持续推进，以确保能够遵守这些时间期限。”卢比奥说。
这位美国最高外交官员解释道，该计划要求在12月中旬前任命新的最高法院大法官，随后不久将组建一个新的选举委员会。
卢比奥还强调了扩大委内瑞拉国际关系对于支持该国复苏的重要性。
“我们认为他们不仅能为委内瑞拉的复苏作出很多的贡献，而且在我看来，委内瑞拉越是多与俄罗斯、中国和伊朗以外的世界接触，就越能在经济和社会层面取得复苏进展。”卢比奥说。
这份由毕马威会计师事务所(KPMG)撰写的报告指出，截至2026年9月，大部分拨付的资金都是通过委内瑞拉商业银行开展的外汇交易进入该国经济。报告并未说明谁最终接受了这些资金。
此外，另有约1.33亿美元被调拨于向商品和服务供应商进行直接支付，以满足委内瑞拉过渡政府的运营及行政需求。
根据这一报告，2026年1月3日至9月30日期间，存入托管账户的资金超过122.6亿美元，其中121.1亿美元已拨付。
截至9月30日，另有1.6856亿美元仍由美国代管，未来委内瑞拉中央银行代表过渡政府提出后续的转移请求后再作授权释放。

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

「2026 FunPark童書星創獎」舉行總決賽暨頒獎典禮，第2排左5起依序為教育部學特司副司長許嘉倩、中華電信董事長簡志誠、總經理林榮賜、法務部保護司視察歐惠婷、中華電信執行副總暨智趣王董事長林文智。（中華電提供）中央社記者江明晏傳真 115年11月14日
（中央社記者江明晏台北14日電）中華電信與子公司智趣王主辦的「2026 FunPark童書星創獎」自2013年創辦以來，今年參賽作品數量創歷年新高，中華電信董事長簡志誠表示，將持續串聯教育、科技與產業資源，深化數位平權與原創人才培育，為台灣數位內容產業注入新動能。
由中華電信與子公司智趣王數位科技主辦的「2026 FunPark童書星創獎」今天舉行總決賽暨頒獎典禮，今年共有7365人報名、3523件作品參賽，創下歷年新高。
中華電表示，「FunPark童書星創獎」14年來累計吸引8萬297人報名、2萬2518件作品參賽，頒出570個獎項，培育近475名小小繪本作家及繪本創作新秀，持續結合數位科技、教育與出版資源，打造多元創作舞台。
中華電信表示，自2016年起，連續11年攜手教育部、法務部及衛生福利部推動反毒教育。今年持續透過「兒童創作組」與「反毒創作組」，鼓勵孩子從生活經驗與社會議題發想，將反毒觀念融入數位繪本創作。
2025年專業創作組金獎得主吳政倫，以獲獎作品「小小點點」與小魯文化合作出版，展現創作成果從數位競賽走向實體出版的可能。
中華電信董事長簡志誠表示，「FunPark童書星創獎」不僅鼓勵兒少發揮想像力，更透過數位平台、專業課程及出版合作，協助創作人才從競賽走向實際應用。未來將持續串聯教育、科技與產業資源，深化數位平權與原創人才培育，為台灣數位內容產業注入新動能。（編輯：林克倫、萬淑彰）1151114

美国空军改变了战略前景，宣布了新的《部队设计 2026》，取代了 2024 年制定的先前标准。
一位空军发言人告诉《军事时报》：“美国空军设计 2026 提供了一个持久的框架，用于识别作战问题、塑造能力发展和告知现代化优先事项，确保空军不断发展其作战方式，并部署一支制胜力量。”
“原力设计是一份机密文件，因此没有可发布的副本，”发言人说。
2024 年 10 月，空军宣布将遵循“单一部队设计”文件中规定的指导，该文件由时任参谋长戴维·奥​​尔文上将签署，据称该文件是空军现代化计划的“北极星”。
它引入了三个不同的任务领域，有效地划分了针对无人机系统的防空系统。 2024年文件将空军的无人机杀伤能力分别分为近程、远程和洲际防御三类。
尽管新的 Force Design 2026 文件属于机密，但该服务的发布暗示了一些关键变化。
据称，新的战略展望“更明确地阐明了变革的必要性以及空军所需的能力”，以击败尖端技术。
报告将传感器、网络和人工智能列为对防空系统产生迅速影响的因素。
部队现代化副参谋长兼首席现代化官克里斯·尼米中将在新闻稿中表示：“新技术正在实现几年前难以想象的神奇能力，但这些技术也威胁到了我们历史上产生空中力量的一些方式。”
该文件还指出，“未来空军”将寻求将自主性、传感器以及指挥和控制与飞机整合起来，以“产生效果”，特别强调能够在被拒绝的环境中同步执行任务。
换句话说，新的重点是传感器和软件，而不是拦截和摧毁单个无人机。
空军参谋长肯·威尔斯巴赫上将在军种声明中表示，新的部队设计“体现了空军方法的根本转变”。
威尔斯巴赫说：“新技术正在实现几年前无法想象的神奇能力，但这些技术也威胁到了我们历史上产生空中力量的一些方式。”

An F-15 refuels. (Alexis Morris/U.S. Air Force)
The U.S. Air Force has changed its strategic outlook, announcing a new Force Design 2026 that replaces its previous standards established in 2024.
“The U.S. Air Force Force Design 2026 provides an enduring framework for identifying operational problems, shaping capability development, and informing modernization priorities – ensuring the Air Force evolves how it fights, and that it fields a winning force,” an Air Force spokesperson told Military Times.
“The Force Design is a classified document so there is no releasable copy,” the spokesperson said.
In October 2024, the service announced it would follow guidance set out in a “One Force Design” document, signed by then-Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin and said to be the “North Star” for Air Force modernization plans.
It introduced three distinct mission areas, effectively divvying up air defenses against unmanned aircraft systems. The Air Force’s drone-killing capabilities were classified in the 2024 document in categories of short-range, long-range and intercontinental defense, respectively.
Although the new Force Design 2026 document is classified, the service’s release hints at some key changes.
The new strategic outlook is said to be “more sharply articulating the need for change, and the capabilities the Air Force needs” to defeat sophisticated technology.
It lists sensors, networks and artificial intelligence as having had a rapid impact on air defenses.
“New technologies are enabling fantastic capabilities that were unimaginable just a few years ago, but those same technologies threaten some of the ways we have historically generated airpower,” Lt. Gen. Chris Niemi, deputy chief of staff for Force Modernization and Chief Modernization Officer, said in the release.
In another nod to where air defense is going, the document also notes that the “future Air Force” will seek to integrate autonomy, sensors and command and control with aircraft to “generate effects,” with a particular emphasis on being able to perform synchronously in denied environments.
In other words, a new focus on sensors and software is at play rather than on intercepting and destroying individual drones.
Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach said in the service’s statement that the new Force Design “presents a fundamental shift” in the Air Force’s approach.
“New technologies are enabling fantastic capabilities that were unimaginable just a few years ago, but those same technologies threaten some of the ways we have historically generated airpower,” Wilsbach said.
Zita Ballinger Fletcher previously served as editor of Military History Quarterly and Vietnam magazines and as the historian of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. She holds an M.A. with distinction in military history.

summary: 黄仁勋退出 Nvidia 对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 - 大西洋理事会东亚科技与创新美国和加拿大 黄仁勋退出 Nvidia 对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 有很多事情需要处理。周四，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情。但其影响超出了该人和他的前公司的范围，该公司因其领先的计算机处理器而成为人工智能（AI）繁荣的关键引擎。下面，大西洋理事会的专家们
content:
黄仁勋退出英伟达对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么 - 大西洋理事会
东亚科技与创新美国和加拿大
黄仁勋退出英伟达对华盛顿、华尔街和北京意味着什么
有很多事情需要处理。周四，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括与一名疑似中国间谍的婚外情。但其影响超出了该人和他的前公司的范围，该公司因其领先的计算机处理器而成为人工智能（AI）繁荣的关键引擎。下面，大西洋理事会专家将探讨人事变动将如何影响美国政策、全球市场等。
今天为您带来的专家反应
Trisha Ray：地质技术中心副主任兼常驻研究员
Graham Brookie (@GrahamBrookie)：技术项目和战略副总裁
Jessie Yin：地缘经济中心副主任
Kenton Thibaut (@kentonthibaut)：数字取证研究实验室中国高级研究员
Trisha 解释道，英伟达的先进芯片是“美国减缓对手人工智能能力的关键”。但这种优势也是“单点故障”，因为美国的出口管制力度取决于少数公司及其内部人员的安全措施。
格雷厄姆认为，这一事件并不是美国情报部门的失败，“而是美国政府在管理国家安全威胁方面协调和政策执行方面的更广泛的失败”。由于人工智能行业容易受到知识产权盗窃和直接攻击，华盛顿在风险管理和出口政策执行方面“措手不及”。
“对于投资者来说，将英伟达的成功与黄仁勋分开是很困难的，而对于华盛顿来说，将英伟达与国家安全分开也几乎同样困难，”杰西说。她现在认为国会有机会对该公司对国家安全的影响进行更大的监督，并加强半导体出口管制。肯顿指出，国会对芯片限制的势头不断增强，例如《人工智能监督法案》、《芯片安全法案》和《匹配法案》。
展望未来，特丽莎敦促政府加强审查。她认为，“鉴于支持美国人工智能领先地位的公司很少，政策制定者应该认真考虑政府的直接监督”，例如对公司领导层及其主要客户的安全许可要求，以及对出口实体的安全审计作为出口许可证的先决条件。
由于英伟达股价下跌，今天市场小幅下跌。黄仁勋的离开让投资者怀疑，如果没有这位已成为其成功代名词的领导者，英伟达能否维持其主导地位。杰西推测，公司“将在一段时间内不稳定”。
这些股份比英伟达的股价还要高。格雷厄姆警告说，美国经济已经高度依赖于少数人工智能公司的命运，这些公司“也恰好是该国在地缘政治竞争的决定性领域中的主要战略资产”。其中一个失败可能会影响整个美国经济和国家安全生态系统。
除了销售芯片之外，英伟达还成为人工智能热潮的主要融资者——被称为“人工智能中央银行”——投资初创企业并为购买其产品的客户提供支持。杰西表示，未来几个月将展示“英伟达对人工智能需求本身的整合程度如何”。

What Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit means for Washington, Wall Street, and Beijing - Atlantic Council
East Asia Technology & Innovation United States and Canada
What Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit means for Washington, Wall Street, and Beijing
It’s a lot to process. On Thursday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. But the implications extend beyond the man and his former company, a critical engine of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom because of its leading-edge computer processors. Below, Atlantic Council experts work through how the personnel shakeup could impact US policy, global markets, and more.
TODAY’S EXPERT REACTION BROUGHT TO YOU BY
Trisha Ray: Associate director and resident fellow at the GeoTech Center
Graham Brookie (@GrahamBrookie): Vice president for technology programs and strategy
Jessie Yin: Associate director with the GeoEconomics Center
Kenton Thibaut (@kentonthibaut): Senior resident China fellow at the Digital Forensic Research Lab
Nvidia’s advanced chips are “the linchpin of the United States’ leverage in slowing down the AI capabilities of its adversaries,” Trisha explains. But that advantage is also “a single point of failure,” since US export controls are only as strong as the security practices of a handful of companies and people within them.
Graham sees the incident not as a failure in US intelligence, “but rather a broader failure of coordination and policy execution in how the US government manages national security threats.” With the AI industry vulnerable to intellectual property theft and direct targeting, Washington was “caught flat footed” in risk management and export policy enforcement.
“As difficult as it is for investors to separate Nvidia’s success from Jensen Huang, it has become nearly as difficult for Washington to separate Nvidia from national security,” Jessie argues. She now sees an opening for Congress to exert greater oversight of the company’s impact on national security and tighten semiconductor export controls. Kenton points to growing momentum in Congress behind chip restrictions such as the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act.
Going forward, Trisha urges greater government scrutiny. “Given how few companies underpin the US AI lead, policymakers should seriously consider direct government oversight,” she argues, such as security clearance–like requirements for company leadership and their major customers, as well as security audits of the exporting entities as a precondition for export licenses.
Markets were down slightly today, as Nvidia shares took a hit. Huang’s departure has investors wondering if Nvidia can sustain its dominance without the leader who became a synonym to its success. The company is “going to be unsteady for a while,” Jessie surmises.
The stakes are higher than Nvidia’s stock price alone. The US economy is already highly exposed to the fortunes of a handful of AI companies that “also happen to be the country’s primary strategic assets in a determinative domain of geopolitical competition,” Graham warns. A failure at one could reverberate across the US economy and national security ecosystem.
Beyond selling chips, Nvidia has become a major financier of the AI boom—known as “the central bank of AI”—investing in startups and supporting customers that buy its products. Jessie says that the coming months will show “how integral Nvidia has become to AI demand itself.”
Sign up to receive rapid insight in your inbox from Atlantic Council experts on global events as they unfold.
Ahead of a planned meeting next week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Beijing warned Washington earlier today against further technology restrictions, Kenton notes.
Huang had long opposed strict export controls and was able to speak with both Trump and Xi. “But with Huang out of the picture, there is potentially more political leeway to push forward on a more hawkish approach,” Kenton says.
Jessie adds that the scandal has “permanently damaged the company’s credibility to push back on export controls,” relationships aside.
But tougher controls could invite retaliation, Kenton warns. “Beijing could answer new restrictions with curbs on critical minerals or probes of other American firms,” potentially complicating the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting.

title: Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week
zh_title: 发射预览：Starship、Vulcan 和 Electron 计划在繁忙的一周发射
summary: 来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭提供机密有效载荷
content:
来自四个国家的七枚火箭将于本周发射。星际飞船将尝试其迄今为止最重要的任务，而猎鹰 9 号将为美国太空军发射一对机密有效载荷。联合发射联盟计划让 Vulcan 执行其返回飞行任务，而 Electron 则将完成第 100 次任务，具有里程碑意义。在国际上，中国和韩国将分别发射未知的有效载荷和演示任务。猎鹰 9 号 | USSF-627（“R-5”）本周首次发射将由猎鹰 9 号火箭为美国太空军 (USSF) 提供机密有效载荷。该任务被指定为 USSF-627，最初计划于 11 月 8 日星期日发射。猎鹰 9 号现定于太平洋标准时间 11 月 9 日星期一晚上 7:07（世界标准时间 10 月 10 日 03:07）从范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 的 4 号东部太空发射综合体 (SLC-4E) 起飞，距太平洋标准时间晚上 11:03 (07:03) 的窗口期已过去四分钟。 UTC 时间 11 月 10 日）。由于有效载荷的机密性质，卫星的确切数量尚不清楚。一些指标表明，基于猎鹰 9 号第二级的降落区，星盾将进行发射。 Starshield是为美国政府打造的Starlink版本，其主要客户是USSF、国家侦察办公室和太空发展局。范登堡太空部队基地 4E 号航天发射场发射台上的猎鹰 9 号火箭。
（图片来源：SpaceX）Falcon 9 是一款两级、70 m 高、部分可重复使用的火箭，第一级使用九个 Merlin 1D 海平面发动机，第二级使用单个真空优化的 Merlin 1D。Falcon 9 的第一级降落在自主无人机船上或着陆点，其整流罩在飞行后回收并重复使用。两个阶段都使用液体煤油和液氧作为推进剂。助推器 B1103 将在其第七次飞行中支持这项任务。此前，该助推器已支持 NROL-179、第一批传输层 A 和 E 以及三个星链任务的发射。猎鹰 9 号将搭乘 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”着陆。米尔 |演示飞行 11 月 10 日星期二，韩国计划发射韩国军方小型卫星运载火箭和平号的第二次飞行。继 2023 年 12 月进行了不包括第二级的试飞之后，此次发射将是全尺寸火箭的首次轨道飞行。启动窗口于 05:00 UTC 开始，并延长至 09:00 UTC。和平号是一款四级固体燃料运载火箭，第四级采用液体燃料，可实现精确入轨。 2023 年 12 月飞行的版本能够运载 700 公斤至近地轨道，该版本疑似能够运载 1,000 公斤左右。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 11 日星期三，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭计划从酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空。
目前，发射计划于 11:40 UTC 进行，距离 11:32 UTC 开启并持续到 12:05 UTC 的窗口还有 8 分钟的时间。CZ-2D 将向轨道发射未知有效载荷。 CZ-2D 是一款两级、41 米高的运载火箭，能够向近地轨道 (LEO) 发射 3,500 公斤的重量。 CZ-2D的第一级和第二级均由四氧化二氮和不对称二甲肼提供动力，这两种推进剂都是自燃推进剂。周三的发射将是 CZ-2D 的第 107 次发射，也是 2026 年的第六次发射。快舟 11 |有效载荷未知本周第二个也是最后一个预定的中国任务

【原文 English Original】
Seven rockets from four countries are set to launch this week. Starship is set to attempt its most consequential mission yet, while Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of classified payloads for the United States Space Force. The United Launch Alliance is scheduled to fly Vulcan on its return-to-flight mission, and Electron is set to reach a milestone 100th mission. Internationally, China and South Korea are set to launch an unknown payload and a demonstration mission, respectively. Falcon 9 | USSF-627 (“R-5”) The first launch of the week will feature Falcon 9 delivering a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). The mission, designated USSF-627, was initially scheduled to launch on Sunday, Nov. 8. Falcon 9 is now set to take off from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) on Monday, Nov. 9, at 7:07 PM PST (03:07 UTC on Nov. 10), four minutes into a window that extends until 11:03 PM PST (07:03 UTC on Nov. 10). Due to the classified nature of the payload, the exact quantity of satellites is unknown. Some indicators suggest a Starshield launch, based on drop zones for Falcon 9’s second stage. Starshield is a version of Starlink built for the United States government, with its primary customers being the USSF, National Reconnaissance Office, and the Space Development Agency. A Falcon 9 on the launch pad at Space Launch Complex-4E on Vandenberg Space Force Base. (Credit: SpaceX) Falcon 9 is a two-stage, 70 m-tall, partially reusable rocket that uses nine Merlin 1D sea-level engines on its first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Merlin 1D on its second stage. Falcon 9’s first stage lands either aboard an autonomous droneship or at a landing site, with its fairings being recovered and reused after flight. Both stages utilize liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen as propellants. Booster B1103 will be supporting this mission on its seventh flight. Previously, this booster has supported the launches of NROL-179, Tranche 1 Transport Layers A and E, and three Starlink missions. Falcon 9 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Mir | Demo Flight On Tuesday, Nov. 10, South Korea is set to launch the second flight of Mir, the South Korean military’s small satellite launch vehicle. This launch is set to be the first orbital flight of the full-scale rocket, following a test flight in December 2023 that did not include the second stage. The launch window opens at 05:00 UTC and extends until 09:00 UTC. Mir is a four-stage, solid-fuel launch vehicle with a liquid-fueled fourth stage for precise orbital insertion. The version that flew in December 2023 was capable of 700 kg to LEO, with this version suspected to be capable of around 1,000 kg. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload On Wednesday, Nov. 11, a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) rocket is scheduled to launch out of the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The launch is currently scheduled for 11:40 UTC, eight minutes into a window that opens at 11:32 UTC and extends until 12:05 UTC. CZ-2D will deliver an unknown payload into orbit. CZ-2D is a two-stage, 41 m-tall launch vehicle capable of delivering 3,500 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). CZ-2D’s first and second stages are both powered by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine, both hypergolic propellants. Wednesday’s launch will be the 107th overall for CZ-2D, and sixth in 2026. Kuaizhou 11 | Unknown Payload The second and final scheduled Chinese mission of the week will see a Kuaizhou 11 rocket launch on Thursday, Nov. 12. Liftoff is set for 19:50 UTC from Site 95A at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, during a 45-minute launch window. Kuaizhou 11 is a four-stage Chinese rocket manufactured by the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation. Standing 25.3 m tall, the rocket can loft 1,500 kg to LEO with a liftoff thrust of 1,250 kN. This mission will be the eighth overall Kuaizhou 11 mission and the fourth of 2026. Vulcan VC6L | Amazon Leo (LV-01) United Launch Alliance’s (ULA) Vulcan rocket is set to launch on Friday, Nov. 13, from Space Launch Complex 41 (SLC-41) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The 30-minute launch window opens at 12:54 PM EST (17:54 UTC). This will be the first flight of Vulcan in over nine months, following the ejection of one of Vulcan’s GEM-63XL solid rocket boosters at T+69 seconds on the USSF-87 mission. Flying aboard Vulcan will be a stack of 40 Amazon Leo satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite internet constellation, a rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. A ULA Vulcan (USSF-87) sits next to a SpaceX Crew Dragon (Crew-12). (Credit: Tyler Gray for NSF) Vulcan is a two-stage launch vehicle with a range of launch configurations. Vulcan’s first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines built by Blue Origin, running on liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. Its second stage, Centaur V, is powered by twin RL10C engines running on liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. Centaur V can be configured as Centaur LEO, High Energy, or Endurance. Vulcan can also be configured with solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with options ranging from zero to two, four, or six boosters. The payload is encapsulated by either a short (15.5 m) or a long (21.3 m) fairing. Vulcan will debut the Vulcan VC6L variant, designated by six solid boosters and the long fairing option. Vulcan will debut the LEO-optimized Centaur V, which is 1.94 m smaller than the existing Centaur V High Energy, which has flown on all previous Vulcan launches. Additionally, this flight is a certification flight of this Vulcan configuration for the United States Space Force. Amazon Leo (LV-01) will be the first of 38 scheduled for Vulcan and the fifth overall mission for Vulcan. Starship | Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 Pending regulatory approval, Starship is set to fly its next, and most significant, mission no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 PM CST (22:45 UTC). The launch window extends until 6:00 PM CST (00:00 UTC on Nov. 14). Flight 15 will feature two notable events: the first booster-catch attempt since Flight 8, following stage separation, and the first attempt to catch the ship, roughly 22 hours after liftoff. Starship is a two-stage, super-heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of lofting an estimated 100 tonnes. The first stage, named Super Heavy, features 33 Raptor 3 engines, running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. The second stage, named Starship, features six Raptor 3 engines, three sea-level and three vacuum-optimized, also running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Flying on Flight 15 will be Ship 42 and Booster 22, both on their first flights. Flight 15 is expected to deliver 26 Starlink v3 satellites to LEO. Like Flight 14, three of these satellites will feature imaging capabilities for imaging the heat shield of Starship in orbit. Flight 15 will be the 15th full-stack launch of Starship and the fourth for the system’s V3 configuration. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (“R-6”) Falcon 9 is set to fly again on Friday, Nov. 13, from VSFB with another USSF mission. The designation for this flight is USSF-317. The launch window opens at 8:09 PM PST (04:09 UTC on Nov. 14), and lasts for four hours. This mission will fly another unknown quantity of presumed Starshield satellites to LEO. Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its 11th flight. This booster has previously supported NROL-105, USSF-385, and eight Starlink missions. B1100 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Electron during its 95th launch “Happily Ever Faster.” Credit: Rocket Lab) Electron | The Mountain God Rises The last scheduled launch of the week will see Rocket Lab’s Electron launch from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 05:30 UTC. This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation (SAR). SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Electron is a two-stage small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO and 200 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission — a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017. In addition, this mission will serve as the 269th orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. ( Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

title: Don't Let China's Espionage Become America's Own Goal
zh_title: 不要让中国的间谍活动成为美国自己的目标
summary: 别让中国的间谍活动成为美国自己的目标博客 | 2026 年 11 月 12 日 | ITIF跳到内容 不要让中国的间谍活动成为美国自己的目标 所谓的针对英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的中国情报行动最终可能使美国付出的代价远远超过中国的代价。英伟达失去了长期担任的首席执行官，美国投资者损失了数千亿美元的市值，美国决策者正在考虑对芯片出口实施新的限制，这可能会进一步损害美国科技公司的利益。美国有合法的
content:
别让中国的间谍活动成为美国自己的目标博客 | 2026 年 11 月 12 日 | ITIF跳到内容
不要让中国的间谍活动成为美国自己的目标
据称中国针对英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的情报行动最终可能给美国带来的损失远远超过中国的损失。英伟达失去了长期担任的首席执行官，美国投资者损失了数千亿美元的市值，美国决策者正在考虑对芯片出口实施新的限制，这可能会进一步损害美国科技公司的利益。美国在阻止中国军方获取先进人工智能芯片方面拥有合法利益，但它不应该允许所谓的中国间谍活动推动其采取削弱本国半导体行业的政策。
这场争议始于有报道称，美国情报机构怀疑新加坡 Megaspeed International 前高管 Alice Huang 为中国国家安全部工作。据报道，调查人员怀疑她与黄仁勋建立了关系，以收集有关英伟达及其运营的信息。黄仁勋承认与她有婚外关系，并分别面临与向他汇报的英伟达员工发生另一段关系的报道。 11月12日，英伟达宣布黄仁勋在领导公司33年后辞去首席执行官一职，并任命首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)为临时首席执行官。
这些指控引发了严重的国家安全担忧。据报道，Megaspeed 购买了价值约 48 亿美元的 Nvidia 硬件。美国当局怀疑该公司正在帮助中国客户规避对先进人工智能芯片的限制。据报道，在 2024 年对马来西亚设施的检查中，商务部官员发现 Nvidia 硬件仍然装在盒子里，而不是安装在数据中心，引发了人们对这些设备可能运往中国的担忧。
这些指控仍在调查中。 Megaspeed 否认有不当行为，表示正在配合美国当局的检查，并委托一家美国律师事务所对其芯片库存和出口管制做法进行独立审查。新加坡当局也在调查该公司。
如果这些指控属实，中国将取得重大成就：扰乱美国最重要的科技公司之一，并有可能获得敏感的商业信息。即使没有证据表明英伟达的商业机密或国家安全信息遭到泄露，损失也已经是巨大的。英伟达失去了长期的领导者，其股东看到数千亿美元的市值蒸发，该公司在服务国际客户的能力方面面临着新的不确定性。直接的经济成本落在了一家美国公司及其投资者身上。
中国自己的半导体战略使这一情况尤其具有启发性。北京希望减少对美国技术的依赖，建立国内芯片产业。它越来越多地利用采购限制和政府指导来引导中国企业转向国内加工商。例如，据报道，2025 年 11 月，中国当局指示国家资助的数据中心使用国产人工智能芯片。 2026 年 1 月，中国当局也不鼓励购买 Nvidia 的 H200 处理器，尽管中国公司对此表现出强烈兴趣。

【原文 English Original】
Don't Let China's Espionage Become America's Own Goal | Blogs | Nov 12, 2026 | ITIFSkip to content
Don't Let China's Espionage Become America's Own Goal
An alleged Chinese intelligence operation targeting Nvidia’s now-former CEO Jensen Huang could end up costing the United States far more than it costs China. Nvidia has lost its longtime chief executive, American investors have lost hundreds of billions of dollars in market value, and U.S. policymakers are considering new restrictions on chip exports that could further undermine American technology companies. The United States has a legitimate interest in preventing the Chinese military from acquiring advanced AI chips, but it should not allow an alleged Chinese espionage operation to push it toward policies that weaken its own semiconductor industry.
The controversy began with reports that U.S. intelligence agencies suspected Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, of working for China's Ministry of State Security. Investigators reportedly suspected she had cultivated a relationship with Jensen Huang to gather information about Nvidia and its operations. Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with her and separately faced reports of another relationship with an Nvidia employee who reported to him. On November 12, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as CEO after 33 years leading the company and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
The allegations raise serious national security concerns. Megaspeed reportedly purchased approximately $4.8 billion in Nvidia hardware. U.S. authorities suspected that the company was helping Chinese customers circumvent restrictions on advanced AI chips. During a 2024 inspection of a Malaysian facility, Commerce Department officials reportedly found Nvidia hardware still packed in boxes rather than installed in data centers, raising concerns that the equipment might be destined for China.
These allegations remain under investigation. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, says it is cooperating with inspections by U.S. authorities, and has commissioned an independent review by a U.S. law firm of its chip inventory and export-control practices. Singaporean authorities are also investigating the company.
If the allegations are true, China will have achieved something significant: disrupting one of America's most important technology companies and potentially gaining access to sensitive commercial information. Even without evidence that Nvidia's trade secrets or national security information were compromised, the damage is already substantial. Nvidia has lost its longtime leader, its shareholders have seen hundreds of billions of dollars in market value evaporate, and the company faces renewed uncertainty about its ability to serve international customers. The immediate economic costs are falling on an American company and its investors.
China's own semiconductor strategy makes the situation particularly revealing. Beijing wants to reduce dependence on American technology and build a domestic chip industry. It has increasingly used procurement restrictions and government guidance to steer Chinese companies toward domestic processors. In November 2025, for example, Chinese authorities reportedly directed state-funded data centers to use domestically produced AI chips. In January 2026, Chinese authorities also discouraged purchases of Nvidia's H200 processors, despite strong interest from Chinese companies.
Yet Chinese companies continue to seek access to Nvidia's most powerful processors, including through overseas data centers. This reflects a distinction between Beijing's long-term industrial ambitions and the immediate commercial interests of Chinese technology companies. China wants its domestic chipmakers to capture the market, but its AI developers still benefit from access to the best available hardware.
Congress now risks helping China achieve its goals. One proposal, the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), would expand export controls to cover foreign access to restricted U.S. technology through cloud computing services. The legislation addresses a legitimate concern: Chinese companies could potentially rent computing capacity overseas even when they cannot legally purchase the underlying chips. But an overly broad law could also create uncertainty for legitimate international cloud services and impose new compliance costs on American technology companies.
The AI OVERWATCH Act and Chip Security Act would go further. The AI OVERWATCH Act would require licenses for certain advanced-chip exports to countries of concern and give Congress advance notice of proposed sales, with an opportunity to block them through a joint resolution. That process could make access to U.S. chips subject to greater political uncertainty, even for transactions that meet existing export-control requirements. The Chip Security Act would require security mechanisms to help verify whether exported chips have been diverted, potentially including location trackers, on-site audits, or legal attestations. Such measures could help detect illicit transfers, but they could also raise concerns among legitimate international customers about monitoring, data security, and government access to information about their computing infrastructure. Both bills risk making U.S. technology less attractive to customers who have other options.
The United States should strengthen enforcement against companies and individuals that knowingly divert restricted chips. It should also improve verification of end users and investigate suspicious transactions. But Congress should be careful about creating new restrictions that unnecessarily limit legitimate commercial activity.
American semiconductor leadership depends heavily on private-sector investment in research and development. Nvidia and other U.S. chipmakers spend billions developing successive generations of increasingly powerful processors. International sales generate revenue that supports this investment, helps companies achieve economies of scale, and finances future innovation. Overly restricting access to the Chinese market would weaken an important source of commercial demand while giving Chinese competitors more opportunities to improve their products and gain market share.
China has an obvious interest in reducing its dependence on American semiconductors. But its own record of economic espionage and trade-secret theft—including documented efforts to steal semiconductor technology—underscores why the allegations deserve serious attention. President Trump should put the issue on the agenda when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen later this month.
Any proven violations should carry meaningful consequences. But a domestic response that hurts American companies, reduces their global markets, and encourages customers to adopt Chinese alternatives would compound the damage. China may have played Jensen Huang. Congress should make sure it does not play into Beijing's hands.

title: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): Implementation of 2027 GCTF Workshop in Eswatini

summary: 资助机会通知 (NOFO)：在斯威士兰举办 2027 GCTF 研讨会 资助机会通知 (NOFO) 在斯威士兰美国台湾学院举办 2027 G CTF 研讨会 机会编号：GCTF-TAIPEI-FY2 7 -00 1 申请截止日期：202 年 11 月 23 日 6 日晚上 11:59 （台北时间） A. 基本资料 1. 概述 资助方式：合作协议。合作协议包括局或大使馆实质性参与项目的计划实施。实质性参与的例子包含在下面的 C.2 节中。项目
