|Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
The blue tsunami of the midterms had barely landed onshore when yet another crisis hit the Trump administration.
On 8 November, Jensen Huang admitted (Opens in new window) to an affair. American intelligence agencies, according (Opens in new window) to the New York Times, have concluded that his mistress is an intelligence asset for China’s Ministry of State Security.
News of the affair shocked markets and regulators. Huang leads Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company that provides the core technology for the West’s technological competition with China. He is deeply tied with the American political apparatus, flying on Air Force One with President Donald Trump for his state visit to Beijing earlier in the year.
Huang’s affair shows a new contradiction at the heart of Washington’s relationship to Silicon Valley. Private executives have more power than ever, while the institutions designed to protect America’s national security haven’t adapted to that change.
National security apparatuses are set up to protect sensitive information. They also protect government decision-makers from influence efforts. The threat against Huang centred on the potential for China to influence Nvidia’s position on selling AI chips to China, rather than control of any particular item of classified information.
The leaders of major American technology firms are becoming structurally decisive figures in American national security policy.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures.
In September, the Pentagon named (Opens in new window) SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk and Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey, alongside former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, as the leaders of Project Meridian. The three will guide the future of American warfare, including acquisition of hundreds of billions of dollars of equipment.
In December 2025, Huang himself told (Opens in new window) CSIS, “our nation’s extraordinary technology industry is part of our national security”. His company, which controls 80–85% of the global market (Opens in new window) for AI chip hardware, positions itself at the vanguard of American power through its grip on the infrastructure.
Silicon Valley executives are giving themselves the job of shaping America’s national security interests rather than delivering what the government requests – in turn influencing how the world sees American power.
US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman speak with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and other business leaders at the US-Saudi Investment Forum, 19 November 2025, at the John F. Kennedy Centre for the Performing Arts in Washington, DC (Daniel Torok/Official White House Photo)
When Musk throttled Starlink access to Ukraine’s soldiers, speculation abounded about who authorised the slowdown between Musk or Trump. The question itself proved the point, that critical decisions may be made on either side of the sector wall.
In Brazil’s presidential election, thousands of protestors gathered outside of Meta’s Sao Paolo office to decry what they saw as the company meddling in their election. In the months prior, the President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign released evidence (Opens in new window) that Meta’s platforms were promoting his opponent’s campaign and limiting Lula’s ability to reach voters. Meta accepted the result but denied any political intention behind it. The reputational damage had been done: a majority of Brazilians believe that American technology poses a risk to their national security.
A Silicon Valley executive who controls technology used by military and intelligence services may not have access to classified information, but can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates.
These companies, deeply tied to the Trump White House and at the vanguard of its definition of American power, are producing consequences that have a significance that rivals that of entire governments.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures. This scandal shows that counterintelligence services need to account for that reality.
The FBI, the key counterintelligence service in the United States, has some efforts in place to protect private industry. They investigate attempts by foreign governments to infiltrate critical companies. Their goal is to protect classified information and hardware that could be stolen and repurposed.
As the public role that these executives play changes, so too does the problem of counterintelligence defence. A Silicon Valley executive who controls the technology used by military and intelligence services around the world may not themselves have access to classified information, but they can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates. These decisions could change what a country is capable of doing, or what technology an adversary is able to access.
Beyond the question of the appropriate counterintelligence protection for figures like Huang, there also comes the question of their political relationships.
Well before the public was made aware, Trump was informed (Opens in new window) about Huang’s relationship, including the intelligence community’s assessment that his mistress was tied to Chinese intelligence. Even after those briefings, Trump continued to speak with Huang and, once the scandal was revealed, publicly defended him.
Even once counterintelligence services adapt to the moving future, they can always be countermanded by chief executives who make political calculations about figures. Trump could have pushed Huang out, but in doing so would have alienated a key political ally, someone central to his strategic competition with China. Huang’s embrace of MAGA has also been helpful to Trump in building a political and economic support base in Silicon Valley.
The decision to do nothing with the information developed by the FBI was a political one, made because Trump saw Huang as indispensable.
This dynamic matters for every country that relies on American technology in both its civilian and public sectors. These new vulnerabilities will not stop at American borders.
The new generation of leaders taking centre stage in the United States must grapple with the seemingly insurmountable power that Silicon Valley has accumulated in the Trump era. Backlash to that very group was part of the substantial rebuke delivered by voters.
In governing, these new leaders from both parties will have to reimagine national security – including counterintelligence – to cover the public power now wielded by private actors.
Cory Alpert is a PhD researcher at the University of Melbourne, where he studies the impact of AI on democracy. Previously, he served in the Biden White House for three years and as the senior adviser to Mayor Steve Benjamin.

外交部：5个盟友支持台湾参加COP31
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月14日电 外交​​部周六表示，台湾五个邦交国在《联合国气候变化框架公约》第31次缔约方会议(COP31)上表示支持台湾参与全球气候努力。
据外交部新闻稿称，上述言论是在 11 月 11 日至 12 日于土耳其安塔利亚举行的 COP31 期间举行的领导人峰会上发表的。这五个国家分别是马绍尔群岛、帕劳、斯威士兰、图瓦卢以及圣基茨和尼维斯。
外交部表示，马绍尔群岛总统希尔达·海涅表示，应该听取包括台湾在内的所有声音，并指出台湾正在努力将经济增长与碳排放脱钩，并增强气候适应能力，因此值得参与讨论。
帕劳总统苏兰吉尔·惠普斯 (Surangel Whipps Jr.) 表示，台湾是重要的合作伙伴，在抗灾、能源转型和粮食安全方面发挥着主导作用。外交部表示，他表示世界需要台湾参与《联合国气候变化框架公约》会议和其他联合国论坛。
外交部表示，斯威士兰总理拉塞尔·德拉米尼赞扬台湾和日本在备灾和抗灾基础设施方面的经验，同时重申支持台湾参与全球气候努力。
图瓦卢总理张泰奥表示，气候变化和气候行动不受政治界限的限制，并赞扬台湾对全球气候努力的贡献。他强调，国际合作中不应排除任何有意愿的伙伴。
圣基茨和尼维斯副总理杰弗里·汉利强调台湾在环境治理、循环经济、气候适应能力、绿色能源和能力建设方面的贡献。
外交部长林佳龙感谢五国的支持，表示台湾将继续与盟友和志同道合的伙伴共同应对气候变化。

Taipei, Nov. 14 (CNA) Five of Taiwan's diplomatic allies have voiced support for its participation in global climate efforts at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said Saturday.
According to a MOFA news release, the remarks were made at the Nov. 11-12 leaders' summit, held as part of the COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. The five countries were the Marshall Islands, Palau, Eswatini, Tuvalu and St. Kitts and Nevis.
Marshall Islands President Hilda C. Heine said all voices, including Taiwan's, should be heard, noting that Taiwan was working to decouple economic growth from carbon emissions and strengthen climate resilience, and therefore deserved to take part in the discussions, MOFA said.
Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr. described Taiwan as an important partner with a leading role in disaster resilience, energy transition and food security. He said the world needed Taiwan's participation in UNFCCC meetings and other United Nations forums, MOFA said.
Eswatini Prime Minister Russell Dlamini praised Taiwan's and Japan's experience in disaster preparedness and resilient infrastructure, while reaffirming his country's support for Taiwan's participation in global climate efforts, MOFA said.
Tuvaluan Prime Minister Feleti Penitala Teo said climate change and climate action were not limited by political boundaries, and praised Taiwan's contributions to global climate efforts. He stressed that no willing partner should be left out of international cooperation.
St. Kitts and Nevis Deputy Prime Minister Geoffrey Hanley highlighted Taiwan's contributions in environmental governance, the circular economy, climate resilience, green energy and capacity building.
Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) thanked the five countries for their support, saying Taiwan would continue working with its allies and like-minded partners to address climate change.

Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。

（中央社華盛頓14日綜合外電報導）台裔民主黨籍政治人物潘君達在美國期中選舉勝出，將成為新科加州聯邦眾議員。他表示，美國數十年來的對台政策承認台灣自決權，維持台海現狀至關重要，而美國仍是現狀的保障者。
現年61歲的潘君達（Richard Pan）近日接受美國之音（VOA）訪問時指出：「我認為，我們目前對台海兩岸關係的政策－即我們承認台灣的自決權－是非常重要的，這已經持續數十年，相關原則一直都在指引這項政策。」
他說：「我們必須確保維持當前台海現狀，而美國仍是那個現狀的保障者。」
當被問及是否對當前台海情勢感到擔憂，潘君達回應：「當然。我的意思是，我們必須保持和平，對吧？我認為那的確非常重要。」
至於是否會加入「國會台灣連線」（Taiwan Caucus），他坦言先前不知道有這個組織，但他的答案是「會」。
潘君達的父母來自台灣，他是小兒科醫師，曾在加州大學戴維斯分校（UC Davis）任教，2010年當選加州州眾議員，又於2014年至2022年擔任加州州參議員。
在本次期中選舉中，潘君達以將近6成得票率擊敗現任共和黨籍聯邦眾議員基利（Kevin Kiley），將於明年1月3日就任聯邦眾議員。
在他競選辦公室發布的政見聲明中，對於台美關係，他強調兩項重點：美國的承諾與可信度、夥伴關係和自決。
關於前者，潘君達強調，支持亞洲的自由及民主，與美國國家利益一致。他提倡嚴格遵守「台灣關係法」（Taiwan Relations Act）及「六項保證」（Six Assurances），並警告美國政府，勿採取可能助長北京氣焰的交易性政策。
關於後者，潘君達將台灣定位為至關重要的印太地區民主夥伴，呼籲增加台美雙邊接觸、支持台灣參與國際事務，以及捍衛台灣對抗外部壓力的自決權。
潘君達2011年7月曾以加州州眾議員身分訪台，並與時任立法院長王金平會面，討論加強台灣與加州的貿易交流。（編輯：洪培英）1151114

台积电获得美日德中创纪录新台币1676亿元援助
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北 11 月 14 日电 台积电 (TSMC) 今年前 9 个月从美国、日本、德国和中国政府获得总计 1,675.86 亿新台币（51 亿美元）的补贴，以支持其在这四个市场的运营。
根据周五发布的财报，这家全球最大的代工芯片制造商第三季度从四国政府获得了 1669.96 亿元新台币的补贴，而上半年仅获得了 5.9 亿元新台币。
1月至9月期间的补贴总额创下历史新高，有助于覆盖台积电在全球扩张计划中与房产购买、工厂建设和生产设备相关的费用。
为了获得财政援助，台积电的子公司——美国亚利桑那州的台积电亚利桑那公司、德国德累斯顿的欧洲半导体制造公司（ESMC）、日本熊本的日本日月光半导体制造公司（JASM）和中国的台积电南京公司——已与其运营地区的地方政府签署了协议。
台积电目前在南京运营一座12英寸晶圆厂。
台积电在亚利桑那州的第一座晶圆厂采用先进的 4 纳米工艺，于 2024 年第四季度开始商业生产。
亚利桑那州第二座工厂的建设已经完成，设备安装正在进行中。该工厂计划于 2027 年第三季度开始采用更复杂的 3nm 工艺进行批量生产。
台积电在熊本的第一座晶圆厂已于 2024 年底开始商业化生产，第二座晶圆厂正在建设中，计划于 2028 年开始量产。
台积电德累斯顿工厂计划于明年开始量产。
9个月财报显示，台积电Arizona盈利新台币539.86亿元，JASM盈利新台币23.96亿元。与此同时，ESMC仍处于亏损状态，亏损新台币10.79亿元。
（张建中、黄芳芳摄）

Taipei, Nov. 14 (CNA) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) received a combined NT$167.586 billion (US$5.10 billion) in subsidies from the governments of the United States, Japan, Germany and China in the first nine months of this year to support its operations in the four markets.
According to a financial report released Friday, the world's largest contract chipmaker received NT$166.996 billion in subsidies from the four governments in the third quarter, after receiving only NT$590 million in the first half of the year.
The combined subsidies for the January-September period hit a record high, helping cover TSMC's expenses related to property purchases, plant construction and production equipment as part of the chipmaker's global expansion plan.
To receive the financial assistance, TSMC subsidiaries -- TSMC Arizona Corp. in the U.S. state of Arizona, European Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (ESMC) in Dresden, Germany, Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Inc. (JASM) in Kumamoto, Japan, and TSMC Nanjing Co. in China -- have signed agreements with local governments in the areas where they operate.
In Nanjing, TSMC currently operates a 12-inch wafer fab.
In Arizona, TSMC's first fab began commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2024 using the advanced 4 nanometer process.
Construction of a second fab in Arizona has been completed, with equipment installation underway. The facility is scheduled to begin mass production in the third quarter of 2027 using the more sophisticated 3nm process.
In Kumamoto, TSMC's first fab began commercial production at the end of 2024, while construction of a second fab is underway, with mass production scheduled to begin in 2028.
TSMC's Dresden fab is scheduled to begin mass production next year.
The nine-month financial statements show that TSMC Arizona posted a profit of NT$53.986 billion, while JASM generated a profit of NT$2.396 billion. ESMC, meanwhile, remained in the red, reporting a loss of NT$1.079 billion.
(By Chang Chien-chung and Frances Huang)

几天后，国务卿马可·卢比奥向参议院外交关系委员会表示，美国对台政策没有变化。但特朗普的言论仍然令人震惊——部分原因是它们反映出华盛顿的转变超出了椭圆形办公室的范畴。自2025年以来，两党政客一直回避确认美国长期以来对台湾的支持。与此同时，中国正在制定新的战略，以在不发动战争的情况下胁迫台湾，如果北京认为政客和公众对美国对台湾的承诺正在减弱，那么北京将越来越倾向于使用这些战略。

Just a few years ago, U.S. President Joe Biden caused a stir when he confirmed publicly that his administration would defend Taiwan if the island were attacked by China—a divergence from the traditional U.S. policy of strategic ambiguity, in which Washington does not commit to taking any particular action. In May, U.S. President Donald Trump made waves for taking a different position. In a television interview, he described Taiwan as “a very good negotiating chip” in dealings with Beijing and mused that the island was close to China but far from the United States, implying that U.S. interests in Taiwan were negligible. In doing so, Trump seemed to confirm something many Asia watchers had feared: that this U.S. president would be willing to loosen the United States’ commitment to Taiwan to bolster his relationship with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
A few days later, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that there had been no change in U.S. policy toward Taiwan. But Trump’s words were alarming nonetheless—in part because they reflect a shift in Washington that goes beyond the Oval Office. Since 2025, politicians from both parties have been shying away from affirming the United States’ long-standing support for Taiwan. Meanwhile, China is developing new strategies to coerce Taiwan without going to war, and Beijing will be increasingly tempted to use them if it judges that the U.S. commitment to Taiwan is waning among both politicians and the public.
Yet that would be a grave miscalculation on China’s part. In fact, the United States’ interests in Taiwan are growing, not diminishing. Whatever the nature of Washington’s rhetoric right now, the United States would have to respond to any action by Beijing that threatened those interests, and both countries would then face a great-power crisis. To defuse this dangerous situation, American leaders must update the United States’ Taiwan strategy to reflect a new reality—and they should begin immediately.
Taiwan’s unique international status has long made U.S. policy complex. The Republic of China, now known as Taiwan, was a World War II ally of the United States. When the People’s Republic of China was founded on the mainland, in 1949, the Republic of China’s president, Chiang Kai-shek, decamped to Taiwan, and the United States maintained formal diplomatic ties with Chiang’s government, not the People’s Republic of China. In 1954, as the Cold War crested in the Pacific, the United States concluded a formal mutual defense treaty with Taiwan, in part to forestall increasingly aggressive artillery barrages from the mainland. Nearly 20 years later, however, when U.S. President Richard Nixon and his national security adviser, Henry Kissinger, began to engineer a diplomatic opening to the government in Beijing, they knew it would cost Taiwan.
In part because they understood that building diplomatic ties with Beijing would be painful for Taiwan and cause controversy in Congress, where Taipei had many boosters, Nixon and Kissinger slow-walked the process. So did Nixon’s successor, President Gerald Ford. It finally fell to President Jimmy Carter to make the change. On January 1, 1979, the United States ended its alliance with Taiwan and recognized the mainland government as “the sole legal Government of China.” Congress was irate. Lawmakers from both parties quickly drafted the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act, which remains in force. The law requires Washington to provide Taipei with defensive arms, creating the trappings of an alliance with Taiwan despite the relationship’s unofficial status. In 1982, the Reagan administration made an additional set of commitments to Taiwan, known as the Six Assurances. These include an affirmation that Washington does not endorse Beijing’s sovereignty claims over Taiwan and a promise that the United States would not use arms sales to Taiwan as a bargaining chip.
In the 50 years since, U.S. Taiwan policy has been remarkably successful. Through its partnership and arms sales, the United States has helped underwrite peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait, and Taiwan has thrived as a democracy and an economy, even as Washington has maintained a relationship with Beijing. But U.S. commitments to Taiwan have lately come under increasing strain. China has proceeded with a massive military buildup designed to give Beijing the option to take Taiwan by force; used coercive economic tactics, launched cyberattacks, and interfered in elections to put pressure on Taipei; and run frequent army and coast guard exercises to demonstrate its ability to strangle the island. All of this has stoked concerns across the Pacific that the United States’ long-standing partnership might not be enough to keep the peace in the Taiwan Strait.
China is developing new strategies to coerce Taiwan without going to war.
The fear that China could attempt to retake Taiwan by force, possibly during Xi’s tenure, has grown in recent years. Analysts have frequently cited 2027 as the beginning of the window of maximum danger, based on a 2021 statement made by Philip Davidson, the former commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command, about when the People’s Liberation Army might be prepared for an invasion. But this timeline was never hard and fast, and Xi’s recent purge of more than 100 officers has likely delayed the military’s readiness. U.S. intelligence assessments do not anticipate an invasion of Taiwan next year, and most scholars believe the Chinese government would consider such a move as a last resort only if unification could not be accomplished by other means.
The primary danger now is that Xi will escalate a pressure campaign designed to coerce Taiwan into negotiating a change in its status. Since 2025, China’s leaders have used their diplomatic channels to the Trump administration, including Xi’s direct line to Trump, to insist on American concessions on Taiwan in exchange for progress in trade talks. In May, China secured a pause on a planned $14 billion U.S. arms sale and other defense funding for Taiwan. Beijing may hope that additional incremental moves will further weaken Taiwanese confidence in the United States and that such actions will be difficult for Trump or a future U.S. president to reverse.
China is also clearly planning for more dramatic forms of coercion. It has a few options: since 2022, China’s military has practiced blockades of Taiwan, and its coast guard has simulated a quarantine of the island’s major ports. Beijing could also use customs enforcement or other administrative measures to attempt to assert its jurisdiction over Taiwan while minimizing the likelihood that the United States would intervene to stop it. If Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, who favors Taiwanese independence but has not pursued it in office, is reelected in 2028 and Chinese leaders believe that the path to a peaceful unification is closing, Xi may consider using these tools against the island in late 2028 or early 2029, before a new U.S. administration takes office. Given Trump’s alienation of U.S. allies in Asia and Europe and Washington’s limited means to respond to a maritime quarantine, Beijing might hope to get away with such a large-scale coercion campaign without inviting serious pushback.
Taiwan’s growing strategic importance makes Beijing’s development of new coercive options more concerning. Washington is no longer maintaining a partnership with Taipei because of a historical commitment or, as Beijing would have the world believe, to needle China. The artificial intelligence boom has put Taiwan at the center of the global economy. Taiwan is a critical supplier for the U.S. tech industry, and the United States recognizes that it cannot be a leader in AI without Taiwan.
The scale of the United States’ economic dependence on Taiwan is revealing. Taiwan is the country’s fifth-largest trading partner; a Chinese blockade of the island would imperil more than $250 billion in trade and could shave more than three percent off U.S. GDP in a year, according to a Bloomberg report. As much as 97 percent of the global supply of the high-end logic chips used in smartphones and other advanced electronics are produced or packaged in Taiwan. Losing access to Taiwanese chips could reduce advanced electronics production globally by 60 percent, with factories forced to rely on their chip inventories. The United States’ auto and medical device industries could deplete their inventories in a matter of weeks. The U.S. firms Amazon, Apple, and Nvidia are among the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s ten largest customers, which together represent more than $14 trillion in market capitalization. With AI growth buoying the U.S. stock market and the broader economy, a crisis in Taiwan would trigger a crash—potentially one similar in scale to the stock market crash at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The economic effects of a Chinese effort to squeeze Taiwan would not be limited to the United States. The research firm Rhodium Group has conservatively estimated that a yearlong blockade of the island could cost the global economy between $2 trillion and $3 trillion. A full-scale war would be far worse; Bloomberg has estimated that it would cause $10 trillion in economic losses and a global recession. It is therefore increasingly likely that the United States would be forced to act if Taiwan’s supply chains were put in jeopardy. The cost of standing aside would simply be too high.
Yet just when the United States needs to be doing all it can to prevent a crisis, Washington’s support for Taiwan appears to be wobbling. Trump’s musings about Taiwan’s geographical distance from the United States and his use of arms sales as a bargaining chip are the headline examples, but they are not the only indicators of a shaky U.S. commitment. Policy analysts have argued that the United States should change its position to definitively oppose Taiwanese independence or even withdraw U.S. forces from the military bases in Japan and the Philippines that are closest to Taiwan.
Public opinion in the United States is shifting, too. Americans’ feelings toward China have warmed considerably over the past two years, according to a July 2026 Chicago Council on Global Affairs survey. A majority, 57 percent, support friendly cooperation and engagement with China, whereas 40 percent support an active effort to limit the growth of China’s power. The share of Americans who see China’s territorial ambitions as “a critical threat” has decreased by more than ten percentage points since 2022, and those who favor the use of U.S. troops if China invaded Taiwan has fallen from 52 percent to just 38 percent.
The United States cannot be a leader in AI without Taiwan.
In part, the declining support for defending Taiwan reflects Americans’ growing wariness of instability and conflict. A sense that the world was descending into chaos helped fuel Trump’s 2024 campaign; as president, Trump has heightened that sense by taking assertive military action in places such as Iran and Venezuela. Americans are now suffering the economic consequences of nine months of war in the Middle East, further deepening antiwar sentiment, as the midterm election results vividly demonstrate. Candidates for office used to clamor to sound tough on China, but many now blanch at the idea of suggesting that the U.S. military should defend Taiwan against a Chinese invasion, calculating that this is not the time to be seen as a hawk.
Of course, public attitudes can change quickly during a crisis. If China actually committed aggression against Taiwan, Americans could become more supportive of a strong U.S. response. And if the early stages of a conflict saw American casualties or a Chinese attack on U.S. critical infrastructure, the U.S. public could very well rally around the flag and demand a muscular intervention.
For now, however, China may believe that the United States’ will and ability to fight are both diminishing. The war with Iran has substantially reduced U.S. military readiness for a Taiwan contingency. The United States has used up much of its missile defense stock, including roughly two-thirds of its Patriot interceptor inventory, which was already depleted by U.S. aid to Ukraine, and as much as 80 percent of THAAD interceptors against Iranian drones and missiles. Even before the Iran war, analysts had warned that the U.S. military could run out of long-range, precision-guided munitions in a fight over Taiwan; now, the munitions shortfalls have become perilously acute. The war has also drawn military assets away from the Indo-Pacific. In August, Washington moved its last aircraft carrier in Asia, the USS George Washington, out of the region. It has also relocated missile defense systems to the Middle East, including Patriot and THAAD systems that had been deployed in South Korea.
The result is an increased risk of dangerous miscalculation. Should Chinese leaders assess that the United States’ commitment to Taiwan is wavering in both political parties and that the country is ill prepared for a fight, they might conclude that they have an opportunity to pressure Taiwan without inviting an American response. Yet because the United States has a greater interest in Taiwan today than at any point in history, Beijing’s bet could turn out to be wrong. China could announce a maritime quarantine of Taiwan or another coercive measure only to have the United States intervene, potentially prompting a great-power standoff.
Avoiding such a showdown will require American leaders to recommit to deterrence. First, Washington needs to update the way it communicates its positions. In their public remarks, policymakers should clearly state that the U.S. economy’s dependence on Taiwanese exports makes peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait a vital interest of the United States. American political leaders should emphasize to Beijing that the United States has an obligation to prevent a crisis that would tank the U.S. stock market, cut critical supply chains, and fell many American industries.
Clarifying U.S. interests would not impugn 50 years of careful diplomacy with China, nor would it require any change to U.S. policy as established by the Taiwan Relations Act, the Six Assurances, or the series of joint U.S.-Chinese statements, made between 1972 and 1982, known as the Three Communiqués. The updated statements, rather, would convey to Chinese leaders that certain changes to the cross-strait status quo would be unacceptable to the United States, even if Taiwan were to acquiesce to those changes under pressure. Washington would support a peaceful unification, for example, only if the process guaranteed the security of critical supply chains.
Once the United States makes its interests clear, it will also have to back up its statements with a new playbook to deter Chinese actions that fall below the military threshold. Beijing may already be in the early stages of imposing a quarantine on the island. Washington should not tolerate additional measures that interfere with commerce and maritime traffic in and out of Taiwan. To deter China from taking such steps, the next U.S. Congress should use legislation to clarify its wholesale, bipartisan opposition to Chinese blockades, quarantines, and other restrictions. Even if the White House continued to take a softer position, this would send a message to Beijing that other political actors might force the president’s hand. Congress should also press the administration to prepare punitive diplomatic and financial measures for use in the event of an escalating Chinese quarantine of Taiwan. By planning these reprisals well ahead of any coercive action, Washington would signal that a maritime pressure campaign would entail clear costs for Beijing and carry dangerous escalation risks.
Americans’ feelings toward China have warmed considerably.
The United States should strengthen military deterrence, too. The next Congress must pressure the Trump administration to release the stalled $14 billion package of arms sales to Taiwan, as well as other security assistance the administration is slow-rolling. Congress has a legal obligation to do so under the Taiwan Relations Act. Pausing security aid violates U.S. policy, and allowing the Trump team to make this concession in its likely quixotic pursuit of rapprochement with Xi only weakens Washington’s hand.
Washington does not have to—and shouldn’t—take these steps alone. U.S. allies such as Germany, Japan, and South Korea would suffer nearly as much as the United States if China were to take control of Taiwan’s semiconductor industry. These countries have an interest in working quietly together to deter and develop joint responses to Chinese coercion while also collaborating to diversify their chip supply chains and make them more resilient. In the United States, this work does not have to wait for a new presidential administration. Congress can send delegations and use other diplomatic opportunities to start developing plans with parliamentary counterparts abroad.
As the 2028 U.S. presidential election approaches, moreover, candidates from both parties should speak clearly about the country’s strong economic interests in Taiwan and about their commitment to deterrence. This does not require embracing bellicose positions, but presidential candidates do need to state firmly that any move by Beijing to choke off vital supply chains would harm U.S. interests and demand an American response. Consistent messaging would also signal to China’s leaders that they should not expect a future administration to be bound by Trump’s policy concessions—and signal to allies that come 2029, the United States will again be a reliable partner in standing up to China’s economic aggression.
The United States needs to update its Taiwan policy, but ceding ground as Trump has done only makes the cross-strait balance less stable. Unlike other Cold War–era policies, the importance of preventing Chinese aggression against Taiwan has become more—not less—vital with the passage of time. U.S. interests in Taiwan are plainer and easier to explain than they have ever been. Only by stating those interests clearly and backing up the words with actions can the United States continue to avert a crisis or conflict that would be devastating for all.

拥有卫星并不等于拥有替代卫星的专业知识
当下一颗卫星需要更换时，购买该卫星的国家是否会有更多选择，或者只是来自同一供应商的另一张发票？
对于投资卫星服务以监测农作物、海岸线和灾害的印度-太平洋地区各国政府来说，这是一个现实的实际问题。海外合作伙伴可以快速提供有用的技术。它是否也能让国内工程师更好地选择、适应和开发下一个系统，取决于硬件的配套。
阿曼与中国 STAR.VISION 签订的新协议（在新窗口中打开）提供了及时的检查。它们于 11 月 2 日签署（在新窗口中打开），将卫星计划与拟议的组装、集成和测试中心、联合太空人工智能实验室以及为期五年的教育和培训计划结合起来。其雄心是获得航天器和专业知识（在新窗口中打开）以建立国内产业。然而，实现这一雄心壮志的合作伙伴对于实现这一目标仍然是不可或缺的。
拟议的培训包括在中国提供 30 个研究生奖学金（在新窗口中打开）以及为 1,000 名专家提供能力建设课程。该工程中心将提供将组件组装到航天器中并在发射前进行检查的设施。其重要性将取决于阿曼团队是否学会制定和捍卫工程决策，而不是遵循其他地方制定的程序。
此次合作建立在现有关系的基础上。阿曼镜头成立于 2023 年（在新窗口中打开），是火星开发投资公司与 STAR.VISION 的合资企业。其 OL-1 地球观测卫星（在新窗口中打开）于 2024 年 11 月发射。因此，新协议扩大了具有运营经验的伙伴关系，而不是从头开始太空活动。
合作可以在不消除国际依赖的情况下建立自主权；有用的区别是留下学习空间的依赖和阻碍学习的依赖。
还有证据表明，参与超出了所有权范围，尽管它来自公司本身。在 11 月 4 日接受阿曼广播公司 Al Wisal 采访时（在新窗口中打开），Oman Lens 销售总监 Azzan Al Maamari 表示，阿曼人员参与了 OL-1 的设计以及接下来两颗卫星的设计和制造。他说，该运营中心完全由阿曼运营。这些说法未经独立核实，但它们确定了针对哪些责任

Owning a satellite isn’t the same as owning the expertise to replace it
Oman’s expanding satellite partnership with China offers a test for emerging space economies: can buying foreign technology give countries greater control over their next purchase?

|Owning a satellite isn’t the same as owning the expertise to replace it
Owning a satellite isn’t the same as owning the expertise to replace it
When the next satellite needs replacing, will the country that bought it have more options, or simply another invoice from the same supplier?
That is a live practical question for governments across the Indo-Pacific investing in satellite services to monitor crops, coastlines and disasters. An overseas partnership can deliver useful technology quickly. Whether it also leaves domestic engineers better equipped to choose, adapt and develop the next system depends on what accompanies the hardware.
Oman’s new agreements (Opens in new window) with China’s STAR.VISION offer a timely check. Signed on 2 November (Opens in new window), they combine a satellite program with a proposed assembly, integration and testing centre, a joint space artificial-intelligence laboratory and a five-year education and training program. The ambition is to acquire both spacecraft and the expertise (Opens in new window) to build a domestic industry. Yet the partner enabling that ambition could remain indispensable to fulfilling it.
The proposed training encompasses 30 postgraduate scholarships (Opens in new window) in China and capacity-building courses for 1,000 specialists. The engineering centre would provide facilities where components are assembled into spacecraft and checked before launch. Its significance will depend on whether Omani teams learn to make and defend engineering decisions rather than follow procedures devised elsewhere.
This cooperation builds on an existing relationship. Oman Lens was established in 2023 (Opens in new window) as a joint venture between Mars Development and Investment Company and STAR.VISION. Its OL-1 Earth-observation satellite (Opens in new window) launched in November 2024. The new agreements therefore extend a partnership with operational experience rather than initiating space activity from scratch.
Cooperation can build autonomy without eliminating international dependence; the useful distinction is between dependence that leaves room to learn and dependence that prevents it.
There is also evidence of participation beyond ownership, although it comes from the company itself. In a 4 November interview (Opens in new window) with Omani broadcaster Al Wisal, Oman Lens sales director Azzan Al Maamari said Omani personnel had participated in OL-1’s design and also in the design and manufacture of its next two satellites. He said the operations centre was entirely Omani-run. These claims are not independently verified, but they identify responsibilities against which future progress can be judged.
For emerging space economies across the Indo–Pacific, the attraction is clear. Developing every component domestically would be expensive and could postpone useful services for years. International cooperation allows countries to acquire services while developing their own expertise. The policy choice is which responsibilities to retain, which to acquire gradually and which to continue buying abroad. A government need never build its own satellite to benefit from stronger domestic expertise. It still needs people who can compare bids, question technical advice and decide when a different supplier offers a better solution. The test of capability is therefore partly commercial: does each mission make the country a more informed customer, with greater freedom to negotiate the next deal?
That progression is not automatic. Operating a satellite does not necessarily confer the ability to modify its software, diagnose unfamiliar failures or design a replacement. A local facility can provide valuable employment while leaving crucial decisions with an overseas supplier. Scholarships can produce highly qualified graduates without providing the projects, positions and technical access needed to use their skills at home.
Governments can make that progression explicit in their purchase decisions. Successive missions could assign domestic teams greater responsibility for integration, testing, fault diagnosis and design changes. Contracts could specify access to engineering documentation and software, alongside opportunities for local suppliers. Training totals would then sit beside evidence of what graduates can actually do and which decisions they are authorised to make.
These are commercial and institutional questions as much as technical ones. Facilities require sustained operating budgets, experienced staff and a pipeline of projects. Graduates need careers that reward specialised knowledge. Local companies need opportunities to supply equipment or services. A satellite program can help create that demand, but its industrial benefits depend on how purchasing, training and research are connected.
Omani accounts describe expansion (Opens in new window) beyond the first satellite phase as conditional on its results. That creates an opportunity to assess learning alongside technical performance and customer demand. The public announcements do not specify whether that assessment will include domestic learning. But the principle travels: governments commissioning successive spacecraft can use each purchase to secure greater domestic responsibility. Staging hardware purchases does not, by itself, stage capability development.
The senior partner’s role should be assessed on the same basis. STAR.VISION offers a route into spacecraft development and associated infrastructure. Whether that route increases Oman’s choices will depend on the partnership’s terms and implementation. Cooperation can build autonomy without eliminating international dependence; the useful distinction is between dependence that leaves room to learn and dependence that prevents it.
Funding, intellectual-property access and the division of engineering authority remain unclear. Oman’s announcement therefore presents a policy ambition whose implementation deserves scrutiny. For governments across the Indo-Pacific, the useful measure is what changes between one purchase and the next: can domestic teams specify more, solve more and choose among more partners? A satellite eventually needs replacing. The expertise acquired in building and operating it should make the next decision less dependent on its supplier.
Richard de Grijs (Opens in new window) is Professor of Physics and Astronomy at Macquarie University and former Executive Director of the International Space Science Institute–Beijing.

「NATO加盟条件にドンバス放棄」米がウクライナに可否質問 ゼレンスキー氏公表 - 産経ニュース
メンテナンスのため、会員のログイン機能を一時停止しております。メンテナンス終了までメールマガジンの配信も停止します。
ユーザーの皆様にはご迷惑をおかけいたしますが、何卒ご理解のほどよろしくお願いいたします。
ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアとの和平協議を仲介する米国から「ウクライナはNATOに加盟できれば（ロシアが割譲を求めている）東部ドンバス地域（ドネツク、ルハンスク両州）を放棄できるのか」との趣旨の質問を受けたと記者団に明らかにした。ロイター通信や複数のウクライナメディアが14日、伝えた。
ゼレンスキー氏は13日、質問は協議中になされたもので正式な提案ではないと説明。時期には言及しなかったが、10、11日に開かれた米露ウクライナ3カ国の高官協議の場だった可能性がある。
ゼレンスキー氏によると、米国からこうした趣旨の質問をされたのは初めて。ゼレンスキー氏は「NATO加盟と引き換えの領土放棄」などの条件を正式に提示された場合、ウクライナ国民に是非を問うとしつつ、「ウクライナは露占領地を露領土とは認めない」とも強調した。
ゼレンスキー氏は、ウクライナが仮にロシアによるドンバスの実効支配を容認したとしても、ドンバスの法的な割譲には応じないとする立場を改めて示した形だ。
ただ、プーチン露大統領はウクライナのNATO加盟を容認しないと繰り返し明言してきた。ロシアもウクライナのNATO加盟を条件としたドンバスの獲得という案には同意しない公算が大きい。（小野田雄一）

“抗美援朝”。哥哥说刚入朝时毛和中共当局仍迷信人海战术。（图片来源：网络图片） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
前言：本回忆录以本人曲折复杂的人生经历为轴线，力图通过我的人生经历反映我所经历的中国大陆社会各个时期的真实面貌，以还原被中共当局刻意扭曲了的历史真相，所以回忆录中对我周围的社会现实的记录和分析较多。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
─那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的赛程我已经跑尽了，当守的信仰我已经守住了。─
自从父亲到樃梨市见到哥哥后，哥哥便经常给父母和我们兄弟姊妹写信，和我们一家关系非常亲密。那时部队的士兵每月只有七、八块钱的津贴，哥哥虽然从小生活在比较优裕的环境里；又深得父母的钟爱，然而他在部队却十分节俭，很少花钱，节省下的津贴都寄回家，或寄给我们兄弟姊妹购买书籍或学习用品。
那时我很喜欢打篮球，但因个子矮，体力又不强在球场上很难抢到球，只有当别人投向篮筐的球偶尔正好弹到我站的位置，而附近又没有牛高马大的同学时，才能抢到一个球投篮；或只是别人互相争抢球时脱手正好我在旁边才能抢到一次球。当哥哥偶然从我写给他的信中得知这一情况之后，他立即来信告诉我，三个月后一定寄钱给我们买一个篮球，让我们用自己的篮球到人少的有篮球场的机关、单位痛痛快快地玩个够。三个月后哥哥真的寄了30元钱回来，并注明是给我们买篮球用的。于是我和二姐、弟弟一起到二姐一位同学家开的文体用品店买了一个牛皮制作的篮球、橡胶球胆、小打气筒、塞球胆打气嘴和紧牛筋用的凹型叉子和一个装篮球的网兜，一共花了20元钱剩下的10元钱都交给母亲了(我们兄弟姐妹从小都养成了不乱花钱的习惯，因为吃的用的玩的母亲都给我们准备好了，完全不需要我们自己花钱去买)。那时的篮球与现在不一样，真牛皮球壳的里面有一个橡胶球胆，先把球胆放到篮球壳里面再用气筒打足气，然后用牛筯将篮球壳口锁紧才可使用。
这样每到星期六下午或星期天我们就会和邻里的小朋友一起带着自己的篮球到市郊那些有篮球场的机关单位空着的篮球场上去打球，那时我和小朋友们那种高兴的心情是难以言表的。
哥哥入朝作战不久，由于一贯漠视人的生命和尊严的毛泽东和中共当局仍然迷信人海战术，以及“志愿军”与联合国军在军事装备、后勤保障能力、军队训练水平、各兵种协同作战指挥能力上的巨大差距，导致部队伤亡极其惨重，部队只得源源不断地从农村招来几乎没有什么文化知识的新兵，而且仅经过简短的训练便匆匆被派往前线充当炮灰，所以入朝作战不到半年哥哥便由卫生员变成新兵接着就变成老兵，上一线作战了(由此可见当时伤亡之惨重)，接着就当上了班长、副排长。
据哥哥后来告诉我：我们那时候由于联合国军利用空中优势对“志愿军”的交通运输线展开“绞杀战”，致使“志愿军”的军火、粮食、衣被、鞋袜及其他军用物资损失巨大，一线作战部队生存状态异常艰苦，很难吃上一顿热菜热饭，往往是饿了就抓一把炒面(炒熟的干面粉)，渴了就抓一把雪塞到嘴里，遇到有山泉溪水的地方就喝一口凉水。由于长期缺乏蔬菜、肉类食品导致士兵们普遍营养不良，许多士兵因此患病，也是造成部队减员的重要原因。长期缺乏蔬菜、肉食，还导致士兵们维生素缺乏，使夜盲症、脚气病等在部队中广泛流行，这严重影响了惯于夜战和善于奔走的“志愿军”作战能力的发挥(夜战可降低联合国军的空中和地面火力优势，善于奔走是因部队缺乏现代运输工具，行军作战、后勤供应几乎全靠步行)。后来引起上级重视给士兵们发放多种维生素丸以补充维生素的缺乏，又设法向前线供应了一些鱼、肉罐头、压缩饼干之类的物品情况才有所好转。
哥哥说刚入朝时毛和中共当局仍迷信人海战术，仍采用解放战争时代屡试不爽的大部队不顾伤亡代价的集团冲锋的战术，但遭到的却是拥有大量自动武器、机枪、大炮、坦克和拥有绝对空中优势的联合国军，尽管冲在前面的士兵一排排倒下，后面的士兵仍前扑后继地不断往前送死，“志愿军”人再多也多不过联合国军的枪炮子弹、飞机炸弹。以致入朝作战初期“志愿军”领导订出标准：一场战斗打下来如果敌我双方伤亡达到一比七(即敌方伤亡1人我方伤亡7人)这场战斗就算打赢了，打赢了尚且如此，那么，打输了时的伤亡比例达到什么程度岂不更令人毛骨悚然。
面对如此重大的伤亡，“志愿军”不得不改变以集团冲锋为主的人海战术，转而采用小股部队穿插突击，防守时也将人员分散防守，以减少集中人员于一处的传统防守方式，减少了过去敌方一颗炮弹打来我方倒下一大片的的惨状的发生。此外，用从极度贫困的中国大陆民众身上搜括来的金钱、物资从苏联换来的飞机、大炮、坦克、汽车源源不断地运到朝鲜前线，缩小了与联合国军在武器装备上的差距，才逐渐缩小了与联合国军的伤亡比例。
哥哥说：打过仗的人都对战争深恶痛绝(特别是士兵和低级军官)，面对一个个亲密战友的突然死亡；或变得缺胳膊少腿，变得面目全非……等惨不忍睹的状态，内心感到的悲痛和失落是无法用言语表达的，你想想：昨天，甚至是几小时前还和你说说笑笑、活蹦乱跳的伙伴，突然一下子就死去，而且还死得那么惨，有的脑袋炸开脑浆四溅，面部血肉模糊；有的胸开肚破，内脏外溢，附近的泥土都被鲜血浸透了，那是什么滋味？打的时候人都麻木了，一心只想如何保护自己，消灭对方。一仗打完后，神经松弛下来了，才感到失去战友的悲伤和内心对死亡和受伤的恐惧。
由于哥哥对战争的反感和恹恶，所以很不愿意和我们谈及战争的细节。只有一次例外，哥哥说：有一次他所在的营伤亡惨重，由于联合国军飞机、大炮对道路的封锁，许多重伤员无法及时运到后方医院救治，有八十名重伤员停留在前线附近的野战包扎所，包扎所只有两名医务人员照顾，忙不过来，急需人来帮忙照顾这些重伤员，那天哥哥发烧、咳嗽，营长见他生病，以前又在卫生队干过，就对他说你今天生病就不要在前面打了，到山后的野战包扎所去帮忙照顾那些重伤员，那两个医务人员实在忙不过来。他上午到野战包扎所帮忙，帮那两位医务人员护理那八十位重伤员，到当天下午3点左右，联合国军向野战包扎所打来两发黄色的烟幕弹，他们老兵都知道，这是对方为校正着弹点而打来的烟幕弹，这意味着一场地毯式炮轰马上就要到来(因野战包扎所常有伤员抬进抬出被对方的侦察机发现)，他和那两位医务人员连忙将还未抬进防炮洞的伤员往单人防炮洞里抬(大部分重伤员原来都已经安置在单人防炮洞内)，安置完八十位重伤员后，只剩下两个单人防炮洞了(这种单人防炮洞又称“猫耳洞”)，那位年纪较大的医务人员要哥哥和另一名医务人员躲进这两个防炮洞，他自己另找地方躲避炮火，哥哥说自已年轻腿脚灵活坚持要那两位医务人员躲进防炮洞，还未等他们两位同意，哥哥便把他们二人分别推进剩下的两个防炮洞，自己拔腿就往山下的小溪跑去，哥哥知道小溪边有一块巨石虽比不上防炮洞安全也可以躲避一下弹片的袭击，哥哥刚跑到小溪边的巨石下，对方的排炮轰击便开始了，他说：刚开始还能听到炮弹爆炸时发出的巨响，过不不久就只能看到山上(包扎所所在地)火光不断地闪、炸起的石头、泥土、树枝四处乱飞，耳朵已被震聋(暂时性的)，已经听不到炮弹爆炸的声音了，后来突然感到大地一下巨震，胸前一阵巨痛后，便失去了知觉。原来一颗炮弹落在他藏身的巨石上，炸裂的一块大石头落在他的背部，把他砸昏了过去，到晚上八、九点钟因气温降低，他才被冻醒过来，藉着月光一看地上吐了一滩鲜血，胸部一阵阵巨痛，当他爬回部队时，便被连夜送往后方的野战医院，当他问送他去野战医院的战友，那八十位重伤员和两位医务人员的情况时，战友告诉他，哪里还有什么伤员和医务人员，那天下午炮轰后连一具完整的尸体都找不到，整个包扎所地域全被对方的炮弹翻了个底朝天，只剩下一些尸体碎片。哥哥一听不禁潸然泪下，泣不成声，他得知这一噩耗时，感到是无比的悲痛和哀伤，一点也没有感觉到侥幸脱险的幸运。
他在后方医院治疗了一段时间伤愈后又重返前线了(他是胸部肋骨多处骨折和肺部损伤)。在治疗的那段时间，那八十二位重伤员和医务人员的容貌总是不时浮现在他的眼前，直到他重返前线后，紧张激烈的战斗生活使他很少有时间来回忆那惨烈的一幕，那八十二位亡灵的身影才逐渐变得渺茫，而在脑海中逐渐被新的惨烈战斗场面所取代。
那时的哥哥和当时许多青年学生一样是满怀着对共产党、对新中国的巨大希望；满怀着被共产党的宣传所激发出来的对“美国侵略者”的巨大仇恨；满怀着饱满的爱国热情和献身精神去参军、去抗美援朝保家卫国的。他们哪里知道那是一场由苏联的斯大林和中国的毛泽东幕后支持、怂恿北朝鲜的金日成主动发起的侵略南朝鲜的侵略战争。
这一真相直到“改革开放”后和前苏联解体后解密的许多内幕资料中才被曝光。哥哥在朝鲜作战从1951年春直到1953年7月朝鲜停战，停战后又在朝鲜驻守了一年，到1954年冬季为接收苏联占领归还中国的旅顺、大连才随部队离开朝鲜回国入驻旅顺、大连附近的普兰店。在那里哥哥目睹了苏军风纪的败坏的情况。许多苏军士兵酗酒，苏军士兵酒醉后殴打中国民众、买东西不给线、追逐调戏强奸中国妇女的事时有发生。有的守仓库的苏军士兵把仓库里的物资甚至把军官们的望远镜、莱卡照相机(苏联最好的照相机)偷出来到中国老百姓家里换酒喝。
有一次哥哥驻地附近村子一名醉酒苏军士兵无端殴打一村民，被闻讯赶来的村民们追打，不慎掉到井里，乡村干部好不容易才制止了村民们的继续追打，费尽口舌才动员了几位村民拿出绳索将这名肇事士兵从井里救出，送往苏军驻地，这名苏军士兵被苏军军官用皮带猛打了一顿，才平息了村民的怒气。
还有一次，哥哥和排里的一位东北藉的战友外出时，走到一僻静处，忽听得一位妇女大喊救命，他们抬头一看，只见一名苏军士兵正在追赶一位中国妇女，哥哥和那位战友不由怒火中烧，心想：“中国人民已经站起来了”，光天化日之下哪容得“老毛子”(东北人对俄国人的蔑称)再在中国的土地上奸滛虏抢，随即拔出枪，子弹顶上膛，打开保险，两把枪对着那个苏军土兵大喝一声：“站住！”那苏军士兵一看这阵式，便吓得立即跪下来举起手求饶，那位妇女一见两位解放军战士来了，如同见到救星，一面往他们身边跑，一面骂那个苏军士兵。哥哥的那位东北藉战友更是怒不可遏，硬要一枪嘣了那个苏军士兵(因这位战友以前在日本占领时期目赌过日本兵在东北奸滛虏抢的惨状)。鉴于上级有明确规定：遇到此类苏军违法乱纪的事，一律移交苏军当局处理(这岂不是意味着被国民政府收回的“治外法权”又被毛泽东和中共当局白白地送给了“苏联老大哥”(中共当局对苏联的尊称)？哥哥虽也无法容忍苏军士兵的劣行，但迫于上级的媚苏规定，只好强忍心中的怒火，放下枪并劝阻他的战友不要开枪，两人一起押送这名强奸未遂的“苏联老大哥”士兵到他所在的苏军驻地兵营交给苏联驻军的值日军官和翻译，值日军官当即命令该士兵脱去军装只剩一条短裤，值日军官随即解下自已的皮带对着这个苏军士兵一顿猛抽，打得他在地上乱滚乱叫。然后值日军官又叫来两名士兵把这名肇事士兵押到禁闭室关禁闭。哥哥对我们说：苏军士兵虽然素质很差，但军官一般素质都比较好，都是苏联各级军事院校的毕业生，很少在外面干出违法乱纪的事来。苏联军官的待遇很好，吃得也很好，吃的是白面包、饼干、牛奶、白兰地、伏特加，各种罐头，而苏军士兵的生活待遇都很差，吃饭时一班人围成一圈，一个大黑面包这个士兵啃两口又传给下一个土兵啃两口，菜就是黄瓜、红萝卜、白萝卜用刺刀剖开撒上一点盐。比中国士兵吃得还要差。苏军军官和士兵待遇和受教育程度上的巨大差别大概是造成苏军士兵军纪差的重要原因。

Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

summary: 香港长者享长者日免费出行及入场 |中国劳工公告 星期日, 15 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工英文新闻 香港长者可于长者日免费乘车及入场 在长者日，65岁或以上的香港居民可免费乘坐港铁、巴士及电车，而60岁或以上的香港居民则可免费参观康乐及文化事务署博物馆和游泳池。山顶缆车和海洋公园等景点也提供免费入场服务。今天是香港长者日，长者可在公共场所享受一系列折扣

在长者日，65岁或以上的香港居民可以免费乘坐港铁、巴士和电车，而60岁或以上的香港居民则可以免费进入康乐及文化事务署的博物馆和游泳池。山顶缆车和海洋公园等景点也提供免费入场服务。
今天是香港的长者日，长者可享受一系列公共交通、景点和休闲设施折扣。
65岁或以上的居民凭快乐卡、长者八达通或个人八达通可免费乘坐港铁、轻铁、九巴、城巴、龙运巴士及新大屿山巴士。老年人只要出示老年人卡或身份证，即可免费乘坐有轨电车。
天星小轮为长者及一名陪同人员提供免费通行服务，但须出示长者咭或身份证。山顶缆车、海洋公园、香港摩天轮和香港湿地公园等景点均免费为长者游客开放。
康乐及文化事务署博物馆及游泳池免费开放予60岁或以上持有欢乐咭、长者咭或身份证的旅客。香港科学馆及香港太空馆亦为长者及一名陪同人士提供免费入场服务。

Hong Kong seniors enjoy free travel and entry on Elderly Day | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 15 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong seniors enjoy free travel and entry on Elderly Day
On Elderly Day, Hong Kong residents aged 65 and above can ride MTR, buses and trams for free, while those aged 60 and above get free access to Leisure and Cultural Services Department museums and pools. Attractions including the Peak Tram and Ocean Park also offer free admission.
Today is Elderly Day in Hong Kong, and seniors are entitled to a range of discounts on public transport, attractions and leisure facilities.
Residents aged 65 or above can travel free of charge on the MTR, Light Rail, Kowloon Motor Bus, Citybus, Long Win Bus and New Lantao Bus when using a Joyful Card, Senior Octopus or Personalised Octopus. Tram rides are also free for seniors who present their Senior Card or identity card.
Star Ferry offers free passage to seniors and one accompanying person upon presentation of a Senior Card or identity card. Attractions including the Peak Tram, Ocean Park, Hong Kong Observation Wheel and Hong Kong Wetland Park provide free entry for elderly visitors.
Leisure and Cultural Services Department museums and swimming pools are open free of charge to visitors aged 60 or above who hold a Joyful Card, Senior Card or identity card. The Hong Kong Science Museum and Hong Kong Space Museum also offer free admission for seniors and one accompanying person.

summary: 香港在离岸人民币市场的作用迅速增强 - 东盟+3宏观经济研究室 - AMRO ASIA 本文首次于2026年11月3日发表于《中国日报》。人民币不断扩大的国际影响力正在开启中国与全球市场金融一体化的新篇章。其下一阶段的发展将不仅仅取决于跨境贸易中使用的增加。它还需要更深层次、更具流动性和国际联系的金融市场。中国人民银行在 10 月份发布的政策声明中重申了市场驱动的承诺
content:
香港在离岸人民币市场的地位迅速提升 - 东盟+3宏观经济研究办公室 - AMRO ASIA
本文首发于2026年11月3日《中国日报》。
人民币日益增长的国际影响力正在开启中国金融与全球市场一体化的新篇章。其下一阶段的发展将不仅仅取决于跨境贸易中使用的增加。它还需要更深层次、更具流动性和国际联系的金融市场。
在十月份发布的政策声明中，中国人民银行重申了对市场驱动的汇率和更大的双向货币灵活性的承诺。一个数字引人注目：据报道，大约 80% 的人民币外汇交易是在离岸进行的。
美元的主导地位不仅取决于其在贸易中的广泛使用，还取决于深厚的市场和丰富的流动资产。人民币不需要取代美元来发挥更重要的国际作用，但它确实需要更强大的金融生态系统。
作为世界领先的离岸人民币业务中心，中国香港完全有能力帮助建立这一生态系统。
自2009年推出跨境贸易人民币结算以来，人民币存款、贷款、债券和外汇交易市场大幅拓展。
最近的势头令人鼓舞。截至2025年底，人民币存款和存款证达到1.10万亿元人民币（1650亿美元），接近2014年1.16万亿元人民币的峰值。人民币贷款和点心债券发行也强劲扩张，到2025年分别达到9300亿元人民币和1.10万亿元人民币。
然而，人民币的大部分离岸流通仍然与涉及中国内地实体的交易挂钩，资金经常通过贸易和投资渠道回流境内。这种门户模式对香港来说效果很好。国际化的下一阶段可能涉及更多非内地同行之间的交易。
基础正在显现。 2020年以来，香港转口至内地的份额已超过原产地份额，扭转了历史格局。随着东盟+3供应链一体化的深入，这种转变可能会产生对人民币结算、融资和对冲服务的更大需求。
将这种势头转化为持久的国际需求需要在三个方面取得进展。
首先是流动性。可靠的国际融资货币需要随时获得流动性。这与人民币尤其相关，因为内地部分开放的资本账户可能会限制在岸和离岸市场之间的流动。
7月，香港金管局将人民币业务融资规模扩大至5000亿元人民币，并将融资期限延长至最长三年。除了改进离岸和跨境债券回购安排外，这些措施还加强了融资渠道。
成熟的离岸市场还需要活跃的银行间拆借、更深层次的回购市场和可靠的国际流动性渠道。香港可以成为连接内地资金来源与亚洲及其他地区金融机构的枢纽。
第二个挑战是给予投资者持有人民币的强烈动力。
贸易结算可以将货币转移到海外，但有吸引力的金融资产有助于将货币保留在海外。离岸人民币投资机会依然相对狭窄，二级市场流动性有限，市场关注度高

Hong Kong's Role in Offshore RMB Markets Grows Apace - ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office - AMRO ASIA
This article was first published in China Daily on November 3, 2026.
The renminbi’s growing international reach is opening a new chapter in China’s financial integration with the global market. Its next stage of development will depend on more than just increasing use in cross-border trade. It will also require deeper, more liquid and internationally connected financial markets.
In a policy statement released in October, the People’s Bank of China reaffirmed its commitment to a market-driven exchange rate and greater two-way currency flexibility. One figure stood out: Around 80 percent of RMB foreign exchange trading was reported to take place offshore.
The US dollar’s dominance rests not simply on its widespread use in trade, but also on deep markets and abundant liquid assets. The RMB does not need to displace the dollar to play a more significant international role, but it does need a stronger financial ecosystem.
As the world’s leading offshore RMB business center, Hong Kong, China is well positioned to help build that ecosystem.
Since the introduction of cross-border RMB trade settlement in 2009, the city has substantially expanded its markets for RMB deposits, lending, bonds and foreign exchange transactions.
Recent momentum has been encouraging. As at end-2025, RMB deposits and certificates of deposit reached 1.10 trillion yuan ($165 billion), approaching their previous peak of 1.16 trillion yuan in 2014. RMB lending and dim-sum bond issuance have also expanded strongly, reaching 930 billion and 1.10 trillion yuan respectively in 2025.
Yet much of the RMB’s offshore circulation remains tied to transactions involving Chinese mainland entities, with funds frequently returning onshore through trade and investment channels. This gateway model has served Hong Kong well. The next stage of internationalization could involve more transactions among non-mainland counterparts.
The foundations are emerging. Since 2020, the share of Hong Kong’s re-exports destined for the mainland has exceeded the share originating there, reversing the historical pattern. Alongside deeper ASEAN+3 supply-chain integration, this shift could generate greater demand for RMB settlement, financing and hedging services.
Turning that momentum into lasting international demand requires progress on three fronts.
The first is liquidity. A reliable international funding currency requires ready access to liquidity. This is particularly relevant to the RMB because the mainland’s partially open capital account can constrain flows between onshore and offshore markets.
In July, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its RMB business facility to 500 billion yuan and extended funding tenors to up to three years. Alongside improvements to offshore and cross-boundary bond repurchase arrangements, these measures have strengthened access to funding.
A mature offshore market also needs active interbank lending, deeper repo markets and reliable international liquidity channels. Hong Kong could become a hub connecting mainland funding sources with financial institutions across Asia and beyond.
The second challenge is giving investors a strong incentive to hold RMB.
Trade settlement can bring a currency offshore, but attractive financial assets help keep it there. Offshore RMB investment opportunities remain relatively narrow, with limited secondary-market liquidity and a concentration of Chinese mainland-related assets.
Hong Kong could encourage greater issuance of renminbi-denominated bonds by foreign sovereigns, multilateral institutions and international companies. Renminbi-denominated funds tracking global equity benchmarks or markets in Japan, South Korea and ASEAN could also broaden investment opportunities.
Such products could attract international investors while allowing mainland investors to diversify overseas through established channels. They could also expand the RMB’s use in financing activities and acquiring assets beyond the mainland.
The third challenge is building networks that allow RMB to circulate globally.
International currencies benefit from network effects: The more widely a currency is used, the more attractive it becomes. Hong Kong already has important building blocks, including Bond Connect, Swap Connect and established payment and settlement infrastructure.
Further integration of the Cross-border Interbank Payment System and Hong Kong’s Central Moneymarkets Unit with international financial infrastructure could expand the reach of offshore RMB transactions. Regional arrangements for direct exchange and settlement between RMB and other Asian currencies could broaden payment options and improve efficiency.
Digital innovation, including tokenized financial assets, offers further opportunities to improve cross-border settlement. But technology is merely an enabler: Faster payments need sufficient assets, reliable funding and willing counterparties.
Deeper offshore markets would also require attention to liquidity risks, market segmentation and cross-border financial stability, supported by appropriate safeguards and cooperation among relevant authorities. Ultimately, the RMB’s international future will depend on China’s approach to financial opening, exchange rate flexibility and cross-border capital flows. A more market-driven exchange rate and deeper hedging markets can help accommodate more diverse flows. Stronger offshore liquidity arrangements can support market development consistent with domestic financial stability and the authorities’ approach to financial opening.
Hong Kong’s opportunity lies in developing markets and infrastructure that allow the RMB to be held, invested and used more widely across the region and beyond.

（中央社記者楊淑閔台北15日電）民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋今天指對手陣營在市民大道縫合議題上，應是想用資訊落差，跟人民說可能是空想；台北市長蔣萬安則說，團隊提出挑戰都是拿出具體質疑，包括有沒有考慮到空間大小、噪音問題、車流量等。
九合一選舉倒數，國民黨籍台北市長蔣萬安尋求連任，昨天舉辦「安心大遊行」，今天一早則出席第12屆電器盃節能公益路跑，隨後到士林市場掃街拜票。
蔣萬安接受媒體聯訪時，被問及昨天大遊行是否已打破沉默螺旋。蔣萬安說，非常感動昨天這麼多人走上街頭，因為風雨很大，呼籲支持者28日投票日堅定支持他。至於先前表示要參加民眾黨21日造勢活動，他說，相關邀約確定後，會跟大家報告。
針對作詞人林夕在社群平台Threads發文質疑政見抄襲沈伯洋，並評論市府執行力不足。蔣萬安則回應說，他不確定林夕指的是哪個部分抄襲，任何評論還是要有具體陳述問題，才能具體回應。
媒體追問，主持人蔡康永昨晚也在Threads上發表與「陪伴、彌補、在乎、珍惜」有關的貼文。蔣萬安說，尊重各方的評論跟發言，「我想我也沒有特別的解讀」。
媒體也問及縫合市民大道議題，指沈伯洋認為蔣萬安陣營想用資訊落差，跟人民說這些都是在空想。蔣萬安說，沈伯洋很喜歡用「資訊落差」4個字，但團隊對沈伯洋的政見提出挑戰，都是拿出確切數字或具體質疑，好比市民大道橋下到底能不能做廊帶或藝文展演空間，有沒有考慮到空間大小、噪音問題、車流量等等。
蔣萬安說，真正的資訊落差是根本不知道事實就提出批評，甚至是用猜的。所以連自己跟自己都有資訊落差，這才是更嚴重的。
此外，媒體關注基泰大直案仍無進度。蔣萬安說，有發現此案的都更速度緩慢，除再次積極協助住戶的安置及協商，也再次開放參與公辦都更，得到住戶正面回應。松機遷建細節部分，他說，都很清楚的跟大家做了報告。
媒體也問到，新台灣國策智庫民調顯示，沈伯洋的支持度領先蔣萬安4.1個百分點、看好度也領先。蔣萬安說，團隊對於民調都會參考，最後階段全力以赴。（編輯：蕭博文）1151115

content:
USNI 新闻图 这些是根据海军和公开数据，截至 2026 年 11 月 9 日，美国海军在世界各地部署的航母打击群和两栖战备群的大致位置。如果 CSG 或 ARG 正在进行分类操作，图表会反映主力舰的位置。 2026 年 10 月 11 日，在日本，航空水手长的大副飞行员 Tykwon Young（右）和航空水手长的大副飞行员 Saabirah Parker 在停泊在佐世保湾的美国级两栖攻击舰的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 的飞行甲板上涂上小白眼。美国海军照片 USS 的黎波里号 (LHA-7) 停泊在日本佐世保港口。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在日本海，第 13 海军陆战队远征队第 2/4 营登陆队的一名海军陆战队员在黄蜂级两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 上进行静态快速绳索训练。美国海军陆战队照片 据舰艇观察员称，美国海军陆战队照片两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 于周六从日本横须贺出发。马金岛两栖准备大队包括马金岛、安克雷奇号航空母舰 (LPD-23)、约翰·P·穆萨号航空母舰 (LPD-26) 和已上船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队，目前正在日本海执行任务。 2026 年 10 月 22 日，来自新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基的加勒比海船体维护技术员二等迈克尔·布卢瓦斯三世 (Michael Bloise III) 在加勒比海航行的自由级濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 上进行焊接操作。
美国海军照片 濒海战斗舰明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号 (LCS-21) 正在加勒比海中部作业。自由级濒海战斗舰驻扎在佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。在地中海，三级内政通信电工 Micah Lee 在与刘易斯和克拉克级干货船 USNS Medgar Evers (T-AKE-13) 一起在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰 USS 上进行海上补给之前检查通信设备巴尔克利号（DDG-84）在地中海，2026 年 10 月 22 日。美国海军照片 在地中海执行任务的独立部署的导弹驱逐舰包括：奥斯卡·奥斯汀号航空母舰（DDG-79），母港为罗塔海军基地。 USS Bulkeley (DDG-84)，母港为罗塔海军基地。美国海军保罗·伊格纳修斯号 (DDG-117)，母港为罗塔海军基地。斯托特号 (DDG-55) 母港位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 10 月 6 日，美国海军水手在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号 (DDG-79) 上的驾驶室里站岗，当时该舰正通过苏伊士运河。美国海军照片 有两艘导弹驱逐舰在红海执行任务： USS Jason Dunham (DDG-109)，母港为佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。美国海军冈萨雷斯号 (DDG-66)，母港为弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。2026 年 11 月 7 日，在阿拉伯海，乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 与刘易斯和克拉克级干货和弹药舰沃利·施艾拉号 (T-AKE-8) 一起进行海上补给。
美国海军照片 乔治华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 以及第 5 号舰载航空联队 (CVW) 和舒普号航空母舰 (DDG-86) 正在阿拉伯海执行任务，以支持美国在中东的行动。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，隶属于第 147 攻击战斗机中队 (VFA) 的第 5 航母战斗群的一架 F-35C 闪电 II 准备从尼米兹级航空母舰乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰 (CVN-73) 的飞行甲板起飞。美国海军照片航空母舰乔治·华盛顿号 (CVN-73)，母港为日本横须贺。航母航空联队 5 “皇家狼牙棒”

title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
zh_title: 台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米
summary: 台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯玛哈桑和他年迈的父母一直致力于复兴几乎被遗忘的地方。
content:
台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯马哈桑和他年迈的父母一直在台东县布克拉武村的布农社区努力恢复几乎被遗忘的农作物。 “我们只是希望带回许多传统的布农族作物，并再次在这片土地上种植它们，”48岁的伊斯马哈桑在晴朗的蓝天下的油小米田里告诉法新社。油小米，即布农语中的“莳萝”，是台湾特有的植物，可以在山上野生生长。伊斯玛哈桑首先在网上了解到这种植物，然后开始自己的研究，梳理历史文献并与部落长者交谈，其中包括一位记得上次吃这种植物是在半个世纪前的妇女。他发现，布农族农民过去常常在种植主要作物谷子的同时种植油小米，作为收成歉收或发生灾害时的“后备”。经过多年亲自种植油小米，伊斯玛哈桑开始明白为什么他的祖先依赖这种作物。
一粒油小米种子可以长出 15 至 20 个圆锥花序或分枝种子簇，并且茎可以自行再生，而谷子通常每粒种子长出一个圆锥花序，必须在切割后重新播种。事实证明，当极端天气或疾病爆发破坏了他 2.2 公顷（5.4 英亩）的农场时，它比谷子更坚强。伊斯马哈桑说，几年前一场持续了 200 多天的干旱期间，油小米“保持鲜绿色”，而其他作物却枯萎了。台风、洪水，甚至锈病爆发也没有影响到它。台湾中央研究院退休教授、植物遗传学专家邢月娥15年前在一个国际论坛上第一次听说了油小米。幸不知道的是，1890 年代采集的台湾油粟标本就存放在英国皇家植物园 (Kew)。兴带领一个研究小组在台湾东南部的山区找到了油小米，并开始研究这种鲜为人知的谷物。她发现，种子的保护性蜡涂层使其无需灌溉、化肥或杀虫剂即可生长，即使在质量较差的土地上也是如此。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民 Linkav Ismahasan 在台东的一块田里收割油小米。照片：I-Hwa Cheng / 法新社 油小米富含油、蛋白质和矿物质，可用于人类和动物消费，也可用作燃料。 “它在利用阳光和水方面自然非常有效，”辛说。
“至于土壤条件，即使是在地面布满大石头的山区，它也能生长得很好。” “非常珍贵”伊斯玛哈桑从一粒油小米开始了他的种植。现在，这个家庭每年在他们种植其他传统布农谷类作物的土地上每年收获两次油小米。油小米个头小，无味，可以用来做粥、馒头、面包，甚至爆米花。但该家族一直在努力说服其他农民种植这种植物，因为它在商业上尚不可行。油粟不仅是劳动密集型产业，而且意义重大

【原文 English Original】
Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan , harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather. Taiwan farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county. “We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, told AFP in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky. Oil millet, or “dill” in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains. Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago. He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit. After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop. A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut. It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare (5.4-acre) farm. During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said. Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either. Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum. Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal. She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilisers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land. Taiwan farmer Linkav Ismahasan harvests oil millet in a field in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel. “It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing. “As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.” ‘Very precious’ Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops. Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn. But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable. Oil millet is not only labour intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple. While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop. Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the centre, told AFP. Seeds are kept in aluminium foil packets and stored at -18C under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said. “In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognised and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.” Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders”. “If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.
